- Use the official `hf auth login` flow for explicitly gated models. Keep tokens in secret storage; never commit them to the repository or evidence logs.
- Weights and inference caches belong outside version control; retain hashes, provenance and artifact pointers.
- Reject suspicious executable model code, unexpected deserializers, symlinks or undocumented remote downloads until an independent security review.

## 3. Which model types HEY needs and how each should work

The 75-row role matrix enumerates the full logical fleet. This table groups those roles into implementation families with their canonical base architecture and training trigger.

| Family | Representative HEY roles | Initial realization | Fine-tuning/retraining threshold | Ground-truth verification |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| General Brain/reasoner | Conversation, planner, orchestrator, analyst, creative ideation, coach | Licensed Qwen3 general or hosted model + structured tools | Repeated failures on measured HEY missions that retrieval/tools cannot solve | Task completion, calibrated uncertainty, evidence/source grounding |
| Code developer | Architect, coder, code editor, debugger, test writer, security reviewer, SQL/API/DevOps | Code-specialist model + repository index, AST and compiler/test tools | Exact patch rate on untouched repositories improves under blinded benchmarks | Minimal diff, compile, tests actually executed, no unauthorized side effects |
| Text and document editor | Writing editor, proofreader, translator, summarizer, legal/academic style | General model + grammar/format/semantic-diff validators | Human-edited before/after corpus shows better scope fidelity after adaptation | Meaning preservation, changed regions, citations, format/RTL |
| Learning and teachers | Tutor, curriculum planner, worksheet/quiz generator, grading assistant | General model + approved curriculum retrieval + deterministic export | Consented, educationally reviewed examples improve learning quality beyond baseline | Correct answer key, rubric, grade/subject fit, no pupil-data leakage |
| Business/product | Strategy, finance, operations, market research, missing-requirement hunter | General model + calculator, evidence board, spreadsheet and decision graph | Specific style/workflow improvements validated on business cases | Actual numeric correctness, risk coverage, cited assumptions, source lineage |
| Retrieval + memory | Embedding, reranker, entity/decision extraction, temporal contradiction resolution | Multilingual embedding + lexical search + structured graph | Relevant-query recall unsatisfactory on representative multilingual eval | Recall@k, MRR/nDCG, privacy boundary, deletion, freshness |
| Vision/document | VLM, screen understanding, OCR, object detector, mask segmentation | OCR-specific model and licensed VLM; SAM for masks | Fine-tune narrow screenshots/handwritten content after data permissions | Bounding box overlap, document fields, table/formula parse, no false clicks |
| Image/design | Prompt designer, image generator, inpaint/restore/upscale, UI designer | Licensed image diffusion/flow API + masks, renderers, style data | Approved brand consistency dataset justifies LoRA or trained edit adapter | Mask/outside-mask preservation, identity consistency, usability and cost |
| Video/motion | Storyboard, shot scheduler, video generator, motion/title/caption editor | Structured scenes + externally priced video renderer + codecs | Licensing and budget-backed shot consistency improvement | Actual playable artifact, precise shot-locks, correct duration/export |
| Speech | VAD, wake word, ASR, voice activity, TTS, diarization | Device-efficient detector/ASR + separate expressive TTS | Noise/accent/code-switching tests expose improvement possible with data rights | WER/CER, latency, barge-in, pause, consent, language coverage |
| Native/gestures | Hand landmark detector, custom gesture recognizer, command classifier | Local MediaPipe-type landmarks + tiny temporal classifier/state machine | New custom gesture dataset outperforms thresholds reliably | False triggers per hour, FPS/latency on board, pause/stop, accidental actions |
| Safety/control | Risk detection, prompt injection evaluator, hallucination and permission critic | Deterministic policy/mandate checks plus measured detection models | Detector gap warrants training, not authorization changes | False allow rate, false deny, cross-user isolation, external proof |
| Fusion arbitration | Expert selector, model quality predictor, council synthesis, independent verifier | Deterministic/learned router + available specialist backends | Calibrated outcome labels yield demonstrated lower cost for same quality | Routing regret, cost, latency, independent task-success |

**Explicit sample specialist division:**
- **Coder:** produces new working modules or applications with repo inspection, test harnesses and dependency validation.
- **Editor:** makes minimal specified changes to existing text, documents, images, video or code; supports locks, before/after diff and rollback. Different asset types have different engines.
- **Generator:** creates an image/audio/video/document/presentation artifact with the modality-appropriate foundation and structured editors, not one universal “generator weight.”
- **Tester:** designs hard tests, but a real isolated runner is the authority on whether they passed.
- **Verifier:** independently checks postconditions and provenance; cannot rely solely on the implementer's statement.
- **Researcher:** retrieves current sources and gives traceable support rather than pretending weights store today's facts.
- **Teacher:** uses actual grade/subject/curriculum context, generates and edits lessons, quizzes, rubrics, presentations and exports.
- **Translator:** deliberately handles Sorani Kurdish (script and dialect), Kurmanji, Arabic and English, with native evaluation; never equate general multilingual marketing with real dialect proficiency.
- **Visual designer:** operates HEY brand and structured layout tokens; precise edits preserve approved regions and assets.
- **Native operator:** reads devices and executes actions through an authorized permissioned Edge adapter; no LLM has raw privileged access.

## 4. Repeatable training process — execution contract for each learned specialist

### Phase A — benchmark first

Define exact I/O JSON schema (including user intent, task type, attachments, sensitive-data scope, permitted tools, expected output contract). Select zero-shot baseline, scaffolded baseline, and candidate alternative. Prepare 100+ independent representative evaluation examples **as a recommended minimum for an initial exploratory suite, not a universal statistical guarantee**. Record dialect, device and risk coverage. Blind-test on different projects/users from training. Performance baseline must distinguish model answer quality from actual downstream action success.

### Phase B — data collection and creation

Data must have a permitted source: properly licensed public corpora; S&A-created examples; properly consented approved human edits; synthetic examples only when checked against independent real cases. Exclude school children's identifiable information, secrets, unpublished correspondence, and private records from weights unless separately legally authorized (prefer NEVER for mutable/private user facts). Preserve annotation instructions, split lineage, contamination audit, data subject rights and deletion process.

A supervised tool call is a **plan**, not evidence of execution. Use explicit `tool_proposal` and separately recorded real `tool_result` with provenance; do not train fabricated success messages. Tool results may contain untrusted text, so training examples must identify instruction versus retrieved data.

### Phase C — dataset structure

Example of a fictional (non-sensitive) code editor example:

```json
{"id":"hey-codeedit-demo-001","task_family":"code_editor","input":{"user_instruction":"Change only the label of the Save button to Save Project","repository_snapshot":"sha256:EXAMPLE_ONLY","locked_files":["src/payments.ts"]},"ideal_output":{"type":"unapplied_patch","changed_paths":["src/components/SaveButton.tsx"],"must_preserve_other_files":true},"labels":{"requires_approval":false,"security_scope":"workspace_edit_only"},"rights":{"source":"synthetic_SA_example","commercial_use_approved":true},"split":"train"}
```

Separate `chat_messages` training formulation from downstream app execution. Create task-family loaders that validate JSON schema and train/test isolation. Report rare and hazardous labels, not just aggregate accuracy.

### Phase D — adaptation selection

- **Prompt/format conditioning first:** for common style, task routing and bounded text editing; no expensive GPU training if enough.
- **RAG and tool use:** for current facts, user memory, school lesson material and exact workspace data; weights are the wrong database.
- **LoRA:** train task-specific low-rank layers when evidence shows a repeated skill gap. Recommended exploratory ranks 8–32; actual settings depend on architecture, compute, tokenizer and evaluation.
- **QLoRA:** train adapters over appropriately quantized compatible foundation weights to reduce accelerator memory demand; compatibility with selected MoE/attention architecture must be checked.
- **Distillation:** train smaller narrow models against legally and contractually permitted qualified demonstrations, using independent human/source verification and ensuring teacher/student private data is not leaked.
- **Full fine-tuning:** only for funded hardware/data and when PEFT demonstrably inadequate.
- **From-scratch pretraining:** not part of the $25–50 infrastructure plan; requires separate data, compute, safety and finance program.
- **Vision/media adapters:** use model-specific pipelines and compatible license; image LoRA does not transform into a video or TTS adapter.

### Phase E — practical reference SFT adapter sketch

This is an **illustrative implementation pattern, not an executed training run**; engineers must validate tokenizer, context, `target_modules`, GPU VRAM and current API for their actual pinned foundation.

```python
# requirements: a compatible CUDA training environment, licensed dataset, pinned package versions
# pip install transformers datasets accelerate peft trl bitsandbytes
from datasets import load_dataset
from peft import LoraConfig, TaskType
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
from trl import SFTConfig, SFTTrainer

BASE = "Qwen/Qwen3-8B"  # replace with a verified pinned model revision
REVISION = "REPLACE_WITH_VERIFIED_PUBLISHER_COMMIT"
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(BASE, revision=REVISION, torch_dtype="auto")
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(BASE, revision=REVISION)
# Train file is a consented, deduplicated, prevalidated JSONL dataset of chat-formatted examples.
dataset = load_dataset("json", data_files="data/approved_train.jsonl", split="train")
peft = LoraConfig(task_type=TaskType.CAUSAL_LM, r=16, lora_alpha=32,
                  lora_dropout=0.05, target_modules="all-linear")
config = SFTConfig(output_dir="artifacts/hey_role_adapter",
                   max_length=2048, per_device_train_batch_size=1,
                   gradient_accumulation_steps=8, learning_rate=1e-4,
                   num_train_epochs=1, logging_steps=10, save_strategy="steps",
                   save_steps=100)
trainer = SFTTrainer(model=model, args=config, train_dataset=dataset,
                     processing_class=tokenizer, peft_config=peft)
trainer.train()
trainer.save_model("artifacts/hey_role_adapter")
```

The code must **not** be run as written until `REVISION`, hardware, `target_modules`, dataset format, training privacy, pinned dependencies, and training budget are reviewed. Train/dev/test separation and comparison against the original foundation are mandatory for promotion. No model should learn to execute malicious or unauthorized operations.

### Phase F — evaluation and acceptance

Run one consistent frozen evaluation bundle per task family:
1. Task correctness, real tool use and edit fidelity.
2. Faithful uncertain and negative responses instead of unsupported confident statements.
3. Multilingual English/Sorani/Arabic and appropriate code-switching.
4. Permission denial and prompt-injection challenge cases.
5. Long-context retention, contradictory history and supersession.
6. Latency p50/p95, throughput, cold start, resource draw and quality/cost ratio.
7. Reliability under 429, 500, retries, task cancel, network drop, context overflow, DB unavailability.
8. Out-of-domain and novel cases; report regressions per cohort, not only average.
9. Licensing and provenance integrity; ensure only permitted datasets used.
10. Independent evaluator reproducibility on unshared holdout cases.

Gate condition: observed task-level improvement that matters to HEY, with no material policy regression and with service unit economics staying inside spending controls. Neither a benchmark leaderboard score nor a polished answer proves mission success.

### Phase G — deployment, rollout and governance

`CANDIDATE → LICENSE_REVIEWED → BENCHMARKED → SHADOW → CANARY → APPROVED → ACTIVE → RETIRED/REVOKED`.

For each revision, record source repo+SHA, model weights hash, tokenizer/template, adapter hash, dataset/rights manifest, signed eval report, hardware/runtime, quality distribution, p95 latency, cost/use, safety/permission tests, fallback endpoint, incident contact, rollback instruction and explicit authorized approver. Version endpoints; never change an active model alias without canary + rollback.

#### Serving choice

- `vLLM` / `SGLang` / applicable high-throughput inference server for a funded CUDA GPU/managed dedicated environment; evaluate tool calling, streaming, MoE and batching compatibility.
- `llama.cpp` and `Ollama` for user opted-in local quantized model experiments where device resources are sufficient; they cannot silently monopolize RAM or force downloads.
- Usage-priced third-party inference when modest workloads make dedicated GPU uneconomic, subject to provider privacy/retention and availability review.
- Special media engines may need provider-specific asynchronous job APIs and object storage, not a chat completion endpoint.

## 5. Model registry — canonical typed schema

```json
{
  "model_id": "hey-one-general-candidate",
  "status": "BENCHMARKED",
  "base": {"publisher": "Qwen", "repo_id": "Qwen/Qwen3-8B", "revision": "ACTUAL_SHA_REQUIRED", "weights_sha256": "ACTUAL_HASH_REQUIRED", "license": "REVIEWED_LICENSE_REQUIRED"},
  "adapter": {"type": "none", "artifact_hash": null, "owner": null},
  "runtime": {"kind": "hosted_or_selfhosted", "endpoint_secret_ref": "secret_manager_reference", "supports_streaming": true, "supports_json": "TO_VERIFY", "supports_tools": "TO_VERIFY"},
  "roles": ["general_brain", "summarizer", "teacher_planner"],
  "modalities": ["text"],
  "verified_languages": [],
  "resource_budget": {"max_cost_per_request_usd": 0.01, "max_parallel_calls": 1, "p95_ms": null},
  "privacy": {"allowed_data_scopes": ["public", "user_consented"], "school_data_allowed": false},
  "evaluation": {"suite_version": "PENDING", "task_success_rate": null, "citation_precision": null, "security_false_allow_rate": null},
  "routing": {"fallback_ids": [], "circuit_breaker": true, "quality_tier": "baseline"},
  "rollout": {"approved_by": null, "promoted_at": null, "rollback_to": null}
}
```

**Contract:** Unknown means `null`/unverified, never optimistic defaults. Per-role scorecards map to actual model instance IDs. The server, not an LLM, enforces entitlements, privacy eligibility, call budgets, user authorization, output contracts and action mandates.

## 6. Cost, hardware and training honesty

- HEY's initial cloud operating budget is **$25–50/month**. The earlier provisional allocation was ~$25 Supabase Pro, ~$5 Cloudflare Workers Paid, ~$12 prepaid inference, ~$2 amortized domain and ~$5 contingency. This is a **planning proposal** requiring live vendor eligibility/pricing checks, not a purchased subscription or guaranteed hard cap.
- A several-tens-of-gigabytes model may have a small number of *active* MoE parameters, but the full total weights still require hosting/caching/storage. Active parameters do not eliminate memory, bandwidth, or total cost.
- The 8GB/older laptop needs an optional minimal companion (Edge), not a mandatory HEY One server. Use local tiny classifiers when appropriate and cloud LLM if permissioned/affordable.
- Model research, GPU rentals, training, video rendering and school pilot consumption must be budgeted separately if they exceed the $12 inference allocation. Do not auto-provision GPU servers.
- Any training plan should have an estimated per-run accelerator bill, storage/output cost, retry budget, expected benefit and stop criteria before initiation.
- Make every model route independently disableable on high cost, privacy failure, benchmark regression or provider outage.

## 7. Testable user examples for model-to-model composition

### A. Build a native application
User: “Make a functional desktop app for my school lesson planner.” HEY: identifies platform/resources → architect creates structured design → coder changes scoped repo → compile/test tools run → UI agent performs browser/native inspection → independent verifier checks install/run → document actual outputs. No “compiled” claim without tool receipt, no “deployed” claim without real URL/runtime.

### B. Edit one part of a presentation
User: “Change only the headline on slide 3; preserve every other slide.” HEY: resolves artifact version → editable document graph → model proposes exact semantic diff → deterministic renderer/exporter → compare unchanged slides 1,2,4+ and all non-target elements → produce verified export and rollback snapshot. The editing model is only one piece.

### C. Generate marketing video
User: “Generate fifteen seconds with these three product shots, and keep the approved brand text.” HEY: storyboard → scene constraints/locked assets → priced job proposal → appropriate licensed video/image engine → actual clip result → duration/content/brand verification → accessible media artifact with edit controls. Credit exhaustion checkpoints cleanly; no fake video preview.

### D. Tutoring and teaching
Teacher: “Create a Grade 8 chemistry worksheet and quiz from this approved textbook page.” HEY: parse pages → evidence-grounded lesson planner → age/level alignment → answer key fact check → worksheet/export renderer → Kurdish/English/Arabic layout if requested → teacher review → saved version. No real pupil data needed for a trial.

### E. Sorani and speech
User code-switches Kurdish/English, says “rewrite this paragraph, don't execute a command.” HEY Flow records as dictation, transcribes with confidence, applies requested edits in focused app, never routes dictated words into privileged VoiceOS commands. On lost microphone permission the stream must stop with accurate status.

## 8. Official source checks used for the 2026-10-15 candidate review

- Hugging Face LoRA/QLoRA workflow: https://huggingface.co/docs/trl/peft_integration ; official Hub model cards: https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/model-cards ; Hub CLI: https://huggingface.co/docs/huggingface_hub/guides/cli .
- Licenses and repositories **must be rechecked at an exact pinned revision at acquisition time**, not treated as immutable because this dated specification says they existed.

# 06 — HEY GOLDEN USER JOURNEYS AND INDEPENDENT ACCEPTANCE TESTS

**57 executable test contracts; NOT executed.** These are additive acceptance tests, not substitutes for detailed original per-subsystem test requirements. School tests must use fictional people and synthetic records until formal authorization. Before each attempt, replace generic wording with exact build routes, device IDs and configured services from the actual repository. Never invent results.

All scenarios must record exact SHA, service/device, request/action, actual output, negative-condition observation, independent verifier, screenshots/recordings where safe, latency and provider spend. Tests that require a service or hardware absent from the current environment remain `BLOCKED_EXTERNAL` rather than `PASSED`.

## HEY-E2E-001 — Auth: New account
**Action:** New user registers with permitted email method; confirm real provider and persisted identity

# 07 — COMPLETE MODEL-ROLE IMPLEMENTATION CARDS

This chapter expands all 75 documented logical roles from `MODEL_ROLE_MATRIX.csv`. **Roles do not require 75 independent trained weight sets.** Every card is a design contract, not evidence the implementation exists. Role owners derive richer use cases from the original master source, verify rights and evaluate hardware before selecting weights.

## M-001 — Orchestrator / HEY One General
**Initial execution architecture:** general LLM + tool runtime. **Foundation candidate or implementation starting point:** Qwen3-8B or gpt-oss-20b.
**Training/evaluation input program:** multi-step mission traces, precise final state, correct tool selection.
**Measurable evaluation:** task success, evidence fidelity, cost and latency.
**Completion evidence:** a frozen model/tool revision, typed output and permission scope, representative held-out dataset, independent measured improvement (or documented decision not to train), actual service result, failure-path result, cost/latency and rollback. **Forbidden:** fictitious training, invented metrics, provider API called owned weights.

## M-002 — Intent and task classifier
**Initial execution architecture:** small typed classifier/rules. **Foundation candidate or implementation starting point:** small encoder or Qwen3-8B as temporary.
**Training/evaluation input program:** user utterances labeled intents and uncertainty.
**Measurable evaluation:** macro-F1, OOD abstention, multilingual.
**Completion evidence:** a frozen model/tool revision, typed output and permission scope, representative held-out dataset, independent measured improvement (or documented decision not to train), actual service result, failure-path result, cost/latency and rollback. **Forbidden:** fictitious training, invented metrics, provider API called owned weights.

# PART ONE — NEWEST DECISIONS

# LATEST APPROVED REFINEMENTS — explicit full behavioral specification

This chapter complements, never replaces, the original 39,501-line HEY source; conflicts are resolved according to the preceding precedence rules. Each behavioral statement should become a traceable requirement with ID, source, owning domain, conditions, expected result, permission boundaries, error/recovery path and independent acceptance evidence. “Should” refers to design intent; external-platform constraints remain real.

## R01. Global product definition and experience

HEY is one AI Life Operating System and personal intelligence environment: assistant, operating layer, second brain, research and creative system, planning and business companion, developer studio, teacher experience, device bridge and extensible intelligent platform. Users ask for outcomes, not which of hundreds of hidden agents to call. The same Brain, Cosmos, security/trust, mission, tool and artifact infrastructure serves every mode. Never implement duplicate teacher/developer/voice-specific brains as shortcuts. Expose expert controls only if wanted. Subsystems must communicate through versioned typed contracts, capability manifests and data/event schema migrations.

Primary promise: user expresses intention by text/voice/screen/selection/camera; HEY selects tools/agents/models/devices, requests authorization when necessary, executes, verifies actual state and reports what really happened. A response must never claim an external file was edited, a lesson exported, a message sent, or a device action completed without a real success receipt and independent target-state check where feasible. Preserve undo, version history, progress, pause, resume, cancellation and diagnostics.

## R02. Global UX, navigation, brand, themes and motion

**Default after authentication is the Chat/Voice Conversation Surface.** The user's recent conversation, project, artifact and current mission are restored when safe; user-configured startup override wins. Persistent prominent destinations Home (conversational entry + contextual personal view), Tools, Spaces, Activity, Settings; dedicated Create/Projects/Cosmos/Live routes and advanced inspectors may be reachable from navigation, search and quick actions without cluttering the default. “Home” must not become a mandatory generic dashboard before HEY can be used.

Desktop: compact/collapsible/resizable sidebar, command palette, global shortcuts, split/overlay artifact workspaces, window management. Tablet: adaptive rails/panels, rotation, touch. Mobile: bottom nav + context drawers, voice-first affordances, safe-area, virtual keyboard and offline views. Large displays/smartboards: readable distance type, privacy-aware public display, multi-user handoff where legitimate. Keyboard navigation, screen readers, focus management, touch targets, RTL (Kurdish/Arabic), localization, reduced-motion and high contrast must be tested. Theme direction is premium near-black graphite glass, real depth, tactile interactive states, muted nature accents; avoid cyan hologram clichés and performance-heavy effects on weak hardware. Adjustable themes/accents, visual density, typography and motion; user can choose a brighter variant without losing contrast.

Every major feature requires discoverable, contextual, animated or stepwise tutorial, replayable/skippable with a text fallback. Tutorial must use real product UI state and not demo a nonexistent action. Empty/error/offline/pending/no-permission/expired-token/recovery states are designed, not generic spinners. Startup, install/updates and PWA vs native must be clearly differentiated. Dynamic Island is genuinely native/persistent where supported: survives main app minimize/close while authorized helper remains active, exposes task-relevant controls (Voice call, media, jobs, timers, approvals, errors, handoffs); never masquerade a React card as a system-wide overlay.

## R03. First-run onboarding and adaptive preference setup

First major question **“Why do you want to use HEY?”** with multi-select: `AI Assistant`, `AI Models`, `Control & Automation`, `Create & Build`, `Teaching & Learning`, `Life & Work`, `Custom`, `Skip`. Each choice shows plain-language examples, not unexplained model/provider acronyms. Multiple options allowed; the selection initializes recommendations, pins, suggested Spaces and the right onboarding tutorial. No choice permanently hides other tools. Custom accepts user's own goal in natural language; Skip yields excellent default Chat/Voice access. Permissions for mic/camera/screen/devices are asked contextually rather than all at once. Users can later change role interests, tool pins, language, model preferences, voice, theme and startup location; all persist across permitted devices. School organization membership is a separate access grant and never inferred from selecting Teaching.

Acceptance: first-run select Developer + Teacher, create default mixed Space, launch tools in both categories, restart and verify all preferences retained; account B cannot read A's onboarding state; skip works; denied mic still allows chat.

## R04. Modes, personalities, adaptive answer depth

Use original full mode/personality source. Recognize Quick, Standard, Deep Dive, Mentor, Strategist, Research, Creative, Emotional Support, Crisis, Teacher, Debate, Execution, custom combinations and earlier user-favored Hey Brother/Explorer style as product options where appropriately defined. Modes guide voice/style/tool/routing, never strip baseline capabilities or alter permission policy. Auto adapts to complexity, user preferences and task. Voice default concise natural with expandable full transcript/artifacts; Chat can be detailed, structured and citations-backed. Brand personality may use a calm deep British male voice option; voice library, legitimate user-authorized custom voice and wake-word preferences. Avoid implying medically or legally regulated professional advice is certified.

## R05. Tools Library + universal discovery + command palette

One canonical capability registry supports installed/available/experimental/platform-constrained entries, per-person/account/organization permissions, costs, dependency health, entitlements and discoverability. Search semantic natural-language requests e.g. “write by speaking everywhere”, “control this slide with my hand”, “edit slide three only”, “run an agent over my code”, “teach chemistry using a quiz” and return actual launchable tools and a truthful support explanation. Each tool provides name/category/description, examples, launch/stop, configure, permissions, status, platform matrix, model/provider dependencies, usage/allowance display, errors/help/version. Provide Favorites, Recently Used, popular/recommended, pin/reorder/add shortcuts, context-aware suggestion and advanced mode. Do not list internal agents as ordinary apps. Tool availability must be evaluated server/runtime side, not only with hidden UI flags.

Tool launch lifecycle: DISCOVERED → PERMISSION_REQUIRED/READY → STARTING → RUNNING → PAUSED/DEGRADED/FAILED → STOPPED, with durable mission linkage when needed. Missing plugin or disconnected provider launches a concrete connection/permissions flow, not fake success.

## R06. Custom Spaces — the user's own operating environment

A Space is a persistently named user- or organization-scoped environment containing selected tools, widgets, project contexts, layouts, shortcuts, saved Living Answers, models, language/theme tweaks and filtered activity. Provide create/rename/duplicate/archive/delete, import/export if safe, default templates, blank canvas, natural-language Space setup with preview, pinned catalog selection, drag/reorder/resize/snap/stack/minimize/dock, multiple view layouts, task/project tabs, undo/redo/snapshots. A Developer may add Teacher tools; a Teacher may add Software Studio and Model Lab. Spaces do not create authorization: access depends on the underlying user/org permission for every item. Organization-managed spaces inherit policy but cannot silently overwrite personal Spaces. Context switch cannot lose draft or active tasks; preserve safe mission continuity. User controls startup Space and workspace defaults. Load only active widgets and refresh them within resource budgets.

Workspace widgets: clock/date/timezone, weather, calendar, task list, routines, notes, project status, music/media, timer, notifications, news, quote, prayer/Quran/Hadith if enabled, HEY/S&A stats where authorized, device battery/health, research, terminal, code, audio, image, video, saved art, agent monitors. Sensitivity is location/time dependent: user controls location and religious widgets; public-display mode conceals private content. Weather/prayer info has source and freshness. Broken widget cannot crash full workspace; stale data explicitly labeled.

## R07. HEY Living Answers — full Generative UI engine

User intent determines output form. A short fact uses concise text; a numerical comparison uses a chart/table; navigating a city uses a real map; editing a file uses an editable artifact; building a calculator can generate a sandboxed working mini-app. Rich component vocabulary includes:

- Editorial: headings, block quotes, inline equations, citations, references and verified source links, collapsible details, comparison tables, badges limited to real statuses.
- Data: sortable/filterable virtual tables, graph/bar/line/pie/scatter/time series, trend lines, uncertainty bands, KPI tiles, export, unit and currency calculations using trusted math code.
- Controls: sliders, switches, segmented selections, radio/checkbox, dates, time ranges, file pickers, editable field/form validation, play/pause, progress, optimistic state with rollback where safe.
- Places: geocoded maps, multi-stop routes, travel time/ETA when backed by actual provider, nearby business data, opening hours with data freshness and verified reservation availability.
- Media: images, before/after, gallery/carousel, 3D/AR previews where supported, audio waveform/player, video/tracks, rich captions/transcripts, camera/screen previews with visible permission states.
- Work: editable doc/spreadsheet/presentation, source-code diff, interactive terminal/test output, calendar event, task board, milestone timeline, agents/delegations, mission logs, approval cards, file/result previews, provenance.
- Learning: flashcards, quizzes, interactive science/simulation diagrams, step-by-step visual math, hint/reveal, progress and teacher feedback.
- Generated app: calculator/planner/dashboard/custom workflow, bounded local state, save/export/reopen, declared data connectors and actions, versioned sandbox.

**Rendering contract:** model outputs a validated, versioned declarative scene/AST describing allowed components, data schema, trust level, source/citation IDs, event handlers by server-known action ID, state persistence scope, permissions and streaming/lifecycle states. Never trust raw model-produced HTML/JS/CSS as privileged app code. The renderer checks schema/size/depth/URL/safe markup, encodes text, enforces resource limits, a11y and content security, and denies unauthorized actions. Rich components using untrusted user-supplied code run in isolated iframe/webview/worker sandboxes (depending on platform) with explicit capability channel and bounded network/file access; clean fallback to static content on unsupported devices. Do not expose keys in component props. All host write actions go through Trust Kernel authorization, actual result receipt and optional undo. Data binds to real scoped services; stale/failed and unavailable states visible, without made-up numbers. A control never advertises a feature it cannot perform.

**Persistence:** Save widget to Space/project/conversation; versions, source data, interaction state and permissions persist only as authorized. On reconnect, restore from safe snapshot; if data source revoked show explanation and enable repair, never silently reuse stale privileged data. External links sourced from actual provider/reference records. User can copy/export where type permits. Voice can narrate widget changes, and screen reader/touch interaction must remain possible. Generated widgets have a resource/cost allowance and suspend when hidden as appropriate.

**Acceptance examples:** user asks for AI-cost calculator → functional sliders recalculate totals (server-backed pricing must show date); saves to Business Space → reload persists; switch account → unauthorized view fails; revoke price data → stale/disabled state; inject malicious model-output component → blocked; keyboard-only interaction passes; small-phone layout works; graph with missing data never invents data; click Deploy requires explicit real mandate and returns actual deployment receipt.

## R08. Detail Intelligence — owner-level attention to small important details

HEY analyzes high-stakes tasks for missing requirements, assumptions, scope gaps, dependencies, failure modes, ongoing costs, security, permissions, maintenance and user experience. Example for a business launch: payment-provider eligibility in the owner's country, bank/age/contract requirements, taxes, refund and support workflow, capacity, billing ceilings, backups, vendor outages, licensing, legal/privacy notices, signup/account recovery, measured performance, cancellation and accessibility. For software: exact build/runtime versions, contract matching, migrations, resource exhaustion, secret handling, rollback, edge cases, realistic tests, platform permission differences. For school: real teacher pain points, smartboard hardware/model/camera presence, offline internet, student data policy, localized materials, printable/exportable formats, substitutes, training and maintenance.

Present **explicit requirements**, **approved changes**, **inferred risks**, **recommended additions** separately. Ask approval before implementing materially new product direction or spending money. Avoid bloat or one generic disclaimer repeated every time. The attention engine may use deterministic domain checklists + model critique + source checks on valuable tasks; it may not claim certainty it does not have. Surface one highest-value overlooked item in brief mode, a fuller risk/dependency map in company-owner/advanced mode. Store rejected suggestions to avoid repetition. Measure precision of valid reminders vs nuisance rate; require user override and adjustable proactivity.

## R09. Product Integrity Engine — requirements that survive agent/context turnover

Every project/change has append-only auditable events (`proposed`, `clarified`, `approved`, `rejected`, `superseded`, `implemented`, `integrated`, `verified`, `released`, `regressed`). Canonical requirement record: stable ID, source conversation/document, exact excerpt/hash, author, created/changed time, privacy scope, approval status, priority, version, semantic summary, acceptance criteria, dependencies, affected systems, owner, implementation links, commits, tests, evidence artifacts, risk, rollout and rollback; sensitive texts ACL-scoped. Distinguish direct user commands vs speculation, quoted data, assistant ideas and tool outputs. Revisions are typed `adds`, `narrows`, `replaces`, `contradicts`, `clarifies`. Superseded versions remain readable to authorized owners. Never infer approval from silence.

On new requested work: retrieve relevant approved state and conflicting history, propose resolved behavior, diff old/new, show what will be preserved, and create/refine acceptance tests. Before claiming feature completion, trace each applicable requirement to UI/backend/db/provider/native tests and independent evidence; flag omissions, unverified claims, broken integrations, unavailable sources and regression to an old design. Avoid just “all requirements read”: verify actual agent got relevant text plus stable source references. Cross-chat personal memory requires user permission; school/org records cannot leak between tenants. Deletion must remove user-governed data according to retention policy without silently compromising legally required audit logs. Reconcile concurrent updates transactionally; conflict UI and rollback. Product Integrity must not hallucinate recovered history.

**Proof scenario:** A→Developer mode; B→Developer includes Teacher tools; C→all Modes customizable Spaces. After context reset, HEY returns final C design and records A/B lineage, identifies an implementation with a hard-coded Developer-only tools list as erroneous, finds code owner, generates failing test, verifies fix in application. Another example: prototype says successfully generated PDF but returned empty object → completion rejected.

## R10. Chat, Voice, Live, HEY Brother and invocation

The complete conversation is one canonical timeline across text/voice/live, with attachments, sources, mission references, project context, widget state and artifacts. Voice should feel like a real call: living visualizer, listening/thinking/speaking states, mute, end, captions, interrupt/barge-in, audio output/voice choice, camera/screen controls, inline active task. Deep calm polished British male voice as preferred default option subject to an appropriate licensed TTS voice; custom voices only with authorization and consent. Wake word configurable, with brand `HEY` preferred and historical `Wake up` an allowed custom value; activation via wake word, push-to-talk, manual action and user-controlled background listening. Per-device visibility and low-power behavior, mic/privacy indicator, wake-word false-positive tests, noisy classroom adaptation, echo cancellation, VAD, timeouts, recovery if speech recognition double-starts. Do not retain raw audio by default beyond processing needs. Detect English, Sorani Kurdish, Kurmanji and Arabic where models genuinely support accuracy, fallback gracefully and expose corrections. User can turn off voice entirely and use quiet text.

Live may combine chosen screen/window/monitor/region, camera, file and audio sources. Guide overlays target controls, Assist proposes steps, Act follows scoped authorization and verifies. Stop/pause/revoke available instantly; external page/document content is untrusted and cannot command HEY as authority. Selection “Ask HEY about this” uses scoped capture only, never full-device hidden harvesting. Common mission can continue between modalities without spawning duplicate actions.

## R11. HEY Flow dictation, native VoiceOS and gestures are separable products

**HEY Flow:** global shortcut/toolbar/compact overlay, start/stop, microphone state, speech recognition, auto punctuation, capitalization, filler cleanup, custom vocabulary, snippets, rewrite selected text, translation if requested, dictation into actual focused application where permitted, per-app settings and offline/local/cloud selection. Make text insertion atomic or undoable and safe: preserve cursor/selection, detect focus switches and private fields, avoid sending sensitive text to wrong app, show targeted preview on ambiguous actions. If an app blocks global injection, offer clipboard/authorized share fallback. Distinguish transcription from commands (“open file” spoken while dictating should not launch a file without explicit mode/intent).

**VoiceOS:** “open VS Code”, “locate this file”, “rename it”, “organize my desktop”, “change slide” uses shared actual computer-use action engine; scoped approvals, confirmation where appropriate, postcondition and action logs. Controlled by Voice, keyboard/command palette or screen selection; no action falsely reports success because OS adapter returned an optimistic result. Guide/Assist/Act levels. **Gesture mode** can be launched alone by a user who never talks to HEY. Gesture controls function on Android smartboards or attached cameras subject to hardware realities; users can map gestures per app, workspace, device and teacher profile.

## R12. Complete gesture vocabulary and calibration

Default proposed-to-test gesture mapping (may be adjusted per real hardware/use case): open palm → show HEY/overview; open palm→fist → grab; held fist motion → move widget; pinch → select/click; pinch-and-move → precision drag; spread both hands → enlarge/zoom; bring together → reduce; swipe left/right → previous/next slide or page depending on context; swipe up → restore; swipe down → minimize; two fingers → pause/resume; point+pinch → target+activate; raised hand → stop HEY speech; thumbs up/down → low-risk confirm/dismiss only; both palms → leave manipulation. Provide presentation-focused profiles with reverse slide mapping if requested. All mappings customizable; none grants payment/data-deletion authorization.

Calibration: available camera enumeration + explicit permission, device orientation, distance/light evaluation, handedness, threshold/hold/cooldown, confidence feedback, conflict and accidental detection, gesture preview with dry-run, custom-gesture recording and versioning, pause/hide/stop, on-device pose where practical, frame budget and frame-rate throttling on weak hardware, webcam/device disconnect auto-stop. Target disambiguation via focus/pointer/voice context; don't click random targets. Recorded raw video not saved by default. Custom gesture enrollment requires clear data deletion. No student-face identification for class operation unless a separate authorized consent-sensitive use case is explicitly approved; camera is for hand tracking.

## R13. HEY Board — Leaders smartboard-specific details

Distinct teacher smartboard helper/experience, not merely a separate presentation generator. For Android boards with uncertain camera/API support: investigate physical camera, supported Android version, external USB webcam, system microphone, OEM lockdown, accessibility APIs, local network, screen/control integration. Provide a real compatibility diagnostic report. Device management should not assume unsupported device-owner/kiosk provisioning; user previously rejected default kiosk/device-owner mode and teacher proximity confirmation. Enable teacher-created/deletable profiles with own wake word and a safe default/no-profile fallback. Teacher access may use school/S&A-approved codes; proper codes must be revocable and tied to organization policy, not universal backdoor. Principal dashboard/PIN/role only if securely designed. Offline core gesture controls and presentation profiles should remain available where hardware permits; local encrypted profiles, predictable background lifecycle and restart recovery; clear wake/active indicators, noise adaptation, camera/mic controls, per-board keys, health monitor/self-healing with loop prevention and user stop. Real teacher verification, no unapproved student face recognition, and public-display privacy. Substitutes can use safe generic profile when permitted. End-of-Class button/task ends class-relevant temporary permissions, clears sensitive on-screen content, saves/exports teacher work as configured and releases board sessions without deleting teacher artifacts. Do not advertise capability if Android hardware/OS cannot support it.

## R14. Teacher Mode and full school platform, distinguished

**HEY Teacher Mode** is one configurable HEY Space/tool collection with teacher identity/grade/subject/preferences, lesson outlines, concept explanations, differentiated difficulty, teacher-guided tutoring, PDF/textbook imports, worksheets, question banks, quizzes, exams, answer keys, activities, presentations, classroom visualizations, homework, rubrics, editable/exportable documents, printable materials, re-use, version history and smartboard integration. Teachers should request “change only question 4” or “simplify slide 3 without touching the others” with Pinpoint fidelity. Edits happen inside conversation-linked Studio. Teacher code grants school-specific mode only after server-side validation; code itself is not unrestricted administrative access. Kurdish/English/Arabic layout and print correctness tested. User remains free to add coding/model/creator tools from other categories.

**Full school management platform** is a separate ambitious integration surface with teacher/student/parent/admin roles, timetable, assignments/submission, grades, attendance, transport/bus reporting, announcements, end-of-class workflows, student progress, resource portals, permissions, audit and school policy; avoid copying or conflicting with existing principal-facing buses/attendance/grades system without integration agreements. Principal/IT requirements precede real data onboarding. Do not confuse “school platform planned” with something already sold/approved for use. HEY stays one common intelligence. School pilot can use teacher content and synthetic pupils before written school authorization for real student data. Child data, parent visibility, data retention, role isolation, audit, school contractual status and age-appropriate security require explicit governance.

**Teacher needs discovery:** a bilingual Sorani+English double-sided A4 form for all teachers asks (1) time-consuming/difficult tasks, (2) classroom/smartboard/equipment/systems problems, (3) tasks to simplify and desired tools, (4) anything teachers would improve at school; optional teacher name/subject/grade and priority field. Two questions per page, large writing areas, school-first branding; `S&A × Leaders` only if school authorizes co-brand. Completed feedback must become a needs register, with user-approved priorities, measurable acceptance criteria and feature owner; teacher requests are user research, not automatically all approved development scope.

## R15. HEY Edge: tiny trusted native companion + Device Mesh

Cloud/hosted HEY Brain need not run on user laptop. Edge has minimal idle footprint; real OS adapters for file/window/process/screen/clipboard/shortcuts/notifications, per-app automation, mic/wake, local gesture inference and verified device actions; no fake platform parity. Windows: UI Automation, window/process/filesystem/input APIs; macOS: Accessibility, ScreenCaptureKit, Shortcuts/AppleScript where legitimate; Linux: xdg portals, Wayland/X11, DBus; Android: intents, foreground-service notifications, user-enabled accessibility where appropriate, MediaProjection, camera, share flows; iOS/iPadOS: App Intents/Shortcuts/share extensions/Live Activities, no privileged unrestricted background terminal for ordinary apps; Web/PWA: constrained browser APIs. Enforce signed scoped mandates, device registration/pairing, nonce/replay/expiry and audit, revocation on target change, local policy; immediate stop and least-privilege. Device Mesh can handoff projects/mission state by authorized encrypted channel and choose device based on active capabilities, not invent access to an offline device. Conserve RAM/CPU/battery on older hardware; disable fancy effects as appropriate. No raw screen/audio retention without user's explicit settings.

## R16. Personal memory / Cosmos, research and situation

Cosmos uses event timeline + structured profile/project/fact graph + embeddings/search index as needed. Facts include source, confidence, timestamps, subject, consent scope, owner and supersession. Do not “save every single piece of info” indiscriminately; support user-selectable privacy scopes, private/no-memory modes, memory inbox and explicit deletion/corrections. Query current relevant memory without dumping all context into every prompt; retrieve evidence; explain when data is stale. Context compiler uses consented real-time situation/time/location/device/current document, not covert data harvesting. Cross-org/private data must never leak to shared school project. Universal search uses local docs/connectors/web with freshness, citations and injection defense; distinguish search results from instructions. Project DNA and Pinpoint Precision enforce consistent branding/approved assets and surgical edits across outputs.

## R17. Agents, Intelligence Council, Forge, Evolution, automations and proactivity

Model and agents are separate axes. A 229-specialist historical catalog is neither an engine limit nor 229 always-running expensive models. Agent registry supports families → specialists → temporary specialists, lazy retrieval, typed contracts, scope, permissions, health/cost/timeout/retry/evaluation/retirement. Evidence Board and council select only helpful participants (Architect, Builder, Verifier, Contrarian, Flaw Hunter, Opportunity Hunter, Missing-Requirement Hunter, UX/Business/Teacher etc.); preserve minority evidence and stop debate when marginal gain is low. Deterministic policies, math, schedulers, validators and classifiers should not waste large-model tokens. Forge safely synthesizes tools/workflows/agents/actions if existing tools do not suffice, with source/dependency analysis, sandbox/dry run, Risk Twin + Solution Twin, tests, preview, opt-in save, versioning and revocation. Evolution observes useful advancements and makes evidence-backed proposals; ordinary owners approve new internal product evolution, critical security emergency procedure may permit fast fixes with transparent rollback and notifications. Never let an AI self-approve privileged change.

Automations are durable event/time schedules, with timezone/DST, idempotency, atomic outbox, retry with backoff, poison queue, pause/resume/recovery/revoke, visible next-run and last-run receipts. Morning/Focus/Review modes and proactive nudges use consent and configurable quiet hours; no spam or repetitive suggestions. Real scheduled work must outlive browser tab closure where legitimate and report unavoidable external blocks.

## R18. Full studios and pinpoint output

Image: text-to-image, image editing, variations, masks/object-level selection, reference styles and locked subject consistency; edit exactly requested region. Video: prompt/image/storyboard/first-last-frame → clips, multi-shot assembly, script, scene planning, continuity, camera motion, retime/split/trim/crop, titles, subtitles, voiceover, audio ducking, source/project provenance, long-form via scenes and actual export. Audio/music/speech: transcription, enhancement, narration, TTS, licensed sound/music generation, dubbing, translation, diarization if supported. Motion: kinetic typography, charts, transitions, product/UI demos and editable scene graphs. Documents/books/PDF/presentations/spreadsheets: editable layouts, graphs, speaker/content synchronization, formulas, pagination, language, print/export and revision/undo. Code/software/websites: repo editing, semantic diff, build/run/tests, previews, dependency/license checks and secure file/secret controls.

Embedded studio: user requests creation inside Chat/Voice → a synchronized Studio opens in same conversation with current project/context; user can keep talking, change only page/slide/shot three, collapse/expand full Studio without losing history, see structured progress and a real generated artifact. Dedicated Studio route opens same state, not a duplicate. Do not fabricate “video generated” when only an image/storyboard exists. Creation providers may be usage-priced; plan allowances and capability fallback. Media output must respect relevant content licensing and rights and should never imply an external provider has been called when not.

## R19. Organizations, family, marketplace, API, billing

Three top-level S&A founders/owners govern HEY according to original source; audit owner commands and use strong MFA/re-auth; no fourth top-level owner via normal API flow; public extension publication requires all three owner's authorization if that original rule remains approved; critical proven security fixes have monitored emergency process/notification. Organizations use role-based membership, separate data, entitlements, audit and policy. If HEY supports parent/child/family accounts, implement careful privacy, permissions and age restrictions; do not silently expose a child's conversation to unrelated guardians. Marketplace extensions have signed manifest, trust review, dependency scanning, versions, sandbox, publication and quarantine/revocation. Public developer APIs must be versioned and explicit about quota/permissions and avoid exposing internal secrets.

Subscription layers may include Free, Pro, Elite and institution licensing; plan entitlements are independent of payment provider; metering includes tokens, tool calls, expensive media, GPU minutes, storage and concurrent agents. Do not promise unlimited costly usage under a flat plan. Payment providers must be legal/available for S&A's actual jurisdiction and merchant eligibility (Iraq cannot be assumed supported by Stripe/Paddle); use approved adult/business representative for provider and school contracts as appropriate. Refund/support/failed payment/webhook dedup and transactional ledger are production requirements. Avoid storing card data directly.

## R20. Deployment and operating budget — approved current constraint

Initial HEY monthly cloud operating ceiling: **$25–$50**. Proposed cost envelope: Supabase Pro $25 for one paid Postgres/Auth project; Cloudflare Workers Paid $5 for web/API; model inference $12 prepaid, no auto-recharge; domain annual reserve ~$2/month; uncommitted reserve $5. These are planning allocations, not guaranteed enforceable all-vendor bill caps or approval to purchase. Prefer Cloudflare R2 within free allowances for private object storage; managed auth/DB and lightweight API, legitimate queue/workflow for long tasks, SMTP mail free tier while eligible, GitHub CI, basic monitoring. Separate stage and production secrets/data; staging use synthetic info and a free DB project where suitable; never grant staging service role in prod. Real runtime data stores authorization/revocation, durable jobs, memory, budget holds and audited receipts; mocks/in-memory state don't qualify. Reject arbitrary “everything runs inside Workers” design for long/CPU/GPU jobs. Paid hosted inference rather than dedicated GPU initially; actual GPU training/serving requires separate approved compute. Rate limits and provider spend controls must handle concurrency and irreversible costs. Use spend/failure/latency alerts, backups plus real restore drill, incident stop/rollback. Benchmark actual users in Kurdistan and classroom networks where possible.

School pilot: isolate one approved Leaders organization with 5–10 initial teacher accounts and fictional student records, small $3 portion of initial $12 inference allowance; no assumption of unlimited teacher generation. Teacher questionnaire, IT coordination, compatibility and printed forms are not fully paid for by cloud envelope. HEY public rollout and school pilot are separate release audiences, with transparent readiness and support.

## R21. Continuous engineering execution and reality check

The real codebase must be inventoried by SHA before claims. Coordinator-reported 500/500 tests and 73/73 Fusion/Edge tests are historical code-level evidence but NOT proof of live DB, deployed Deno functions, native device, real model provider or browser end-to-end validation. Do not restart 11 specialists merely to rename tasks. Make tasks vertical: actual user journey → UI/backend/provider/db/native → auth/privacy → error/recovery → independent verification. Maintain one canonical integration/release branch; isolate parallel work in distinct worktrees; frontend has sole shared UI ownership while backend owners export contracts; integration owner resolves compatibility and QA owner independently retests. Never create one gigantic same-file merge conflict across agents.

Use status chain MISSING → DESIGNED → IMPLEMENTING → FUNCTIONAL → INTEGRATED → VERIFIED → PRODUCTION_READY; also distinguish external credentials/hardware blockers. An entire 47-step item is NOT “done” based on one green test. Every feature entry must link source, final requirement, real entrypoint, commits, live provider evidence, auth/security, cross-account tests, failure injection, weak-device tests and rollback. When external services unavailable, build independently testable code and state honestly what remains; neither fake a deployment nor idle all workers. Recover or replace unavailable requirement inventories only with visible provenance. Independent full-product QA covers new and returning users, permission denial/revoke, provider timeout/429, network drop, stale/missing data, multiple concurrent calls, retries/idempotency, native helper crash, corrupted state, backup restore, school-user isolation, device-specific restrictions, a11y/RTL and low-resource behavior.

## R22. Known product-version conflict decisions (prevent old agents from reverting)

- Historical fixed mode catalogs / non-customizable modes → superseded by fully customizable Spaces, cross-category tools and personalized onboarding. Preserve useful original modes as templates/behaviors.
- Old dashboards as default → superseded; signed-in landing is unified Chat/Voice unless user changes.
- Historical fixed 229 agents → legacy seed; no arbitrary system limit; lazy loaded, not displayed as apps.
- “4,210 features” → engineering inventory items, NOT number of separate HEY apps or widgets.
- Local full supermodel on 8-GB laptop → superseded by remote HEY One + compact HEY Edge / optional small local models.
- All-billing-free imperative → updated to $25–50 approved monthly envelope, but no unapproved purchases.
- Gesture control only inside chat or web window → wrong; native/Android helper as supported, teacher-presentations first-class and independent use.
- Teacher Mode as only presentation builder → wrong; teacher workflow suite plus distinct future school management platform.
- UI “structured paragraphs” alone → wrong; Living Answers includes live functional widgets, maps, artifacts and sandboxed mini-apps.
- Current 11 specialists know all older chats → false; explicit source-bound per-task briefs are mandatory.
- Repeated audits without functioning release → unacceptable; final-product build must stay active with independent in-app E2E validation.
- “No gaps because an agent said so” → prohibited: evidence must be attached and rechecked.

## R23. Acceptance journeys from customer point of view

For each scenario run a real staged cross-account/device path, record timestamp, build SHA, actual backend/provider, input, output, artifacts, cost and failure/recovery:

1. New user signs up, verifies email, signs in, recovers account, revokes session.
2. User chooses Create & Build + Teaching; all other categories still discoverable; change preferences after onboarding.
3. Create Developer Space; add Teacher quiz and VoiceOS; reorder, rename, refresh browser/second device; layout persists.
4. Ask simple fact -> concise answer; complex task -> cited sources and actionable table; missing source -> no invented citation.
5. Ask for interactive calculator -> working controls, save to Space, refresh and restore, permission revoke behavior.
6. Start Voice, interrupt speaking, toggle Chat without losing active artifact/context, deny mic and continue text.
7. Use Flow dictation into authorized external text field with punctuation; switch focus/private field -> no unwanted insertion.
8. Say “open app” -> native companion acts with scoped mandate; real process/window verified.
9. Ask rename/move file -> correct file changed, receipt linked, safe undo available; denied folder doesn't change.
10. Webcam gesture Next/Previous slides -> correct presentations state, false positive protection, disconnected camera stop.
11. Teacher creates lesson, worksheet, quiz answer key and editable presentation from supplied source, exports and reloads.
12. Live screen guidance highlights actual element; stop capture revokes sensing and indicators disappear.
13. Create image with actual licensed provider; edit only selected region; check unchanged parts.
14. Storyboard-to-video job produces actual playable video where enabled, not synthetic receipt; export and resume.
15. Create/edit spreadsheet cells with formulas; reload and export with correct formula results.
16. Cosmos stores a consensual fact, recalls correct latest version, corrects/deletes and respects privacy/organization scope.
17. Automation scheduled in Baghdad timezone survives a server restart/DST where applicable, runs once, actual effect verified.
18. Model routing: cheap->strong escalation under task quality threshold, Fusion only when justified, show spend and rationale.
19. Native device handoff on trusted devices resumes task without duplicated side effects.
20. User revokes access during mission -> calls stop and UI reports partial exact status.
21. Cross-school/private account isolation including files, tools, memory, widgets and logs.
22. Load concurrent model requests against $12 prepaid allotment, ensure reservation/limiter and graceful exhausted-state.
23. Weak laptop UI and HEY Edge idle usage meet measured performance budget.
24. Owner Console escalation requires high-security login; extension publication follows required multi-owner policy.
25. Recovery drill: backup restore, schema rollback, killed worker, poison job, expired auth, provider outage and interrupted output.
26. Accessibility: screen reader, keyboard, touch, RTL Sorani/Arabic, screen magnification, reduced motion and captions.
27. Product Integrity detects requirement contradiction across multiple simulated contexts, warns of missing final behavior, rejects fake completion.
28. Install PWA in compatible browser, standalone startup, offline shell, upgrade, deep link; unsupported install explains limitations.
29. School smartboard teacher profiles independent wake phrases, default fallback, principal health view, End-of-Class privacy cleanup.
30. Full regression: none of the above is broken by the next merged specialist branch.

## R24. No open-ended self-improvement loop

The requirement to improve every system means achieving testable capabilities, not endless speculative optimization. Feature review must propose measurable refinements and implement approved refinements; unapproved new major concepts remain proposals. Freeze acceptance criteria for a version until clear new user approval; defects and regressions still must be fixed. Source amendments and version tags are distributed automatically to assigned agents and their tests updated. Nothing called “maximum performance” without hardware/cost/workload-specific benchmarks.

# PART TWO — MODEL FLEET

# HEY ONE + FUSION + COMPLETE SPECIALIST MODEL FLEET

## M00. What “our own AI model” means in engineering terms

A **capability role** (Coder, Editor, Presenter, Tutor, etc.) is not automatically a separately trained neural network. HEY should maintain *logical specialist contracts* and select the least costly reliable realization: deterministic algorithm, constrained prompt/tool schema, a licensed hosted model, a dedicated open-weight fine-tuned adapter, or a full separately trained model only when cost/evaluation warrants it. Otherwise 60 specialist models would create high GPU bills, version drift and inconsistent permissions. Do not mislead users by branding APIs as weights that S&A owns; differentiate `HEY One branded routing`, `HEY One adapted model checkpoint`, `licensed third-party foundation`, `S&A-trained adapter` and `S&A-trained-from-scratch model`.

HEY One initially = strongest legally usable foundation chosen through benchmarks + adapted LoRA/QLoRA specialists + system tool orchestration + verified memory/retrieval/action layer. Fine-tuning improves an existing foundation; retrieval changes the evidence available at inference; tooling performs actual actions; hard permission rules are enforced outside the model. A model should never be the sole authority for security or payments. Private proprietary third-party APIs do not give ownership of their weights, and their outputs are not automatically authorized training data.

## M01. Where to obtain genuine weights — verified starting points as of 2026-10-15

**Model acquisition portal:** https://huggingface.co/models and the **original publisher's model card**, not arbitrary Telegram links or unofficial repacks. Download by exact repo ID and pinned revision/commit, retain SHA-256, model card, license, README, dependencies, allowed uses and attribution. Some model cards are gated and require individual account approval. Re-check current card, model revision and rights before commercial use, redistribution or training; a model-hosting website's availability is not licensing permission.

Unverified families such as Wan, Qwen VL/TTS or newer releases remain candidate searches only until publisher card/model artifact/license are confirmed. Do not invent license terms.

**RECOMMENDATION:** Organize model artifacts in a licensed private registry, containing `repo_id`, `revision`, `artifact_sha`, `architecture`, `role`, `context_limit`, `modalities`, `languages`, `license`, `allowed_commercial_use`, `license_review_date`, `dataset provenance`, `tool reliability`, `quantization`, `runtime`, `RAM/VRAM requirements`, `per-token cost`, `latency p50/p95`, `evaluation score`, `fallback`, `rollback`, `approval status`. Never copy training data or API keys into a model repo accidentally.

## M02. Model training/adaptation is an evaluation-driven pipeline, not a model-count race

### Step-by-step acquisition

1. Define one specialist output contract, target users, input language/mode, allowed tools, required factual/procedural correctness and latency/cost budget.
2. Build 100–1000 representative **licensed and consented** evaluation cases before training, including English/Sorani/Arabic where appropriate, ambiguous/malicious inputs, realistic failure cases and counterfactual consistency tests. Separate public and private datasets; no real pupil records for experimental model training.
3. Benchmark 2–4 foundation candidates zero-shot/few-shot, then with deterministic tools/retrieval. If baseline + scaffolding meets acceptance, **do not train** a separate model simply for branding.
4. If a measurable gap remains, acquire publisher original weights, pin revision/hash/license and run a secure weight-loader vulnerability/dependency review. Prefer `safetensors` when available, avoiding blindly executing model repo code or pickle checkpoints.
5. Prepare role-focused dataset. Clean, de-identify, deduplicate, verify provenance, separate train/dev/test by project/user and time, remove test leakage. Example supervised records contain `messages` with explicit role and permitted structured tool plans, not model hallucinated success receipts.
6. Fine-tune LoRA (e.g. r=16/32, alpha adapted to rank, dropout, bf16, gradient checkpointing where supported); use QLoRA 4-bit for feasible GPUs and model/runtime compatibility. Treat parameter values as tuning *starting points*, not universal best settings. GPU must have headroom for gradients/optimizer/KV/sequences, not just weight sizes. The 8GB laptop is NOT a suitable platform for broad full-model training.
7. Compare new adapter against frozen base on blind task-level evaluation, red-team security and regression suite. Require measurable improvement, confidence intervals and no material deterioration in tool/authorization behavior.
8. Optional preference optimization (DPO/RL) only with qualified pairwise examples/reward specifications; never train a model to falsely claim tasks completed or to bypass policy. Never teach real secrets or private user memory into model weights without specific lawful permission and deletion plan.
9. Produce versioned adapter artifacts, reproducible configs, exact dataset versions/consent ledger, training metrics, eval results, model card and rollback. Export/merge only if license, dtype and adapter-runtime support allow it; keep original immutable checkpoint.
10. Deploy canary to limited user segment through service API, profile p50/p95, tool correctness, feedback and cost; instant rollback. A promoted model must be shown to outperform incumbent under production-relevant conditions, not based on benchmark cherry-picking.

### Concrete acquisition commands (illustrative, run only with licensed access and sufficient disk)

```bash
python -m pip install --upgrade huggingface_hub
hf auth login
# Replace REVISION_SHA with the validated commit ID from the publisher card.
hf download Qwen/Qwen3-8B --revision REVISION_SHA --local-dir ./models/qwen3-8b
# Verify artifact manifests/SHA-256 and run license/dependency checks BEFORE loading.
```

For no-account public artifacts `hf auth login` may be unnecessary; gated access requires valid publisher-approved credentials. Use service tokens stored in a secrets manager, not shell history, for automation. Do NOT try to download 8B/30B/120B models onto an almost-full weak laptop just because the CLI command exists; send this work to funded remote GPU infrastructure. If using `.safetensors`, still audit config, tokenizer, custom code, weights origin and dependency versions.

### Dataset example (format contract; synthetic example only)

```json
{"messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are HEY Code Editor. Propose minimal verifiable patches; never claim tests ran without tool results."},{"role":"user","content":"Change only the login button label from Enter to Sign in."},{"role":"assistant","content":"{\"operations\":[{\"type\":\"edit\",\"target\":\"LoginButton\",\"scope\":\"text_only\",\"value\":\"Sign in\"}],\"verification_needed\":[\"UI renders new label\",\"all other DOM behavior unchanged\"]}"}]}
```

Dataset annotation must include the exact before/after artifact, preservation constraints, failed examples, evaluator label, permission and proof of requested outcome. A model's generated JSON proposal is *not* an authorization or executed side effect; a trusted code/tool runtime executes and verifies.

### Training configuration example (starting point, not a completed training job)

```yaml
run_name: hey-coder-editor-lora-v0
base_model: Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct # candidate; VRAM must be available
base_revision: REQUIRED_PINNED_SHA
training_method: QLoRA
peft:
  method: lora
  rank: 16
  alpha: 32
  dropout: 0.05
quantization: nf4_4bit_if_supported
gradient_checkpointing: true
train_data: s3://private-datasets/hey-code-editor/train-v0.jsonl
validation_data: s3://private-datasets/hey-code-editor/validation-v0.jsonl
test_data: s3://private-datasets/hey-code-editor/blind-test-v0.jsonl
security:
  secrets_in_data: forbidden
  student_data_in_data: forbidden
  cross_tenant_samples: forbidden
  tool_authority_from_model: forbidden
promotion:
  code_patch_preservation_must_improve: true
  no_critical_security_regressions: true
  required_independent_evaluation: true
  rollback_revision_required: true
```

Training scripts must be pinned to actual current Transformers/TRL/PEFT API versions; example configuration is intentionally declarative rather than an unverified copy-paste script. Consider Unsloth only when hardware/kernel compatibility and benchmark justify. For image adapters use Diffusers official task-specific LoRA scripts after license verification. For TTS, training a cloned voice is permitted only with verified speaker consent and correct voice rights; don't use scraping or unconsented impersonation.

### Required data assets and eval harness per specialist

- Model card: model/version/base/license/training lineage/intended uses/known limitations/languages/performance/energy and cost.
- Gold dataset: examples labeled by domain experts, realistic target actions and expected state checks.
- Training split and blind holdout, data rights, ownership, deletion/retraining policy.
- Quality metrics *per role*: e.g. unit-test pass + patch diff size for code, edit preservation for design, OCR field accuracy, teacher factual accuracy, TTS intelligibility, gesture false-activation per hour.
- Hard security gates: tenant leakage, instruction-in-data attack, invalid tool invocation, refusal to invent receipts, malicious content processing, privacy compliance.
- Runtime metrics: accuracy/precision/recall as appropriate, success@k, latency, tokens, GPU memory, throughput, cold start, concurrency, pricing and routing confidence.
- A/B evaluation: compare one model role against shared base+prompt/tool/retrieval baseline; retire role if no measured benefit.

### Provider/hosting separation

`Provider Model API` ≠ `Licensed Open Weights` ≠ `Trained Adapter` ≠ `Hardware Execution Engine` ≠ `HEY Agent`.

A provider may host Qwen/gpt-oss/other permitted foundation and return a model response, but **provider access does not make its weight files available for editing**. HEY can fine-tune the original open weights if license/training rights permit and separately host the result on GPUs later, or use provider-supported fine-tuning of that provider's endpoint. Adaptation is not performed by “editing a prompt and renaming the API model”. Routing/Tools/Memory give a branded experience without false claims of underlying weight ownership.

With $25–50 monthly infrastructure and ~$12 of prepaid AI credits, use low-cost hosted calls and tiny classifiers, no always-on dedicated GPU, no unbounded high-end video generation, and no promise of full-model training. Research/finetuning should run only when separately approved GPU credits/funding exists. Key issuance, usage caps and multi-request spend reservations are part of deployment.

## M03. Model selection / router and self-hosted serving

Model Router input: `task_type, modality, language, risk, complexity, required_context, tool_requirements, budget_remaining, latency_target, privacy, region, user_pref, device_capabilities`. Return `candidate_model_role, provider_endpoint, adapter_revision, max_cost, expected_latency, fallback, confidence, tool schema`. **Risk policy** may restrict endpoints or demand permission; it is not a model's self-granted privilege. Deterministic tasks (arithmetic, authorization, timezone calculations, hashing, storage state) bypass LLM when possible. Routing tiers: deterministic → tiny classifer/embedding → fast language model → specialist LoRA/API → powerful model → bounded Fusion council. Use uncertainty escalation and calibration, not naïve keyword matching. Keep continuity budget reserve bounded.

Remote serving candidate vLLM/SGLang-compatible stack with HTTPS gateway, auth outside raw runtime, rate limiting, streaming, tracing, adapter management and autoscaled GPU if eligible. vLLM `--api-key` must not be trusted as the only internet security boundary because not all paths are protected; use isolated network and a reverse proxy/service authorization. Local optional llama.cpp/Ollama/MLX for quantized compatible models; do not force this onto low-RAM Windows clients. The model registry lists resident/adapted variants and permitted inference locations. Multi-model Fusion can use parallel council, sequential critic/revise, independent scoring, and evidence synthesis with hard caps; final action executor remains canonical.

## M04. Model role inventory — role ≠ mandatory separate costly checkpoint

The following is the intended **specialist-role coverage matrix**. “Recommended realization” is an engineering starting point; choose based on measured results, license and actual device/GPU budget. Every role must have a typed input/output contract and permitted tool set, escalation/fallback strategy, security boundaries, language/format support and blind evaluation set. Do not train fifty role variants automatically; benchmark the shared base first.

| ID | Specialist role | Technical realization | Candidate baseline | Training/adaptation target | Acceptance benchmark |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| M-001 | Orchestrator / HEY One General | general LLM + tool runtime | Qwen3-8B or gpt-oss-20b | multi-step mission traces, precise final state, correct tool selection | task success, evidence fidelity, cost and latency |
