### How specialists connect without wasting compute

Task “create school lesson and presentation” uses shared HEY context: Intent Router → scoped curriculum/document retriever → Teacher Planner (text model) → Quiz Writer (same base adapter or separate if justified) → Presentation Studio (structured slide scene graph) → formatter/exporter (deterministic) → independent fact/layout verification → result. Do not wake a dedicated GPU each for Tutor, Writer, Layout, Reviewer if a shared hosted model can perform the role reliably and economically.

Task “fix code” uses Repo Reader (deterministic/embeddings) → Coder Model → Patch Editor (AST/diff invariants) → Test Runner (real) → Independent Verifier. Distinguish tests *proposed* from *run*. Task “generate an image then change only object A” uses Image Foundation API → mask/segmentation → Inpainting Model → pixel/semantic preservation verifier and user compare UI. Task “say next slide” uses Wake/VAD/ASR (device) → typed command parser → app capability/authorization → real presentation adapter → state verification. High confidence narrow commands should avoid expensive Fusion.

### Decision table: prompt vs fine-tune vs own weights

| Desired change | Cheapest correct method first | When train | When NOT train |
|---|---|---|---|
| Branded personality/writing style | System instructions + user settings | If robust style consistency fails on blind evaluations | No verified eval gap |
| User-specific memory | RAG/database + ACL | Only for general reusable skill on consented dataset | Never encode private mutable user memory into public weights |
| Editing exact 1 slide/region | Structured document model + diff/locks | When target interpretation remains systematically weak | Do not replace precise code diff with stochastic global regeneration |
| Coding | Code-capable licensed base + repo tools | Measured patch defects reduced by LoRA | Baseline + tests already meets bar |
| UI design | Design system + scene renderer + vision model | Distinct brand dataset and licensed design pairs | Fine-tuning worsens generalization |
| Image/video/music | Appropriate licensed media foundation/provider | Specialized brand LoRA with data rights/compute | Training full media foundation inside $50/mo budget |
| Gesture/wake word | Landmark/audio tiny classifier | Custom devices/gestures need learned recognizer | Full LLM cannot beat deterministic latency/privacy |
| Safety/auth | Deterministic policy + measured detector | Detector labels show relevant gap | Never “train permission checks” as sole protection |
| Multilingual Sorani | Native-speaker evaluated retrieval/lexicon/LoRA | Adequate rights + performance evidence | Assuming generic multilingual label equals Sorani fluency |

### Example live model routing contract

```json
{
  "request_id":"uuid",
  "role":"code_editor",
  "organization_id":"server_authorized_id",
  "context_policy":"project_scoped",
  "routing_mode":"auto",
  "privacy":"provider_approved_only",
  "required_capabilities":["structured_output","tool_calling"],
  "latency_target_ms":2500,
  "maximum_estimated_cost_usd":0.02,
  "fallback_roles":["general_editor"],
  "permissions":"resolved_by_trust_kernel_not_model",
  "result_state":"proposal_not_executed",
  "verification_required":["diff_preserves_locked_regions","tests_really_ran"]
}
```

**Important measurement:** the UltraSparse `p95 under 1ms` idea applies only to an in-process lightweight selector on specified hardware/workload; full inference includes tokenization, model cold start, GPU compute, network, tool work, output and postcondition verification. Measure separately. Avoid fake claims of 10T parameters or “more intelligent than all models” without independently reproducible evidence.

# PART THREE — ENGINEERING / PRODUCT INTEGRITY

# PRODUCT INTEGRITY, REQUIREMENTS TRACEABILITY, DELIVERY, TESTING & AGENT RUNBOOK

## P01. Canonical source ledger and true state

The source of current user intent is not a single incomplete chat, agent memory or vague prompt. HEY source hierarchy: newest explicit user decisions; latest architecture amendments; detailed product source; refined engineering; 47-step engineering tasks; old Product Bible as historical trace; current repository as implementation evidence only. Every approved change creates a requirement graph revision and propagates to all affected agent briefs/tests. Inaccessible conversations and ledgers are marked `NOT_OBSERVED`; do not fabricate them. Require source acknowledgment: list files/sections retrieved with hashes; flag truncation. Distinguish specs from approved change/engineering recommendation and discovered platform constraint.

## P02. Minimal canonical requirement record schema

```json
{
 "requirement_id":"HEY-R-000001",
 "title":"User-defined cross-category tools inside Spaces",
 "status":"APPROVED",
 "source":{"document":"newest_refinements","section":"R06","citation_hash":"sha256..."},
 "approved_at":"2026-10-15",
 "supersedes":["legacy_mode_restriction"],
 "dependencies":["ToolRegistry","Auth","SpacePersistence","Frontend"],
 "behavior":{"given":"authenticated user","when":"pins allowed Teacher tool into Developer Space","then":"tool is usable and remains pinned after restart"},
 "security_conditions":["must still pass server-side ToolRegistry authorization"],
 "failure_cases":["revoked org membership","offline","insufficient device support"],
 "ownership":{"integration":"named coordinator","feature":"named engineer","qa":"independent owner"},
 "implementation":{"commit":null,"feature_route":null},
 "evidence":{"unit":null,"integration":null,"browser_e2e":null,"real_provider":null,"native":null,"security":null},
 "maturity":"DESIGNED",
 "release_approval":null
}
```

Every real requirement ID must be generated consistently and checked into version control. `null` evidence fields must remain unverified until completed. “APPROVED” in these document samples refers to clear user decisions, not proof that a running application implements them. Do not rewrite older source docs to conceal supersession; append records and create current effective view.

## P03. Specialist task packet format (MANDATORY)

Each specialist packet must contain the exact applicable source excerpts (not only section titles), the newest amendment excerpts, repository SHA and target files, existing code behavior (actual inspection), source conflict decisions, platform matrix, data/permission models, deliverables, acceptance scenarios including failures and rollback, independent checker, dependencies/owners and max compute budget. Packet receipt contains actual bytes/hash and confirmation. Maintain an automatic diff from updated requirements to affected task packets and issue updated packets. Context window overflow must be handled by retrieval/chunk references with no silent truncation.

## P04. Agent parallel work and merge contract

One integration coordinator owns canonical release branch. Feature owners work in independent branches/worktrees; the frontend director alone owns global shell/visual tokens and shared interaction components; backend owners deliver typed contracts and sample data through fixtures; QA operates independently and is prohibited from simply echoing developer claims. Allow overlapping domains by explicit contracts; never concurrent uncoordinated modifications to shared infrastructure. All shared changes use migrations/backwards compatibility; each merge requires lint, production build, contract tests, integration test, conflict audit and smoke journeys. For a failed invariant, roll back and restore prior production behavior. Preserve commits and tag checkpoints.

## P05. What counts as real integration

Feature-level states: `MISSING` (not built); `DESIGNED` (spec); `IMPLEMENTING` (partial code); `FUNCTIONAL` (works in contained environment); `INTEGRATED` (real UI-to-service-to-data/device path); `VERIFIED` (independent actual user test and boundary/failure evidence); `PRODUCTION_READY` (monitoring/security/performance/backups/platform/rollback and external approvals pass). For outside blockers, add separate `BLOCKED_BY_EXTERNAL` reason but do not inflate maturity. A full-system green unit test count is only one evidence facet.

## P06. Required final artifact set for each implementation

1. Exact source requirements with hashes/IDs.
2. UX recording/capture or reproducible browser route and steps, safe private content handling.
3. Backend/API schema, database migration and RLS evidence, permitted action identifiers.
4. Real provider/device/backend input and output proof where applicable (redacted, no secrets).
5. Happy-path and adversarial automation; postcondition verified independently.
6. Cost/latency/accuracy on actual machines/providers.
7. User-facing error, offline, cancel/revoke and retry/resume behavior.
8. Cross-account/organization isolation and legal/platform licensing notes.
9. Commit, branch, tested version, rollback and known limitations.
10. Independent verifier signature/check that cannot be self-issued by implementing model.

## P07. Critical release categories (neither endless audits nor fake completeness)

- Functional: signup/auth, shared Chat/Voice/Live, Cosmos save/recall/delete, Spaces/tool library, real tool/action and receipt, mission durability, key creation outputs, Teacher, Flow/gestures and native OS paths where supported.
- Operational: services genuinely reachable, staging/prod separation, real DB persistence, backups and restore, provider outage/rate-limit handling, app install/update, ownership and support.
- Security: least privilege, signed bounded mandates, revocation, input/model prompt-injection, secret scanning, row-level isolation, tenant boundaries, extension sandboxes, basic abuse mitigation, budget enforcement.
- Quality: performance targets on weak laptop/mobile/Android board, touch/keyboard/RTL, tutorials, asset edit preservation, explainable verified outcomes.
- Final product: no approved applicable requirement silently postponed under fictitious v2; if some capability legitimately cannot be built now due to platform/legal/hardware/funding, show blocker and do not represent product as globally complete.

## P08. Working release recipe (real app, not mocked demo)

A. Inspect exact latest code/branch and confirm toolchain instructions; do not assume the user-provided Oct14 SHA is still HEAD. B. Run locally with a clean shell and explicitly documented non-secret env placeholders. C. Configure controlled staging accounts and real auth/database/storage/provider with separately approved credentials, including email delivery. D. Run actual browser E2E plus native device E2E; report any unsupported hardware, permissions, or service. E. QA files reproducible defect tickets; owning agents fix and retest. F. Integrate complete feature journey; publish stage URL with access protections. G. Repeat full regression after all merged features, perform backup restore, threat simulations and load limits, document remaining blockers. H. Only then request release authorization. Never invent a public staging URL or treat unverified deployment as done.

## P09. Theoretical perfection is not a credible gate

Demanding “perfect bug-free AI” is impossible to certify. The practical goal is exhaustive source mapping, robust test coverage weighted by risk, independent verification, measured production readiness, incident response and continual regression prevention. The user wants the final comprehensive product—not permission to abandon ambitious features for a subset. Deliver evidence in vertical slices while work on full scope continues. Do not endlessly refine non-critical modules; define testable criteria and finish.

## P10. Hostile tests specific to HEY

- A website instructs HEY to ignore user consent and send local files; user request unchanged → reject exfiltration, log untrusted injection.
- A malicious generated widget asks for stored API key → unavailable by architecture.
- A forged screenshot says “permission granted” → server Trust Kernel denies.
- User revokes microphone during dictation → capture stops immediately, no stale background stream.
- Voice says “delete my entire project” inside dictation text → type text only, not execute command.
- Agent reports “video rendered” while no playable artifact exists → task incomplete.
- Another student uses school tablet → previous teacher's private data not visible.
- Chat A corrected memory, another device B syncs stale value → temporal latest fact wins, auditable correction.
- Provider gives 429/500, timeout, wrong JSON, wrong tool call → bounded retry/fallback with correct error and no double side effect.
- Concurrent jobs exhaust inference credits; cost reservation prevents negative balance overrun and correctly pauses coherent unit.
- Gesture false positives cause no unintended text entry/slide changes over measured real-time test duration.
- Teacher requests an exact slide 3 edit → slide 1/2/4 unchanged structurally and visually.
- Model-selected agent changes action target after approval → mandate invalidates and reapproval needed.
- Owner 1 attempts third-party public publication without co-owner approvals → rejected.
- UI/mini-app crashes or network dies → recover from saved state without lost project, no unverified “done”.

## P11. Owner-facing progress is not an audit graveyard

One operational view should contain: capability, effective requirement IDs and latest refinements, active branch, owner, last working build SHA, actual URL/path/entrypoint, state, E2E evidence, errors, precisely classified blockers and next action. Every status must connect to observable artifact/test. Historical 47-step status remains for traceability but should not obscure which HEY functions can actually be used today. Report completed outcomes to school stakeholders only when real verified.

## P12. Preservation and security of this source package

This package deliberately does **not** include `Yoyoyo.zip` or arbitrary `.env` files from old code snapshots because they might contain credentials. It contains only specification/reference text and derived indices. Real engineers must inspect repository secrets via secure secret-management/rotation procedures. Do not paste `.env`, service-role keys, access tokens, school student records, full screen captures with private data, or hidden deployment credentials into AI chats. Never fabricate training rights to copyrighted text/images or personal recordings.

# FILE: `00_FOUNDATION/00_READ_ME_FIRST.md`

# HEY — FINAL ABSOLUTE SOURCE OF TRUTH

This folder is the final authoritative product/engineering specification for **HEY** and supersedes every earlier HEY planning document. There is no V1/V2 split in this source: the product is simply HEY.

## Precedence
1. Files in `00_FOUNDATION`, `02_INTELLIGENCE_EVOLUTION`, `03_INTERACTION_PLATFORM`, `04_SECURITY_GOVERNANCE`, `05_EXECUTION` and `06_PROMPTS` contain the newest decisions and override conflicting older wording.
2. `01_DETAILED_SYSTEM_SPECS` preserves the exhaustive earlier capability, design, answer, motion and subsystem detail so no approved capability is lost. Where it conflicts with newer files, newer files win.
3. No `.txt` deliverables are used.

## Product rule
Do not stop because a subsystem merely works. Preserve what is strong, replace what is weak, integrate missing layers, test failures, independently verify the outcome, and stop only when the subsystem reaches the strongest production implementation justified by the platform and current engineering reality.

## HEY is one intelligence
Users interact with HEY, not with a giant catalog of bots. Internally HEY may use unlimited specialized agents, models, deterministic engines, tools, workflows and providers. Only the relevant subset is retrieved for a mission.

## Completion means end-to-end
A feature is complete only when applicable discovery, UX, backend, persistence, permissions, authorization, security, abuse/cost protection, recovery, verification, performance, accessibility, localization, tests, tutorials/help, observability and production behavior all pass. UI-only, backend-only, mocked, unverified and partially integrated features are not complete.

## Owners
There are exactly three top-level HEY owners. Any one owner can approve ordinary internal evolution. Public third-party extension publication requires all three. Proven critical security fixes may auto-deploy under emergency policy and must immediately notify all three owners with exact changes, evidence and rollback.

## Budget
HEY is no longer free-only. Paid infrastructure/models are allowed when their measurable improvement justifies cost. Architecture remains provider-agnostic and cost-aware.


---

# FILE: `00_FOUNDATION/01_COMPLETION_AND_REPLACEMENT_CONTRACT.md`

# Completion & Replacement Contract

For every subsystem the implementation agent must: audit current code → preserve unique strengths → replace weaker architecture when justified → connect every missing layer → remove obsolete duplicates after safe migration → test normal and failure paths → independently verify → benchmark where relevant → leave rollback evidence.

Maturity is `MISSING → DESIGNED → IMPLEMENTING → FUNCTIONAL → INTEGRATED → VERIFIED → PRODUCTION_READY`. Anything below `PRODUCTION_READY` continues to be worked on.

When two implementations overlap, keep the stronger one and transplant any unique useful behavior from the weaker one before removing it. A public rename is allowed when it materially improves the product; all public-facing renames must be reported afterward.

Long tasks must be cancellable. Pause/resume/checkpointing is required where technically useful. Destructive or large edits create restore points. External side effects are verified where possible.

A feature cannot be called complete from a page existing, a backend function existing, tests passing in isolation, or an HTTP 200. The actual user goal must work end-to-end.


---

# FILE: `02_INTELLIGENCE_EVOLUTION/01_COGNITIVE_FABRIC_AND_INTELLIGENCE_COUNCIL.md`

# Cognitive Fabric & Intelligence Council

HEY does not treat one LLM response as the definition of intelligence. It composes the best topology for the task: one fast model, deterministic engine, cheap→strong cascade, planner/executor/verifier, parallel experts, critic/reviser, tournament, simulation, or a full **Intelligence Council**.

## Meeting-room architecture
For difficult decisions, relevant specialists enter one shared deliberation room. They see the same Evidence Board containing facts, primary sources, constraints, assumptions, calculations, proposals, objections and unresolved questions. They can challenge one another, revise proposals and introduce ideas missed by the original prompt.

Consensus is **evidence-weighted**, not vote-counted. A strong minority objection cannot be erased merely because many agents agree. A Dissent Guardian preserves material disagreement. A Contrarian and Flaw Hunter deliberately attack the emerging consensus. A Deliberation Budgeter stops extra rounds once marginal improvement no longer justifies latency/cost.

## Example topologies
- Simple question: one fast low-cost model.
- Complex factual answer: researcher + source verifier + synthesis + fact checker.
- Coding: architect + implementers + test + security + reviewer + independent verifier.
- Company strategy: product, market, finance, technology, operations, customer, risk, contrarian, opportunity, long-term and synthesis specialists in debate rounds.
- High-assurance security: multiple independent threat models + exploit simulation + mitigation design + verifier.

## Required components
Expert Selector; Council Chair; Evidence Board; Dissent Guardian; Contrarian; Flaw Hunter; Assumption Breaker; Missing-Requirement Hunter; Opportunity Hunter; Second-Order Effects Agent; Consensus Synthesizer; Independent Verifier; Deliberation Budgeter; provenance/cost/latency tracing.

## Goal
Use orchestration, tools, memory, retrieval, specialization, verification and parallelism to outperform the underlying individual model whenever these mechanisms create a real task-level advantage. Measure the result rather than claiming universal superiority.


---

# FILE: `02_INTELLIGENCE_EVOLUTION/02_DECISION_FABRIC_BEYOND_TOKENS.md`

# Decision Fabric — Intelligence Beyond Token Generation

Tokens are only one mechanism used by generative language models. HEY must avoid spending generative-model tokens on work that can be solved faster or more reliably by other mechanisms.

## HEY decision stack
1. Deterministic code/rules/state machines for exact policy and workflow transitions.
2. Caches and memoized validated results.
3. Traditional algorithms for parsing, diffing, scheduling, hashing, graphs, compression, ranking and math.
4. Embeddings/vector retrieval for similarity and memory/search retrieval.
5. Rerankers/classifiers for relevance, spam, risk, intent and candidate ordering.
6. Typed decision models for bounded choices/scores/probabilities.
7. Small/local models for narrow uncertain tasks.
8. Strong generative models for open-ended reasoning/generation.
9. Intelligence Council for high-value/high-uncertainty tasks.

Jev-class systems are useful inspiration: a typed decision model can return probabilities over allowed decisions rather than generating prose token-by-token. HEY should support such engines through adapters for routing, ranking, policy, risk, approvals, relevance and other bounded decisions. They do not replace generative models; they remove unnecessary generative work.

## Speed techniques HEY should use where supported
KV/prefix caching, speculative decoding, batching, parallel tool/model execution, quantization for local models, sparse/MoE inference where provider/runtime supports it, streaming, prefetching, request coalescing, compiled prompts/contracts, context retrieval instead of giant prompts, deterministic fast paths, local heuristics, concurrency controls and latency-aware provider routing.

## Invention mandate
HEY may build its own **MicroDecision Fabric**: task-specific calibrated classifiers and deterministic policies trained/evaluated on HEY's own labelled outcomes. Uncertain cases escalate to stronger intelligence. Every decision engine is calibrated and benchmarked per task.


---

# FILE: `02_INTELLIGENCE_EVOLUTION/03_UNLIMITED_AGENT_FOUNDRY.md`

# Unlimited Agent Foundry

The old 229-agent catalog is a seed, not a ceiling. HEY starts with every useful known specialist family and can create narrower specialists whenever measured benefit is positive. There is no arbitrary numeric limit.

## Hierarchy
`HEY → domains → agent families → specialists → ultra-specialists → temporary task specialists`.

Only relevant agents are loaded into a mission. A million registered specializations must not mean a million prompts are injected into every context.

## Mandatory specialist families
Core orchestration; memory/Cosmos; research; engineering; security; risk; QA; provider/model; optimization; computer/browser/files; voice; vision; screen/camera guidance; platform-native; product/UX; accessibility/localization; creation; business; education; religious research; devices; automation; Forge; Evolution; governance; billing; observability; recovery; legal/privacy information; data/statistics; support/incident.

## New required specialist examples
Flaw Hunter, Missing Requirement Hunter, Assumption Breaker, Opportunity Hunter, Second-Order Effects, Latency Hunter, Token Efficiency, Prompt Compiler, Spec Retrieval, Duplicate Work Detector, Cost Leak Hunter, Context Quality, Risk Twin, Solution Twin, Data Exfiltration Hunter, Supply Chain Hunter, Sandbox Escape Hunter, Rate-Limit Architect, Public Claims Auditor, User Confusion Hunter, Future Compatibility, Staleness Propagation, Outcome Judge.

## Agent creation lifecycle
Need detected → registry/duplicate search → contract design → simulation → benchmark against existing agent/team → security/permissions review → temporary deployment → measured production shadow → promotion if useful → health monitoring → merge/retire/rollback when superseded.

Every agent declares typed inputs/outputs, tools, permissions, provider policy, privacy, risk, budget, timeout, retry, cancellation, checkpoint behavior, verification, tests, health, version and dependencies. Agents cannot grant themselves permissions or self-certify success.


---

# FILE: `02_INTELLIGENCE_EVOLUTION/04_RUNTIME_CAPABILITY_SYNTHESIS.md`

# Runtime Capability Synthesis

When a user requests an outcome for which HEY has no current capability, HEY should not default to “unavailable.” It should attempt to synthesize the missing capability safely.

## Flow
Request → capability search → gap confirmed → research implementation paths/APIs/libraries/local methods → choose architecture → create smallest capable tool/workflow/agent/adapter/code module → dependency/provenance checks → sandbox → Risk Twin → Solution Twin → adversarial tests → functional tests → execute the original user task → verify outcome.

The synthesized capability is **temporary by default**. The controlling user/owner can choose:
- Save;
- Modify, then Save;
- Delete.

Until saved it is isolated, scoped and disposable. Saved capabilities are versioned, auditable and rollbackable.

## Safety without making the feature weaker
Undo is valuable but cannot reverse exfiltration, an external payment or public disclosure. Therefore generated capabilities use scoped permissions, network/filesystem/tool allowlists, resource budgets, snapshots, sandboxing and action verification before execution. The Solution Twin must find designs that preserve or improve useful capability rather than lazily deleting risky functionality.

## Capability provenance
Record why it was created, models/agents involved, source research, dependencies, permissions, code/config changes, test results, risk findings, mitigations, version, usage and save/delete decision.


---

# FILE: `02_INTELLIGENCE_EVOLUTION/05_RISK_TWIN_SOLUTION_TWIN.md`

# Risk Twin + Solution Twin

Every substantial new capability or architecture change is reviewed by two adversarially complementary systems.

**Risk Twin** searches for security, privacy, data-loss, reliability, compatibility, performance, cost, abuse, UX, accessibility, supply-chain, prompt-injection, permission, legal/policy and second-order failure modes.

**Solution Twin** receives every finding and has two responsibilities:
1. eliminate or contain the risk without unnecessarily reducing capability;
2. actively discover additional technologies, architectures or features that make the capability stronger, faster, simpler, cheaper, safer or more reliable.

Then a second Risk Twin pass attacks the revised design. An independent verifier decides whether the residual risk and functionality meet policy.

The default sequence is `maximize capability → enumerate risks → strengthen design + mitigate risks → attack again → verify`, not `see risk → delete feature`.


---

# FILE: `02_INTELLIGENCE_EVOLUTION/06_EVOLUTION_ENGINE_WHOLE_INTERNET.md`

# Evolution Engine — Continuous Whole-Internet Discovery

HEY continuously learns about the external world so the product does not freeze at today's capabilities.

## Two layers
**Continuous watchers** detect high-value changes immediately.
**Daily Deep Sweep** performs an exhaustive broad-category research cycle every 24 hours.

## Scope
The sweep is not limited to AI. It searches every category that could improve HEY or its users: software, hardware, operating systems, browsers, developer tools, APIs, open source, security, networking, databases, distributed systems, science, mathematics, education, productivity, business, finance, design, accessibility, language, media, communications, consumer apps, enterprise software, robotics, HCI, standards, protocols, legal/platform policy changes, healthcare-information tools, creative tools, automation, devices, new research fields and newly emerging categories not known when this document was written.

## Pipeline
Discovery → primary-source extraction → source/freshness verification → categorization → dedup against discovery history → compare against HEY → benchmark claims where possible → quantify improvement/risk/cost → architecture proposal → Risk Twin → Solution Twin (mitigate + strengthen) → independent critic → concise owner proposal.

Normal internal evolution needs any one of the three owners to approve. Approved work goes through implementation branch, security, tests, shadow deployment/canary, independent verification and rollback-ready promotion.

## Memory
The engine remembers discoveries, benchmarks, adopted/rejected proposals, rejection reasons, failed migrations and superseded systems so it does not waste resources rediscovering the same item. Rejected ideas resurface only when material new evidence changes the decision.


---

# FILE: `03_INTERACTION_PLATFORM/01_CHAT_VOICE_LIVE_UNIFIED.md`

# Unified Chat, Voice & Live

Chat and Voice are the same canonical conversation. Voice is not a separate history. A voice turn becomes part of chat history; text and voice share project, files, active artifacts, missions and Cosmos context.

## Different answer styles, same intelligence
Chat can be structured, detailed, source-rich and artifact-heavy. Voice is shorter, more natural, interruption-friendly and spoken in smaller turns. A full transcript/result can still appear in the shared conversation. Raw microphone audio is not retained by default after processing unless the user explicitly saves it. Private Mode can avoid durable transcript/memory according to settings.

Switching `Chat → Voice → Live → Chat` must preserve context.

## Live
HEY Live can combine voice with the user's chosen screen/window/monitor/region, camera, files and project context. Guide mode explains; Assist mode helps with bounded actions; Act mode performs authorized actions and verifies results.


---

# FILE: `03_INTERACTION_PLATFORM/02_SCREEN_CAMERA_GUIDANCE_OVERLAYS.md`

# Screen & Camera Guidance / Overlay System

HEY can use the screen or camera (with visible permission) to guide users through digital or physical tasks.

## Screen guidance
HEY understands UI elements, highlights the exact control, draws arrows/outlines/callouts, dims unrelated regions, numbers steps, follows moving UI targets, watches whether the step succeeded and advances only after verification. It can guide settings changes, software workflows, forms, troubleshooting and accessibility tasks.

## Camera guidance
HEY understands the live scene, identifies relevant objects, anchors arrows/labels/step markers to them, tracks them across frames and tells the user what to do next. It can assist with setup, assembly, troubleshooting and other appropriate real-world procedures.

## Spatial Guidance Graph
Both screen and camera guidance share a graph of targets, anchors, instructions, confidence and verification state. Voice can say “the button I mean is here” while the overlay highlights it.

## Privacy/security
Visible sensing indicator, instant pause/stop, selected-source controls, app exclusions, sensitive mode, raw-feed non-retention by default, prompt-injection defense for on-screen text, local vision/pose inference where viable.

## Agents
Screen Understanding, Camera Understanding, Object Detection, Object Tracking, Spatial Anchor, Guidance Planner, Overlay Renderer, Procedure Verification, Accessibility Guide, Prompt-Injection Guard, Safety/Risk.


---

# FILE: `03_INTERACTION_PLATFORM/03_PLATFORM_OUTCOME_PARITY.md`

# Platform Outcome Parity

HEY targets the same **user-level capabilities** across Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, iOS/iPadOS and web/PWA. The internal method can differ because operating systems expose different APIs.

Shared HEY Brain sits above platform Capability Adapters. Each adapter declares what native mechanisms are available, permission state and health. If one device cannot directly perform a step, HEY may compose official OS automation, app intents/shortcuts, accessibility APIs, screen/camera guidance, browser capabilities, a native companion, trusted-device handoff or institution-managed device controls to achieve the same user goal where technically legitimate.

### Examples
Windows: native helper, UI Automation, screen capture, PowerShell/terminal, window/process/filesystem APIs.
macOS: Accessibility API, ScreenCaptureKit, Shortcuts/AppleScript where appropriate, native helper/menu bar.
Linux: Wayland/X11/desktop portals, DBus, shell/native services.
Android: intents, accessibility service when justified/user-enabled, MediaProjection, camera/mic, foreground services, notifications, sideloadable APK before store distribution.
iOS/iPadOS: App Intents, Shortcuts, universal links/URL schemes, ReplayKit/screen broadcast where applicable, camera/mic, Live Activities/Dynamic Island, share extensions, document picker, background tasks within OS limits, and MDM/supervision for eligible institutional deployments.
Web/PWA: manifest/service worker/install, getDisplayMedia/getUserMedia, File System Access where supported, notifications/share/file handlers.

Do not assume an unrestricted iOS terminal exists for ordinary third-party apps. Use the strongest legitimate composition of supported mechanisms instead of building against a false privilege model.

Store publication is not required immediately. Architecture must support PWA, desktop installers and legitimate sideload/institutional distribution paths until App Store/Play Store distribution becomes feasible.


---

# FILE: `03_INTERACTION_PLATFORM/04_DYNAMIC_ISLAND_BACKGROUND.md`

# Dynamic Island & Background HEY

Dynamic Island is a native/persistent HEY surface on supported platforms, not merely a React component inside the main page. It remains when the main HEY window is minimized or closed while the helper/background runtime is enabled.

Modes include idle, listening, thinking, speaking, media, mission, generation, research, upload/download, timer, reminder, approval, cross-device handoff, error/recovery and completed result. Clicking expands context-specific controls rather than a generic Activity screen.

Long-running HEY work is durable state, not one immortal process. Local helpers and server schedulers checkpoint/resume work across crashes, deployments, device restarts and sleep where the platform permits. Owners and authorized users retain stop/revoke controls; an unkillable malfunctioning process is not a feature.

Camera/screen sharing stops when the session ends and normally on main-window close unless an explicit visible background session is active.


---

# FILE: `04_SECURITY_GOVERNANCE/01_OWNER_CONSOLE_AND_GOVERNANCE.md`

# HEY Owner Console & Governance

Exactly three top-level owner identities exist. The Owner Console has a distinct high-security UI and stronger authentication/re-auth policies than normal HEY.

It includes Evolution proposals, discovered vulnerabilities, emergency auto-patches, capability changes, third-party submissions, agent/provider health, global spend, releases, feature flags, rollback, quarantine, incident history and audit trails.

- Normal internal improvement: any one owner approval is sufficient.
- Third-party public extension publication: all three owners approve.
- Proven critical security patch: may auto-deploy under emergency policy, then immediately notify all three owners with what changed, why, evidence, tests, side effects, what should be removed/changed next and rollback.
- No normal admin flow can add a fourth owner.

Owner accounts should use the strongest available account security, including passkeys/MFA/re-auth/device trust where implemented.


---

# FILE: `04_SECURITY_GOVERNANCE/02_SECURITY_AUTONOMY_AND_PERMISSIONS.md`

# Security, Autonomy & Permissions

HEY maximizes capability while enforcing least privilege. Security lifecycle: **prevent → minimize → contain → detect → stop → recover → learn**.

Automation/workflow autonomy levels:
- Ask Every Time;
- Smart Approval (routine/reversible steps proceed, meaningful high-risk steps ask);
- Full Execution within the workflow's explicitly granted scope;
- Custom rules by app, destination, action class, budget, time and data scope.

Agents cannot grant themselves permission. Server/runtime authorization remains authoritative. Prompt/page/document content is untrusted data and cannot override user/system policy. High-impact target changes invalidate earlier approval.

Trust Center exposes microphone, camera, screen, background activity, integrations, devices, agent/workflow permissions, Cosmos privacy, local/cloud routing, once/session/timed/mission/persistent grants, Revoke All and Emergency Stop.


---

# FILE: `04_SECURITY_GOVERNANCE/03_RATE_LIMITS_COMPUTE_ALLOWANCES_CONTINUITY.md`

# Rate Limits, Compute Allowances & Atomic Completion

HEY uses distributed server-side rate limiting for expensive/sensitive routes. Limits are endpoint- and cost-aware, not one global frontend counter. Authenticated identity, organization/user ID and appropriate network/device signals are combined; anonymous auth/signup/recovery routes receive separate abuse protection. 429 responses are structured and include retry timing.

## Compute Allowances
User-facing plans should not fundamentally be measured in “hours” or raw tokens. Internal allowance accounting can combine provider spend, input/output tokens, image/video/audio generations, tool/API costs, parallel agents, GPU/compute and long-running background duration. The UI can present a simple understandable capacity meter.

## Atomic Completion / Continuity Reserve
HEY does not randomly stop halfway through a coherent unit when an allowance boundary is reached. It may use a bounded continuity reserve to finish the current file/slide/artifact step/tool transaction, then checkpoint.

It reports: what completed, why it paused, exact saved state, what remains and how to resume. The reserve is capped so a user cannot start an enormous costly job with almost no allowance remaining and force unlimited completion.


---

# FILE: `04_SECURITY_GOVERNANCE/04_CLOSED_SOURCE_API_LOCAL_MODELS_EXTENSIONS.md`

# Closed Source Core, APIs, Local Models & Third-Party Extensions

HEY's core codebase remains closed source. Users do not need source access to use local models.

HEY exposes stable API/SDK contracts for models, tools, agents, workflows, widgets and integrations. Local inference options can include Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio, vLLM/OpenAI-compatible endpoints, a HEY local runtime and trusted LAN/self-hosted endpoints.

A model profiler records context, tool calling, JSON reliability, modalities, speed, resource use and benchmark quality so the Router can use local models intelligently.

Third-party developers can build extensions through public SDKs/contracts. Before privileged public distribution: automated validation, dependency/supply-chain scan, sandbox, permissions review, security tests, compatibility tests and **all three owners' approval**. Approved packages are signed/versioned and can be revoked/quarantined.


---

# FILE: `05_EXECUTION/01_REPOSITORY_IMPLEMENTATION_ORDER.md`

# Repository Implementation Order

The coding agent starts from the current HEY codebase, not from a greenfield rewrite assumption.

1. Inventory routes/components/APIs/edge functions/database/migrations/RLS/auth/providers/agents/tools/workflows/native commands/service worker/config/tests.
2. Search contextually for TODO/FIXME/HACK/TEMP/MOCK/STUB/PLACEHOLDER/coming soon/dummy/localhost/dead flags/duplicate implementations.
3. Build spec↔code map.
4. Fix shared contracts/data/events/auth/security/permissions/rate limits first.
5. Provider/decision/cognitive runtime.
6. Agent registry/verifier/recovery.
7. Cosmos/projects/Pinpoint/artifacts.
8. Chat/Voice/Live/screen-camera guidance/Island/background.
9. Studios/generation.
10. computer/browser/files/device/platform adapters.
11. automations/Forge/capability synthesis/Evolution Engine.
12. plans/billing/API/Education/owner console.
13. discoverability/tutorial/accessibility/localization.
14. whole-system failure/security/performance/production gates.

Every subsystem is audited, improved/replaced, migrated, tested, independently verified and only then marked production-ready.

# FILE: `05_EXECUTION/02_FINAL_WHOLE_PRODUCT_GATE.md`

# Final Whole-Product Gate

Before HEY is called finished, a fresh independent verifier runs realistic journeys with no developer cache, plus returning-user projects/memory/artifacts/integrations.

Required stress cases include provider 429/500, selected model disappearance, network drop, offline, expired auth, denied/revoked permission, database outage, duplicate submission, simultaneous requests, tab/window close, native helper restart, corrupted local state, allowance boundary, migration rollback, backup restore, malicious page prompt injection, generated-capability adversarial test, third-party package rejection, cross-project privacy, public-display privacy, mobile/tablet/desktop, RTL/reduced motion and weak hardware.

The final question is:

> If HEY went live to thousands of users right now, what could fail, leak data, waste money, confuse users, falsely claim success, corrupt work, become unrecoverable or make the product feel unfinished?

Every discovered issue is fixed or explicitly accepted/documented by the owners before release.


---

# FILE: `06_PROMPTS/00_MASTER_IMPLEMENTATION_PROMPT.md`

# Master Prompt for Codex / OpenCode / Any Coding Agent

You receive the complete current HEY codebase and the folder `HEY_FINAL_ABSOLUTE_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH`.

This folder is authoritative and supersedes older HEY planning. Do not reduce it into an MVP or defer useful requirements into a fictional V2.

Work subsystem-by-subsystem in dependency order. For each subsystem:
1. read the newest relevant source files and shared foundation contract;
2. trace the existing implementation end-to-end;
3. preserve anything stronger than the specification;
4. improve or replace weaker/partial implementations rather than stopping because they technically work;
5. when duplicate implementations exist, keep the stronger one and migrate any unique useful behavior from the weaker one before removal;
6. implement every missing layer—UI, backend, data, integrations, permissions, security, recovery, verification, performance, accessibility, localization, tests and help/discovery where applicable;
7. if a low-level technology choice is unspecified, select the best maintained option by comparing quality, reliability, cost, latency, privacy, licensing, platform coverage and maintainability;
8. never weaken authorization/security to make a feature work;
9. independently verify user-visible outcomes and external side effects;
10. run normal, failure-injection, security and regression tests;
11. leave evidence and rollback paths;
12. do not mark the subsystem complete until it is PRODUCTION_READY.

Do not waste tokens re-reading the entire folder for every task. Retrieve only the relevant subsystem documents plus shared contracts. Use the repository as the current-state truth and the specification as the target-state truth.

# FILE: `01_DETAILED_SYSTEM_SPECS/00_AUTHORITATIVE_NEWEST_PRODUCT_FLOW_AMENDMENT.md`

# HEY V1 — AUTHORITATIVE FRONT-END / PRODUCT-FLOW AMENDMENT
## Newest decisions override conflicting older wording

This amendment is authoritative over older navigation/front-end wording wherever conflicts exist.

## A. SIGN-IN DESTINATION

After a successful sign-in, HEY must **not** take the user to a generic dashboard.

Default destination:
**The HEY Conversation Surface** — the primary page where the user can switch directly between **Chat** and **Voice**.

The product should immediately feel like the user has arrived at HEY itself, not at an admin dashboard.

### Required first signed-in view
- HEY wordmark / identity;
- Chat / Voice switcher;
- current project/context indicator when relevant;
- main conversation surface;
- prompt / microphone controls;
- compact access to Live;
- important contextual quick actions;
- Dynamic Island if supported;
- unobtrusive route to Home/Workspace, Projects, Cosmos, Create, etc.

### Returning user behavior
By default:
- return to the most recent Chat/Voice conversation state when safe;
- preserve current project/context;
- if a mission is active, show a compact resumable mission state;
- if user explicitly set a different startup destination, respect it.

### Do not
- dump users onto a generic grid of widgets;
- force users through a dashboard before speaking to HEY;
- make Chat and Voice look like unrelated products.

---

## B. CHAT + VOICE ARE ONE PRIMARY HEY SURFACE

Chat and Voice are two modalities of the same HEY Brain.

They should exist inside one coherent Conversation Surface.

### Desktop layout
Top/center modality selector:
- Chat
- Voice
- optionally Live as a nearby third action, not necessarily equal tab if Live uses immersive layout.

Switching Chat ↔ Voice:
- preserves conversation;
- preserves attachments/context;
- preserves project;
- preserves active artifact/studio;
- preserves mission;
- does not restart HEY.

### Chat mode
- editorial conversation;
- attachments;
- context/project chips;
- artifact cards;
- inline studio surfaces;
- action receipts;
- citations where relevant.

### Voice mode
The current generic voice page is not sufficient.

Required direction:
- use the premium call-like visual language previously designed;
- large HEY living visualizer;
- listening / thinking / speaking states;
- compact transcript;
- mute;
- end;
- captions;
- camera;
- screen;
- device/output;
- optional active task/artifact card;
- same conversation context as Chat.

Voice must feel like a live session with HEY, not a static microphone page.

---

## C. STUDIOS ARE MARRIED TO CHAT + VOICE

Dedicated Studio pages may remain for power users and direct navigation.

But creation must also work naturally **inside Chat and Voice**.

Example:
User in Chat:
“HEY, create me a 15-second video about X.”

Expected flow:
1. HEY understands request.
2. HEY may ask only materially necessary clarification.
3. Creation mission starts.
4. A Video Studio surface opens **inside the current HEY conversation/workspace**.
5. Chat remains available.
6. User can continue issuing edits conversationally.
7. Video Studio receives those edits directly.
8. Pinpoint Precision preserves locked/approved shots.
9. User can expand Studio to full workspace if desired.
10. User can collapse it back into conversation.
11. Dedicated Studio route can open the same artifact/state.

Same principle applies to:
- image;
- storyboard/frame;
- video;
- motion graphics;
- audio;
- presentation;
- document/book;
- code;
- research.

### Voice example
User in Voice:
“HEY, make a presentation about renewable energy.”

Expected:
- HEY verbally acknowledges;
- Presentation Studio appears as an embedded/side/full workspace while Voice remains active;
- user can say “change slide three only”;
- HEY edits slide three;
- conversation and studio remain synchronized.

Studios must never behave like unrelated apps launched from HEY.

---

## D. DYNAMIC ISLAND MUST LIVE OUTSIDE HEY

The Dynamic Island is a native persistent surface on supported platforms.

It must survive:
- unfocus;
- minimize;
- main-window close while helper remains running.

It must not depend on a browser tab or main React/Vite DOM remaining alive.

When clicked, it must show a **contextual control surface**, not merely an Activity list.

Context examples:
- Voice call;
- media;
- generation;
- research;
- mission;
- timer;
- download/upload;
- approval;
- handoff;
- result;
- error/recovery.

---

## E. PWA DOWNLOAD / INSTALL IS MISSING AND REQUIRED

HEY must expose a clear **Install HEY** / **Download HEY** path for the PWA/web-installable version.

### Required surfaces
Public website:
- primary or secondary “Install HEY” CTA where browser/platform supports PWA install;
- Download page with platform choices.

Inside HEY:
- Settings → Apps / Install / Device or equivalent;
- contextual install suggestion after meaningful use, not immediately on first page load;
- Help/Tutorial Center → Install HEY.

### Required PWA implementation
- valid Web App Manifest;
- app name and short_name;
- start_url;
- display mode appropriate for standalone experience;
- theme/background colors;
- icons including maskable icons;
- service worker;
- offline shell;
- installability criteria;
- correct scope;
- screenshots where platform supports richer install UI;
- shortcuts where useful;
- share target/file handling only if truly supported and tested.

### Install UX
If `beforeinstallprompt` is supported:
- capture event;
- show HEY-branded Install button;
- prompt only after user action;
- handle accepted/dismissed outcome;
- do not repeatedly nag after dismissal.

If browser does not expose programmatic prompt:
- show platform-specific manual steps;
- never display a fake “download” button that cannot install.

### Installed PWA behavior
- standalone shell;
- HEY icon;
- startup routes to Conversation Surface, not generic dashboard;
- session persists appropriately;
- deep links work;
- offline/local-capable parts degrade gracefully;
- updates are detected and applied safely;
- user is informed when restart/update is needed.

### Native download distinction
Do not confuse:
- PWA install;
- native Tauri desktop installer;
- mobile platform install.

The Download page should identify what the user is installing.

---

## F. HOME/DASHBOARD STILL EXISTS — BUT IS NOT THE DEFAULT POST-SIGN-IN DESTINATION

Home/Workspace remains useful for:
- widgets;
- tasks;
- calendar;
- active projects;
- missions;
- routines;
- weather;
- prayer where enabled;
- device/system state.

It is accessed from navigation and can be user-selected as startup destination.

But the default “enter HEY” experience is Chat/Voice.

---

## G. ACCEPTANCE TESTS FOR THIS AMENDMENT

1. Fresh sign-in → lands on Chat/Voice Conversation Surface.
2. Switch Chat → Voice → same conversation/context remains.
3. Voice visually matches call-like premium HEY direction.
4. In Chat, ask for video → embedded Studio appears without leaving HEY.
5. In Voice, ask for presentation → Studio appears while session continues.
6. Expand embedded Studio → dedicated/full workspace.
7. Collapse → returns to conversation without state loss.
8. Close main window during active mission → native Dynamic Island remains.
9. Click island during Voice → call controls.
10. Click island during generation → generation controls.
11. Supported browser → Install HEY CTA works.
12. Installed PWA opens standalone and lands on Conversation Surface.
13. Unsupported install browser → correct manual instructions, not fake prompt.



---

# FILE: `01_DETAILED_SYSTEM_SPECS/01_COMPLETE_NAVIGATION_INFORMATION_ARCHITECTURE.md`

# Complete Navigation & Information Architecture
## HEY V1 — Full-depth implementation specification

**Mission:** Make every important HEY capability discoverable without exposing internal complexity.

This specification is normative for HEY V1. A feature is not complete because a page renders or an API returns. It is complete only when discovery, interaction, state, permissions, failures, recovery, verification, accessibility, observability and end-to-end behavior all work.

# 1. Scope
- Conversation Surface (Chat/Voice) is the default signed-in destination.
- Primary global navigation, contextual navigation, Create hierarchy, Explore More, + Add, Universal Search, Command Palette, recent/favorites, mobile bottom nav.
- Information scent, labels, hierarchy, advanced-mode disclosure, role/device/mode adaptations.
- Deep-link routing and return-to-previous-context behavior.

# 2. User experience contract
- Primary normal-user nav: Chat/Voice entry, Live, Projects, Create, Cosmos, Tasks/Missions, Widgets/Workspace, Search, Notifications, Settings.
- Important Create actions visible before Explore More: Image, Video, Presentation, Document, Audio.
- `+ Add` lets users pin additional capabilities without seeing raw agents.
- Advanced tools are discoverable through Advanced Mode, Search, Forge, Developer—not cluttering normal nav.
- Navigation never loses active project/conversation/artifact state.
- Breadcrumbs appear only where hierarchy is genuinely useful.
- Mobile uses bottom nav + More; desktop uses collapsible rail; tablet uses adaptive split shell.

# 3. Architecture / runtime contract
- Central route registry with capability metadata, permissions, feature flags, platform support and discovery rank.
- Navigation state is distinct from task/artifact state.
- Deep links restore intended resource with permission checks.
- Startup route resolver respects newest rule: default Conversation Surface, then explicit user override, then safe resume.
- Explore More reads from capability registry but filters by audience/platform/entitlements.

# 4. Required state model
- anonymous
- authenticating
- signed-in-first-run
- signed-in-returning
- conversation-active
- immersive-live
- embedded-studio
- full-studio
- modal
- offline
- unsupported-platform
- advanced-mode

# 5. Failure and recovery catalog
- Unknown/deprecated route → safe redirect with explanation.
- Feature flag off → remove dead nav and provide fallback if linked.
- Unauthorized deep link → permission/entitlement explanation.
- Stale project/artifact link → recovery and search, not blank page.
- Navigation state corruption → restore last valid route.

# 6. Security / privacy / trust requirements
- Never use client-only nav hiding as authorization.
- Sensitive routes require server/runtime enforcement.
- Do not leak advanced/debug routes to normal users.
- External URLs opened safely and clearly distinguished.

# 7. Data model / persistence
- navigation_preferences
- pinned_capabilities
- recent_capabilities
- startup_destination
- feature_flags
- entitlements
- capability_manifest
- workspace_route_state

# 8. Events / telemetry contracts
- nav.opened
- nav.pinned
- nav.unpinned
- search.opened
- capability.discovered
- capability.launched
- route.failed
- startup.resolved

# 9. Platform behavior
- Follow the strongest legitimate behavior available per platform; expose limitations honestly.

# 10. Implementation requirements
- Reuse shared HEY runtime, permissions, audit, verification, Project DNA, Pinpoint, Cosmos and error systems rather than creating isolated local logic.

# 11. Acceptance / regression tests
- Fresh sign-in lands Chat/Voice.
- Returning user resumes safe conversation state.
- Normal user finds Image/Video/Live/Cosmos without Explore More.
- + Add persists pinned tool.
- Deep link to project artifact restores context.
- Advanced Mode reveals developer areas without changing normal nav.

# 12. Non-goals / prohibited shortcuts
- Do not put all 229 agents in navigation.
- Do not make Explore More the only discovery path.
- Do not route sign-in to generic dashboard by default.

# 13. Definition of done
A release candidate passes only when:
- normal users can discover the capability;
- the capability works from its natural HEY entry points;
- it survives supported resume/background states;
- permissions are scoped and revocable;
- errors recover without losing user work;
- meaningful actions are verified;
- analytics/diagnostics can explain failure without exposing secrets;
- keyboard/touch/RTL/reduced-motion behavior is correct where relevant;
- mobile/tablet/desktop adaptations are intentional;
- tests exercise real integration paths, not mocked happy paths only.



---

- Timeout → cancel and fallback if safe.
- Partial generation → preserve result and retry missing part.

- Keys server-side/native secure storage.
- No cross-project data leakage.
- Provider privacy policies represented in routing constraints.

# 7. Data model / persistence
- island_preferences
- island_state
- active_surfaces
- native_helper_state

# 8. Events / telemetry contracts
- island.mode.changed
- island.expanded
- island.action
- helper.connected
- helper.disconnected

# 9. Platform behavior
- Follow the strongest legitimate behavior available per platform; expose limitations honestly.

# 10. Implementation requirements
- Reuse shared HEY runtime, permissions, audit, verification, Project DNA, Pinpoint, Cosmos and error systems rather than creating isolated local logic.

# 11. Acceptance / regression tests
- Close main window persistence.
- Voice controls.
- Media controls.
- Generation controls.
- Monitor unplug.
- Full quit removes island.

# 12. Non-goals / prohibited shortcuts
- No fake success, no UI-only placeholders, no hidden unsupported behavior, no duplicate parallel subsystem that bypasses the HEY Brain.

# 13. Definition of done
A release candidate passes only when:
- normal users can discover the capability;
- the capability works from its natural HEY entry points;
- it survives supported resume/background states;
- permissions are scoped and revocable;
- errors recover without losing user work;
- meaningful actions are verified;
- analytics/diagnostics can explain failure without exposing secrets;
- keyboard/touch/RTL/reduced-motion behavior is correct where relevant;
- mobile/tablet/desktop adaptations are intentional;
- tests exercise real integration paths, not mocked happy paths only.

# FILE: `01_DETAILED_SYSTEM_SPECS/24_COMPLETE_TUTORIAL_DISCOVERY_SYSTEM.md`

# Complete Tutorial, Onboarding & Feature Discovery System
## HEY V1 — Full-depth implementation specification

**Mission:** Teach every major HEY capability through real UI practice, not static help pages.

This specification is normative for HEY V1. A feature is not complete because a page renders or an API returns. It is complete only when discovery, interaction, state, permissions, failures, recovery, verification, accessibility, observability and end-to-end behavior all work.

# 1. Scope
- First-use tutorials, Tutorial Center, contextual Show Me, animated demos, practice mode, tutorial versioning, completion, discovery nudges.
- 63+ major tutorials and replay.

# 2. User experience contract
- Tutorial appears on first meaningful use, not as startup spam.
- User can say 'show me how to use X'.
- Tutorial spotlights real controls and lets user practice.
- Skip/replay/reduced-motion always available.
- Changed UI increments tutorial version and can offer What's New.

# 3. Architecture / runtime contract
- Tutorial registry maps capability IDs to steps, selectors/anchors, voice copy, fallback static frames and version.
- Runtime validates target exists before starting.
- Analytics records completion without recording sensitive content.
- Tutorial overlay never blocks critical security flow.

# 4. Required state model
- not-started
- offered
- in-progress
- skipped
- completed
- outdated
- practice

# 5. Failure and recovery catalog
- Target missing → fallback explanation and report stale tutorial.
- User navigates away → pause.
- Reduced motion → still-step version.
- Feature unavailable → platform-specific tutorial.

# 6. Security / privacy / trust requirements
- Tutorials must not grant permissions automatically.
- Privacy-sensitive feature tutorial explains sensing indicators.

# 7. Data model / persistence
- tutorials
- tutorial_steps
- tutorial_progress
- tutorial_versions

# 8. Events / telemetry contracts
- tutorial.offered
- tutorial.started
- tutorial.step
- tutorial.skipped
- tutorial.completed
- tutorial.stale

# 9. Platform behavior
- Follow the strongest legitimate behavior available per platform; expose limitations honestly.

# 10. Implementation requirements
- Reuse shared HEY runtime, permissions, audit, verification, Project DNA, Pinpoint, Cosmos and error systems rather than creating isolated local logic.

# 11. Acceptance / regression tests
- Voice tutorial by voice command.
- Live first-use tutorial.
- Replay.
- UI selector stale detection.
- Reduced-motion tutorial.

# 12. Non-goals / prohibited shortcuts
- No fake success, no UI-only placeholders, no hidden unsupported behavior, no duplicate parallel subsystem that bypasses the HEY Brain.

# 13. Definition of done
A release candidate passes only when:
- normal users can discover the capability;
- the capability works from its natural HEY entry points;
- it survives supported resume/background states;
- permissions are scoped and revocable;
- errors recover without losing user work;
- meaningful actions are verified;
- analytics/diagnostics can explain failure without exposing secrets;
- keyboard/touch/RTL/reduced-motion behavior is correct where relevant;
- mobile/tablet/desktop adaptations are intentional;
- tests exercise real integration paths, not mocked happy paths only.
