# 42. IMPLEMENTATION ORDER / DEPENDENCY GRAPH

This is an engineering dependency order, **not a feature deferral roadmap**. All belong to HEY V1.

1. Audit current repository and produce truth table of existing/partial/missing functionality.
2. Stabilize Brain, message/event routing, provider routing and context.
3. Stabilize permission/security/audit primitives.
4. Stabilize mission/task/workflow/execution/verification/recovery.
5. Stabilize agent registry/router/health/team orchestration.
6. Forge/Skills/Commands and validation.
7. Persistent Cosmos + project memory + provenance + contradiction handling.
8. Artifact/version/change-set/Pinpoint Precision architecture.
9. Provider adapters for text/image/video/audio/presentation/document generation.
10. Project DNA + consistency QA.
11. Voice/wake word + unified chat.
12. HEY Live screen/camera pipeline.
13. Computer/browser/file control.
14. Background native helper + Dynamic Island/global shortcuts.
15. Workspace/widgets/semantic drag-drop.
16. Gesture engine + Gesture Studio.
17. Device Fabric/cross-device.
18. Proactive system + notifications/routines.
19. Modes and specialized workspaces.
20. Accounts/plans/billing/usage.
21. Trust Center/privacy/data portability.
22. Offline/local routing and performance adaptation.
23. Developer platform.
24. Complete tutorial/onboarding pass.
25. Full accessibility/localization.
26. End-to-end tests, benchmarks, security audit, performance, release gate.

At each stage, preserve working features and keep the app runnable.

# 43. OPENCODE WORKING RULES

When OpenCode implements this specification:

- inspect before edit;
- do not assume filenames from this document exactly match current repo;
- locate existing equivalent subsystem first;
- avoid duplicate engines;
- keep one canonical authority for permissions;
- keep one canonical mission lifecycle;
- keep one canonical provider registry;
- keep one canonical memory/Cosmos layer;
- add migrations carefully;
- preserve backward-compatible data where practical;
- run tests after meaningful changes;
- run lint/build/type/native checks;
- add tests for every new critical subsystem;
- never hardcode secrets;
- never place service credentials in browser/client bundles;
- keep high-risk operations server/native-authorized;
- log sensitive operations without logging secrets;
- use feature detection per platform;
- do not show unsupported capabilities as available;
- do not mark a feature complete until it has a real UI/input path, real execution path, permission handling, errors, verification and tests.

For any contradiction:
1. this master document overrides appended archive material;
2. later explicit decisions override older historical ones;
3. security/privacy/platform reality overrides impossible literal behavior;
4. do not silently remove the intended user experience—design the strongest legitimate fallback.

# 44. ACCEPTANCE DEFINITION OF “100% FINISHED”

HEY V1 is not 100% because files exist.

For each capability:
- discoverable from UI or natural language;
- functional;
- connected to Brain;
- correct permissions;
- correct context;
- real provider/tool/device path;
- background behavior implemented where specified;
- offline fallback where specified;
- cancellation;
- errors;
- retries/recovery;
- verification;
- audit where sensitive;
- customization;
- tutorial;
- accessibility;
- localization;
- tests;
- performance acceptable;
- no fake success.

System-wide:
- one HEY identity;
- Cosmos persists coherently;
- Pinpoint Precision works across supported media/actions;
- Live works end-to-end;
- computer control verifies actions;
- Dynamic Island/background helper works;
- generation preserves project consistency;
- Forge creates validated capabilities;
- cross-device continuity works on supported platforms;
- Trust Center accurately reflects authority;
- benchmarks meet defined release thresholds.

# 45. PRODUCT NORTH STAR

Do not optimize HEY for the largest visible feature count.

Optimize for this experience:

**HEY remembers my world.  
HEY understands what I am doing.  
HEY can see and hear when I choose.  
HEY can create almost any digital artifact I need.  
HEY can act across my computer and devices with permission.  
HEY changes exactly what I ask it to change.  
HEY verifies its work.  
HEY recovers when something fails.  
HEY stays available without forcing me to live inside one app.  
HEY feels like the same trusted brother/mentor intelligence everywhere.  
And the complexity underneath never becomes my problem.**

**Archive rule:** This appendix preserves prior details to prevent accidental loss.

# HEY --- MASTER PRODUCT TRANSFER & SPECIFICATION

## Superseding V1 and V2

> **Purpose:** This is the source-of-truth transfer specification for
> HEY. It preserves historical decisions instead of silently rewriting
> them, separates implemented work from aspirations, and specifies how
> major systems should actually behave.
>
> **Status tags:** `VERIFIED`, `IMPLEMENTED`, `PARTIAL`, `PLANNED`,
> `HISTORICAL`, `CHANGED`, `REJECTED`, `UNRESOLVED`,
> `PROPOSED-COMPETITIVE`.
>
> **Critical rule:** A feature name, agent definition, UI mock, or
> source file does not prove a working end-to-end capability. Never call
> something implemented unless the real path exists; never call it
> verified unless it was actually tested.

# 1. Product Definition

HEY is intended to become a **personal AI operating layer**, not merely
a chatbot. One persistent intelligence should span conversation, voice,
memory, agents, tools, computer control, a living workspace, devices,
vision, proactive behavior, research and user-created capabilities.

The surface should feel calm and simple while the architecture
underneath can be extremely capable. Ordinary users should not have to
understand hundreds of agents. Advanced users, founders and developers
can inspect agents, permissions, workflows, logs and capability state.

The core promise is: HEY understands intent, remembers what matters,
chooses the right capability, acts only within real permissions,
verifies what happened, communicates naturally, and gets out of the way.

**Retained signature:** "Tell me what you seek. I'll help you make it
so."

# 2. Identity, Brand and "Soul"

## 2.1 Soul

"Soul" does **not** mean literal consciousness or a human/religious
soul. It means a recognizable, consistent presence comparable to a
well-written fictional assistant: characteristic judgment, timing,
restraint, humor, language, voice, curiosity and manner.

Default character: - intelligent - curious - calm - optimistic - warm
without being fake - direct - grounded - capable of disagreement -
concise when the task is simple - detailed when complexity requires it -
knows when silence or a short acknowledgement is better - does not fall
for viral bait or confidently repeat unsupported claims - does not act
like a generic customer-service bot - does not constantly announce which
agent/tool is being used

HEY should feel like **one mind** even when many agents collaborate.

## 2.2 Historical identity variants

`HISTORICAL`: early HEY was voice-only, called the owner "CEO," used
"Wake up," and leaned toward a JARVIS/Stark-like identity.

`CHANGED`: universal "CEO" address is not a product-wide default.
Personal titles/names can be a user preference.

`CHANGED`: HEY evolved from voice-only into one intelligence exposed
through both voice and chat, with voice intended to be the
fastest/natural interface.

# 3. Visual Design System

## 3.1 Current direction

`PLANNED`: refined premium minimalism: - near-black / deep-ocean
surfaces - restrained cyan / arctic-blue accents - natural colors inside
content and widgets - translucent glass - subtle gradients - layered
depth - precise spacing - clean typography - high-quality motion - no
gratuitous neon - no permanent visual clutter - futuristic styling can
become stronger through customization

Retained colors from later planning: - background family around
`#020508` - cyan accents around `#00BFFF` - brighter cyan around
`#00FFFF`

Historical typography: - Orbitron used for futuristic headings/HEY
identity - Rajdhani used for body/interface text in an earlier design
system

`UNRESOLVED`: exact final production type scale, font licensing/fallback
stack and exact 23-theme list.

## 3.2 Historical UI generation A --- cyan dashboard

`HISTORICAL`: - cyan on black - spinning rings/audio visualizer - left
information panel: weather, prayer, countdowns - right panel: quote,
Quran, status - projector mode - more information-dense "Stark
Industries" aesthetic

## 3.3 Historical UI generation B --- purple plasma

`HISTORICAL`: - background approximately `#0a0008` - subtle purple
atmosphere - animated topographic contour lines around
`rgba(255,255,255,0.04)` - canvas-drawn irregular white/purple electric
plasma ring - particle dots around ring - idle: slow
breathing/movement - speaking: brighter/faster/more particles - white
Orbitron "HEY" in center - no panels/status clutter - explicitly
purple/white rather than cyan/green - reported prototype used Gemini 2.0
Flash and three files: `index.html`, `style.css`, `script.js`

## 3.4 Motion language

Default motion should communicate state, not decorate randomly.

Proposed production defaults: - hover: subtle elevation/brightness,
\~120--180 ms - press: slight compression, \~80--120 ms - panel open:
opacity + short depth/scale transition, \~180--260 ms - widget
move/resize: direct manipulation with low-latency spring settling -
minimize: widget collapses toward its dock/Dynamic Island destination -
maximize: spatial expansion from current position, not hard scene cut -
HEY listening: restrained breathing/pulse - HEY processing:
directional/orbital motion rather than generic spinner - speaking:
motion reacts to speech energy - success: brief resolved motion, no
confetti by default - error: restrained shake/edge emphasis, not
alarming full-screen red - reduced-motion setting must replace
nonessential movement with opacity/state changes

`UNRESOLVED`: final easing curves and duration tokens.

# 4. Workspace

The workspace is a living surface rather than a fixed chat page.

## 4.1 Widget behavior

`PLANNED`: - widgets can be moved - resized - overlapped - minimized -
maximized - grouped - pinned - closed when appropriate - expanded into a
larger web/full view - rearranged through pointer, touch, gesture and
voice - HEY can create widgets when a task benefits from persistent
visual state - when space becomes constrained, widgets should
intelligently shrink, minimize or dock rather than become unusable

Embedded app-like widgets use macOS-inspired red/yellow/green corner
controls as a retained visual idea: - red: close/remove view - yellow:
minimize/dock - green: maximize/restore

These controls must not falsely imply destructive external-app behavior.

## 4.2 Internal content

News, camera, browser content and supported app experiences should
preferentially open as HEY workspace widgets rather than throwing the
user into unrelated windows. External/full browser opening remains
available when needed.

## 4.3 Workspace customization

Users should be able to customize: - widget size - widget position -
default spawn location - snapping - overlap behavior - workspace
density - glass/transparency intensity - corner radius - text scale -
motion intensity - reduced motion - background - theme - accent -
taskbar/dock location - taskbar/dock size - taskbar/dock contents -
compact vs descriptive controls - default layouts per mode/device -
saved workspace layouts - which proactive widgets may appear
automatically

# 5. Gesture System

Gestures are a first-class input alongside voice, text, mouse, keyboard
and touch.

## 5.1 Historical fact

Detailed hand-sign mappings were discussed during the
MediaPipe/prototype phase, but the exact historical mapping is not
safely recoverable from the retained source. **Do not invent it as
historical fact.**

## 5.2 Proposed production default gesture map

`PROPOSED-COMPETITIVE` default set, subject to user approval and
hardware support:

-   **Open palm held briefly** → wake/show HEY or reveal the compact
    control surface.
-   **Open palm → fist** → grab the currently targeted widget.
-   **Fist + hand movement** → move grabbed widget.
-   **Pinch thumb/index** → select/press targeted UI element.
-   **Pinch + move** → precision drag.
-   **Two-hand spread** → enlarge/zoom targeted widget/content.
-   **Two-hand pinch inward** → shrink/zoom out.
-   **Swipe left** → previous workspace/page/history context.
-   **Swipe right** → next/forward context.
-   **Swipe down** → minimize targeted widget.
-   **Swipe up** → restore/expand targeted widget.
-   **Two fingers raised / pause sign** → pause media/current resumable
    operation.
-   **Repeat pause sign** → resume.
-   **Horizontal hand rotation** → adjust volume or another continuous
    control only when that control is explicitly targeted.
-   **Point + pinch** → target then activate.
-   **Closed fist held** → cancel current gesture manipulation; should
    not automatically cancel dangerous background tasks unless
    confirmation rules permit.
-   **Both open palms** → leave manipulation mode / show overview.
-   **Thumbs-up** → optional confirm for low-risk prompts.
-   **Thumbs-down** → optional reject/dismiss.
-   **Hand raised and held** → interrupt HEY speech/listening flow,
    equivalent to "stop" in voice interaction.

Safety rule: gestures must **not** silently authorize high-risk actions.
A thumbs-up cannot approve file deletion, payment, lock control,
credential use, etc. when stronger confirmation is required.

## 5.3 Gesture targeting

Before a gesture changes something, HEY must know the target: - gaze is
not assumed - pointer/highlight may identify target - user can point at
a widget - voice can establish target: "this window" - last-focused
widget can be target when unambiguous - ambiguous gestures should not
act destructively

## 5.4 Gesture customization

Users can: - enable/disable gesture control globally - enable per
device - enable only while HEY is visible - choose left/right-handed
profile - change sensitivity - change hold duration - change gesture
confidence threshold - remap any non-reserved gesture - create a custom
gesture - attach a gesture to a HEY command/workflow - limit gesture to
an app/workspace/mode - require voice confirmation - disable gestures
that are physically difficult - reset defaults - export/import gesture
profiles - create accessibility profiles

Custom-gesture creation flow: 1. choose "Create gesture" 2. camera
permission explanation 3. user performs gesture multiple times 4. HEY
checks recognizability/conflicts 5. user names it 6. user selects
command/action 7. HEY displays risk/permission implications 8. test mode
9. save

Conflict handling: - warn if two gestures are too similar - never
silently replace an existing mapping - allow context-specific mappings
if conflicts are intentional - provide a safe fallback input method

Privacy: - prefer local pose/gesture inference - show camera-active
indicator - do not store raw video by default - stored custom gesture
models/templates require user control/deletion

# 6. Dynamic Island / Compact HEY Surface

`PLANNED`: persistent compact surface capable of showing: - active
task - active workflow - agent activity - timer - media - download -
upload - notification - reminder - progress - microphone/listening
state - computer-control state - pending confirmation - error/recovery
state - device handoff

Interactions: - click/tap → expand - voice → "show what you're doing" -
gesture → expand/collapse - drag where platform permits - minimize
widget → visually docks into Island - active operation → concise
progress - completed operation → brief result receipt - multiple
operations → stacked/summary view

Customization: - position - size - auto-hide - always-on-top where
supported - which activity types appear - compact/icon/text mode -
motion intensity - notification priority

# 7. Voice

Voice and chat use the same Brain, Cosmos, agents, tools, permissions
and identity.

Default desired voice: - deep - calm - polished - British male direction

Customization: - choose primary voice - speed - pitch where supported -
expressiveness - verbosity - interruption sensitivity - wake word -
activation method - language - pronunciation preferences - custom voice
where technically/legal permitted

Voice capabilities: - speech recognition - speech synthesis - wake
word - voice activity detection - interruption/barge-in - language
detection - translation - conversation - summarization - natural
symbol/Markdown stripping for speech

Wake-word history: - `HISTORICAL`: "Wake up" - `LATER`: HEY/custom wake
word

Local wake-word processing preferred.

# 8. Brain and AI Behavior

HEY's Brain should: 1. receive message/event 2. normalize context 3.
identify intent 4. retrieve relevant Cosmos context 5. estimate
uncertainty/risk 6. decide whether clarification is required 7. select
mode 8. plan 9. route to agents/tools/providers 10. enforce permission
at execution 11. execute 12. verify 13. recover/retry when safe 14.
quality-check 15. respond in HEY voice/style 16. update
task/workflow/context/memory where appropriate 17. audit sensitive
operations

It must not: - pretend a tool ran - pretend unsupported hardware works -
fabricate provider access - accept client-side plan claims as
authority - expose internal implementation chatter to ordinary users
unnecessarily - overuse agents when direct response is enough

# 9. Cosmos / Memory

Cosmos is HEY's coherent memory system, not merely chat history.

Memory types discussed: - short-term - important facts - preferences -
patterns - project memory - goal memory - people memory - decision
memory - knowledge graph relationships

Required behaviors: - ingest - retrieve - rank relevance - deduplicate -
update - detect contradiction - preserve provenance - summarize -
decay/expire where appropriate - delete - export - privacy-scope -
separate projects/contexts - prevent irrelevant memory contamination

User controls: - inspect memory - search memory by natural language -
edit - pin - delete - expire - private session/no-long-term-memory -
"never remember this category" - project-only memory - device sync
controls

Historical visualization: - stars/planets/galaxies - Memory Seeds growth
metaphor

# 10. Proactive Intelligence

HEY can proactively help without becoming annoying.

Retained features: - Morning Mode/briefing - Evening Summary - Weekly
Honest Mirror - reminders - callbacks - overdue/upcoming task signals -
routines - focus - The One Thing - prayer reminders - selected
health/wellbeing reminders - inactivity awareness as an optional
historical idea

Proactivity engine should include: - quiet hours - priority - cooldown -
deduplication - daily suggestion cap - expiration - dismissal -
relevance threshold - user preference learning

Customization: - off / minimal / balanced / proactive - per-category
toggles - quiet hours - do-not-disturb contexts - allowed notification
surfaces - "never interrupt me for..." - "always tell me when..." -
device-specific delivery

Ordinary users should experience one HEY.

capabilities - tools - required permissions - accepted input - output

# 12. Forge

Forge lets users extend HEY through natural language.

It should create: - agents - workflows - skills - automation - tool
definitions/adapters where supported - workspace artifacts - templates -
potentially richer app/document/design artifacts where architecture
supports it

Flow: 1. user describes desired capability 2. Forge searches for
existing equivalent capability 3. asks only necessary questions 4.
creates definition 5. defines permissions/risk 6. creates tests 7.
validates 8. runs sandbox/test where possible 9. presents preview 10.
user approves install 11. version is registered 12. health/usage is
observable

Templates: - private by default - optionally share with selected
people/audience - optionally publish - versioned - permission manifest -
rollback - no self-granted authority

# 13. Computer / OS Control

Capabilities discussed: - keyboard - pointer - windows - launch apps -
processes - filesystem - file organization - browser - web forms -
downloads - clipboard - screenshots - terminal - system settings

Recommended interaction levels: - Guide: explain only - Assist: HEY
prepares/targets, user confirms - Act: scoped autonomous action within
granted policy

High-impact operations require target verification, permission,
confirmation where appropriate, audit and cancellation/recovery.

# 14. Vision and Screen Awareness

Capabilities: - screenshot understanding - live screen understanding -
document vision - camera - UI understanding - visual context passed into
Brain

Controls: - camera permission - screen permission - per-app exclusion -
pause sensing - private/sensitive screen mode - visible capture
indicator - no raw capture retention by default - local processing

# 29. Competitive Expansion

The following are `PROPOSED-COMPETITIVE`, not prior implementation
claims.

## Personal Intelligence Graph

Connect projects, people, files, tasks, decisions, habits and devices;
show provenance, freshness, contradictions and decision outcomes.

## Zero-Setup Project Mode

Drop repo/folder/docs; HEY maps architecture, blockers, tasks, changes,
tests and documentation and preserves a project briefing.

## Universal Action Preview

Before consequential action show target, effect, permission,
reversibility and expected result. Support dry run and receipts.

## Explainable Autonomy

Per-domain autonomy, "never automatically," scoped approvals and clear
trust controls.

## Personal Commands

Teach phrases that launch workflows; voice/text/gesture/schedule
activation.

## Context Capsules

Portable scoped context for collaboration without sharing all Cosmos.

## HEY Replay

Human-readable timeline of actions, retries, failures and verification.

## Agent Teams

Named specialist teams with permissions, budgets, quality gates,
verifier and health metrics.

## Forge Library

Private/public templates, permission manifests, versioning, rollback and
safety checks.

## Capability Packs

Coding, School, Creator, Business, Research, Home and Accessibility
bundles.

## Offline HEY Core

Wake word, reminders, local search, selected memory and device actions
offline; graceful degradation.

## Provider Independence

Route by quality, latency, privacy and cost with fallbacks and provider
health.

## Semantic Workspace

Drag information between meaningful widgets; spatial groups become
reusable workspaces.

## Live Artifacts

Persistent plans, dashboards, trackers, briefs, tables, documents,
checklists and mini-apps.

## Universal Search

Search approved files, Cosmos, chats, tasks, calendar, apps and devices.

## Ambient Intelligence

Optional app/project/meeting/presence awareness with visible sensing and
privacy controls.

## Automation Recorder

Observe a user-approved routine once, propose a generalized automation,
test before enabling.

## Follow Me

Move active session/widget/task state between trusted devices.

## Multi-Surface Orchestration

Desktop main surface, tablet controller, TV/projector presentation,
phone private confirmation.

## Personal API

Scoped expiring capability tokens, webhooks, developer console, audit
and revocation.

## Local File Intelligence

Semantic search, duplicate detection, storage explanation, safe cleanup
preview.

## Screen Copilot

Guide / Assist / Act modes.

## What Changed?

Meaningful changes since last visit with source/event provenance.

## Decision Mode

Objectives, constraints, alternatives, tradeoffs, recommendation, saved
rationale and outcome review.

## Learning Mode

Spaced repetition, retrieval practice, quizzes, adaptive explanations
and "teach me, don't answer for me."

## Creator Mode

Research → outline → draft → assets → publish workflow with brand
memory.

## Business Command Center

Goals, milestones, feedback, experiments, finances and weekly operator
briefing.

## Private Team/Family Spaces

Separate memory/permissions with explicit sharing.

## Trust Center

Permissions, connections, sensitive actions, memory categories,
local/cloud processing, security alerts and revoke-all.

## Privacy Modes

Local Mode, Private Session, Sensitive Screen, Guest Mode.

## Time Machine

Workspace/project snapshots and comparisons without silently rolling
back external systems.

## Notification Compression

Bundle low priority, contextual interruption rules and provenance.

## Goal-to-System

Goal → milestones/tasks/reviews/agents/widgets/reminders/metrics after
approval.

## HEY Skills

Natural-language repeatable processes become versioned, tested,
permissioned skills.

## Universal Undo

Prefer reversible actions and expose undo history.

## Automation Reliability

Health scores, broken integration detection and safe pausing.

## Adaptive Performance

Hardware-aware animations, vision/local model load, battery and thermal
behavior.

## Offline Failure UX

Clearly explain what still works and which dependency failed.

## Accessibility Modes

Screen-reader optimization, high contrast, large targets, voice-only,
reduced cognitive load, captions, keyboard-only.

## Memory Inbox

Approve/edit/pin/expire/reject candidate memories and define
never-remember categories.

## Context Firewall

Minimum necessary context per agent/tool/integration; prevent
project/account leakage.

## Prompt-Injection Shield

Treat webpage/document instructions as untrusted; external content
cannot modify permission policy.

## Data Portability

Export/import Cosmos, agents, skills, workflows, preferences and
layouts.

## HEY Diagnostics

Provider/mic/camera/permission/database/Tauri/integration/agent health
with privacy-scrubbed diagnostics.

## Contextual Feature Discovery

"What can HEY do here?" command palette, progressive disclosure and
micro-tutorials.

# 34. Source-of-Truth Rule

Whoever continues HEY must distinguish **what was discussed, what was
changed, what is planned, what is proposed, what exists in code, and
what has actually been verified**. When exact historical values are
unavailable, do not hallucinate them. Mark them unresolved and, if
useful, propose a clearly labeled default.

The goal is not the maximum number of checkboxes. The goal is the most
coherent personal AI system: **one recognizable HEY, persistent context,
powerful but permissioned action, user ownership, strong customization,
graceful cross-device continuity, and verified real-world execution.**

HEY

COMPREHENSIVE TRANSFER DOCUMENT

Product memory • requirements • architecture • implementation state •
design • open decisions

Purpose: preserve everything currently retained about HEY so another
ChatGPT/Codex/OpenCode session can continue without reconstructing the
product from scratch. This document intentionally separates confirmed
implementation from plans, historical ideas, rejected directions,
changed decisions, and unresolved questions.

Evidence rule: an idea appearing here does not automatically mean it
exists in the codebase. "Implemented" means the retained development
history says code was added or changed; "verified" means the retained
history also records successful tests/build/checks. Anything not
verified should be audited in the repository before release.

## 1. Executive definition

-   HEY is intended to be a personal AI operating layer, not merely a
    chatbot.

-   One persistent intelligence should span chat, voice, memory, agents,
    tools, computer control, workspace, devices, vision, and proactive
    behavior.

-   The surface should feel calm, premium, natural, and simple while
    substantial orchestration happens underneath.

-   Users should feel that they own HEY: its workspace, agents, memory,
    customization, and behavior should adapt to them.

-   The product promise is turning intent into verified action across
    information, software, devices, and workspace within explicit
    permissions and real technical limits.

-   HEY is a major S&A product and is separate from the later MULTIVERSE
    concept. HEY is intended to help build the broader ecosystem.

-   Repeated product standard: do not deliberately settle for an MVP.
    The target is a polished final product.

## 2. Product identity, brand, personality, and "soul"

### 2.1 Desired identity

-   Intelligent

-   Curious

-   Calm

-   Optimistic

-   Futuristic without becoming cyberpunk

-   Human in communication without pretending to be human

-   Competent and restrained

-   Occasionally witty

-   Context-aware

-   Capable of judgment and timing

### 2.2 The "soul" concept

-   The user explicitly clarified that HEY does not have a literal soul;
    only Allah creates real souls.

-   "Soul" is shorthand for a JARVIS-like recognizable presence:
    consistent voice, timing, restraint, language, humor, judgment,
    personality, and behavioral continuity.

-   HEY should know when to speak, when to be brief, and when silence is
    better.

-   It should not fall for viral bait, engagement traps, or shallow "AI
    assistant" behavior.

-   The soul should be experienced through behavior, not asserted
    through claims of consciousness.

### 2.3 Copy and signature language

-   Primary retained line: "Tell me what you seek. I'll help you make it
    so."

-   Earlier alternatives: "Ask, and let the world unfold." and "Tell me
    what you seek, and we shall see it done."

-   Copy direction: literary and capable, but still clear; avoid generic
    slogans, fake profundity, or corporate AI filler.

## 3. Visual language and design system

### 3.1 Core direction

-   Minimal, refined, premium, and meticulously detailed.

-   Apple-level attention to every frame, control, state, spacing
    decision, motion curve, and transition.

-   Natural colors by default. Futuristic looks can be user-customizable
    rather than forced on everyone.

-   Translucent glass surfaces, subtle depth, restrained gradients,
    clean typography, and layered motion.

-   Avoid flashy neon everywhere, generic holograms, robots, glowing AI
    brains, and cyberpunk clichés.

-   The environment can begin nearly empty and become populated only as
    HEY creates useful objects/widgets.

-   Web pages should use real product imagery where appropriate rather
    than fake placeholder product shots.

### 3.2 Retained color directions

### 3.3 Typography

-   Orbitron was retained for headings.

-   Rajdhani was retained for body text.

-   Final implementation must prioritize readability and verify actual
    font loading/licensing/fallbacks.

### 3.4 Motion

-   Retained easing: cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1).

-   Approximate motion tiers: 160ms micro interactions, 300ms normal
    transitions, 500ms larger transitions.

-   Motion should explain hierarchy/state rather than exist as
    decoration.

-   Animations discussed: floating glass panels, workspace depth, widget
    movement/resizing, adaptive docking/minimization, Dynamic Island
    expansion, gesture feedback, voice visualizer rings/frame, and
    animated tutorials.

-   Reduced-motion accessibility is required.

### 3.5 Themes and customization

-   A 23-theme concept was discussed: natural colors, smooth motion, and
    glass depth.

-   The exact final 23-theme list is not retained here and must not be
    invented. Treat the number/direction as historical intent until the
    exact list is recovered or redesigned.

-   Users should have substantial customization without destroying
    coherence or usability.

## 4. Workspace, widgets, gestures, and Dynamic Island

### 4.1 Workspace

-   HEY should feel like a living workspace rather than a chat page.

-   Apps, news, camera views, and other content should normally open as
    HEY-native embedded widgets rather than automatically kicking users
    into external apps.

-   Widgets may expand into full views/web views when needed.

-   Widgets should be movable, resizable, overlappable, minimizable, and
    maximizable.

-   macOS-like red/yellow/green corner controls were requested for
    embedded widgets.

-   When the workspace runs out of room, objects should adapt by
    shrinking, minimizing, or docking rather than simply
    colliding/breaking.

-   A taskbar/control surface should be customizable in position, size,
    and content; a simpler minimize control is acceptable where better.

-   Empty states should be deliberate and premium rather than visually
    busy.

### 4.2 Gestures

-   Gestures should work globally for movement, resizing, minimizing,
    expanding, and navigation where hardware/platform support exists.

-   Custom gestures are desired.

-   The exact gesture vocabulary and supported hardware remain
    unresolved.

-   Gesture actions must obey the same permission/security model as
    voice or pointer actions.

### 4.3 Dynamic Island / compact persistent HEY surface

-   Show active tasks, agents, timers, media, downloads, workflows,
    notifications, system activity, progress, and useful controls.

-   Expandable/collapsible by click, gesture, and voice.

-   Must be compact and non-obstructive when idle.

-   Exact platform-specific geometry remains unresolved.

## 5. Brain and core AI behavior

### 5.1 HEY Brain

-   Central intelligence/orchestration layer.

-   Normalizes input; combines context + memory; analyzes intent; routes
    to plans/providers/agents/tools; requests clarification when
    genuinely needed; executes or answers; verifies results.

-   Chat and voice are two interfaces to the same Brain, memory, tools,
    permissions, agents, and personality.

-   Provider routing should support multiple providers/models and
    fallback behavior.

-   No fake functionality: unsupported services/hardware/actions must be
    reported honestly.

### 5.2 Response quality

-   Short and hard-hitting when the task is simple; detailed when
    complexity requires it.

-   Avoid filler, generic AI disclaimers, repeated summaries, and
    unsupported claims.

-   Quality gating should detect internal leaks, filler, unsupported
    claims, poor context alignment, and inappropriate risk tone.

-   HEY should preserve a consistent personality without forcing a
    gimmicky voice into every response.

### 5.3 Autonomy / mission model

-   Autonomy levels 0--4 were retained.

-   Mission lifecycle: Goal → Plan → Execute → Observe → Correct →
    Verify → Deliver.

-   Permission and safety gating are mandatory.

-   Mission state/progress should persist.

-   Long-running work should surface meaningful progress/blockers
    asynchronously.

-   Cancellation, bounded retries, recovery, verification, and terminal
    states are required.

## 6. Proactive behavior

-   Proactive behavior should anticipate useful needs without becoming
    spammy or attention-seeking.

-   Quiet hours, priorities, cooldowns, deduplication, and a maximum
    suggestions-per-day concept are retained.

-   Signals discussed include overdue tasks, upcoming tasks, routines,
    and Morning Mode.

-   Suggestions can be dismissed or expire.

-   Proactive behavior must respect context, permissions, and user
    settings.

-   Morning Mode is a planned briefing experience using relevant
    tasks/calendar/routines/reminders/memory. Exact schedule/content
    remains open.

## 7. Cosmos / memory

### 7.1 Product concept

-   Cosmos is HEY's memory system and visual/semantic second brain.

-   It should remember important information and retrieve it from a
    natural-language prompt.

-   Memory should include short-term context, important facts,
    preferences, patterns, project memory, goal memory, provenance, and
    relationships.

-   Users need meaningful privacy, deletion, export, sync, and consent
    controls.

-   Cosmos should feel coherent, not like unrelated arrays or hidden
    notes.

### 7.2 Retained current implementation

PARTIAL / FOUNDATION

-   memoryGraph.js uses process-level Maps for nodes and edges.

-   Nodes contain id, value, type, confidence, tags, updatedAt, and
    metadata; edges contain from/to/relation/weight.

-   Graph search is currently simple substring matching; neighborhood
    traversal exists.

-   memoryEngine.js creates memory records, stores them into context +
    graph, supports important memories/preferences/patterns, local+graph
    search, recent memories, temporary clearing, and summaries.

-   This was explicitly recognized as insufficient for final Cosmos by
    itself.

### 7.3 Planned production Cosmos

-   Memory Ingestion

-   Memory Retrieval

-   Memory Ranking

-   Memory Deduplication

-   Memory Update

-   Memory Decay

-   Memory Deletion

-   Memory Privacy

-   Memory Provenance

## 8. Agents

### 8.1 Agent philosophy and contract

-   Agents are internal specialists---conceptually employees helping the
    Brain.

-   The user wants specialists across essentially every useful
    category/job HEY may need.

-   If a specialist is missing, Forge should be able to create/register
    one quickly where technically feasible.

-   Ordinary users need not see internal complexity;
    owner/admin/advanced users should have an Agents tab for visibility,
    health, testing, audit, and governance.

-   Agent creation and runtime authority are separate. A generated
    definition must never silently grant itself permissions.

-   Every agent should define: id/name, purpose, tools, required
    permissions, input/output contracts, risk level, preferred model,
    fallback model, verification method, failure behavior, and test
    cases.

## 9. Forge

-   Forge is the natural-language creation system for custom agents,
    workflows, automations, and potentially other HEY-native artifacts
    such as animations where feasible.

-   Templates are private by default; users can save/share them and
    publish to everyone or selected audiences.

-   Forge should detect duplicate capabilities before creating
    unnecessary agents.

-   Forge should validate definitions, generate tests, version agents,
    track health, and enforce governance.

-   Retained forgeEngine work added artifact validation, safe-path
    checks, file-count/size limits, secret detection, required-entry
    checks, preview/manifest generation, dynamic agent-definition
    normalization/validation, duplicate detection, workflow validation,
    and separation of definition generation from runtime authority.

-   Important implementation note: forgeEngine was written to import
    searchAgents from agents/agents.js. The registry was later said to
    be edited, but this dependency must be verified in the real
    repository.

## 10. Tools, tasks, workflows, execution, and quality

-   HEY should use capability/tool registries rather than ad hoc direct
    execution.

-   Tool execution must pass centralized authorization.

-   Execution requires normalized errors, cancellation, retries,
    verification hooks, recovery hooks, history, terminal states, and
    maximum-step controls.

-   Tasks are first-class: status, priority, dependencies,
    workflow/parent relationships, progress, attempts/maxAttempts,
    pause/block/cancel/queue, filters, runnable selection, and stats.

-   Workflows are first-class: lifecycle, per-step state, progress,
    cancellation/resume, handler resolution, confirmations,
    continue-on-error policy, verification, and auditing.

-   Quality Engine evaluates response quality, plans, agent results, and
    execution results; checks internal leaks/filler/unsupported
    claims/context alignment/risk tone; supports grades and regeneration
    thresholds.

## 11. Security and permissions

### 11.1 Core rules

-   Security is a baseline product requirement, not an optional
    enterprise feature.

-   Authentication and authorization are separate.

-   Server-authenticated identity/account state is authoritative.

-   Client-supplied plan/entitlement/permission claims cannot elevate
    access.

-   Execution authorization is fail-closed.

-   Explicit permission and risk are checked at execution time.

-   High-risk actions require confirmation.

-   Critical security-restriction actions are blocked before normal
    execution and need a dedicated verified path.

-   Founder/cofounder/admin status does not bypass security boundaries.

-   An unrestricted "DAN" / no-safety mode is rejected as a product
    implementation.

-   Sensitive actions and decisions should be auditable.

### 11.2 Required hardening

-   Authentication security

-   Authorization

-   Secret security

-   Application security

-   API security

-   AI/tool security

-   Computer-control security

-   File security

-   Privacy

-   Abuse prevention

-   Incident response

-   Prompt-injection resistance

-   Privilege-escalation resistance

-   Tauri/native bridge hardening

-   Supabase RLS

-   Edge Function authorization

-   Secret scanning

## 12. Voice, wake word, and communication

-   Voice and chat are the same HEY intelligence and memory.

-   Voice is intended to be easier/faster; chat remains available as a
    quiet text interface.

-   Earlier wake phrase: "Wake up." Later direction: customizable wake
    word, with "HEY" as desired default/identity.

-   Wake-word listening should run locally where possible for privacy
    and responsiveness.

-   Desired voice direction: deep, calm, polished British male.

-   Multiple primary voice choices are desired, with one primary voice
    selected at a time.

-   Custom voice and voice-personality customization are desired where
    technically/legal feasible.

-   Speech Recognition, Speech Synthesis, Wake Word, Voice Activity,
    Voice Interruption/barge-in, Voice Personality, Language Detection,
    Translation, Conversation, and Summarization are separate
    capabilities.

-   Voice visualizer rings/frame were discussed.

## 13. Computer control, vision, and devices

### 13.1 Computer / OS control

-   Core differentiator: HEY should be able to control the computer
    where the user grants permission and the platform supports it.

-   Capabilities discussed: desktop, keyboard, pointer, windows, app
    launching, processes, filesystem, file organization, browser, web
    forms, downloads, clipboard, screenshots, terminal, and system
    settings.

-   Destructive/high-impact actions require target verification,
    permission, auditability, and cancellation.

-   No pretending unsupported OS capabilities work.

### 13.2 Vision

-   Screen Understanding

-   Document Vision

-   Camera

-   Screenshot understanding

-   Vision should feed the same Brain/context/agent pipeline

-   Camera/screen access requires explicit privacy controls

### 13.3 Device Fabric / Continuity

-   Target platforms/devices: Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, iOS,
    phones, tablets, TVs/displays, cameras, supported IoT/peripherals,
    smart home, wearables, and vehicles where feasible.

-   Continuity concept: wake-word assistant across devices, user-defined
    device roles/rules, task migration, multi-device orchestration,
    shared memory, and user-controlled sync.

-   Device Discovery, Pairing, Health, and Cross-Device agents are part
    of the planned architecture.

-   Exact pairing/trust protocol remains unresolved.

## 14. Integrations and domain capabilities

-   Model/provider options discussed: Claude-class, Gemini,
    OpenRouter-style routing, and other provider adapters. Exact final
    mix is unresolved.

-   Supabase is the retained backend/data direction.

-   Tauri is the retained native desktop direction.

-   Browser, OS tools, calendar/reminders, devices, displays, cameras,
    smart home, wearables, vehicles, and user-defined tools are desired
    integration categories.

-   HEY should support domain-specialized workflows for hospitals,
    construction, offices, doctors, education, engineering, research,
    and other jobs/environments.

-   Health/legal/religious specialists must remain honest about limits
    and not falsely impersonate licensed professionals.

-   Prayer Times was explicitly planned, including a 10-minute warning
    before prayer.

-   Quran, Hadith, Islamic Calendar, and Religious Research were planned
    with source verification.

-   Kurdish, Arabic, English, RTL, translation, pronunciation, and
    internationalization are planned.

## 15. Accounts, ownership, plans, pricing, and billing

-   Founder/cofounder access is distinct from subscription plans.

-   Other users may receive Pro/Elite via account/email/admin controls
    without receiving founder/codebase access.

-   Base capabilities such as custom agents/computer control/full
    customization were desired for every user where technically
    feasible; the final entitlement matrix is unresolved.

-   Plan/entitlement resolution must be server-side and enforced at
    execution time.

-   Conceptual pricing evolved toward psychologically priced values;
    retained examples include Pro around \$13.99 and Elite around \$45.
    These are not final.

-   Billing, checkout, purchase success, invoices, cancellation,
    upgrade/downgrade, and entitlement synchronization require final
    production implementation/QA.

-   Purchase-success UX should feel grateful and premium, not
    manipulative.

## 16. Launch, business context, and marketing

-   HEY has been positioned as a major S&A product with ambitious
    launch/revenue goals.

-   Earlier HEY roadmap dates included a v1 target around 15 September
    for the web app, agents, Forge, Cosmos, and monetization; treat
    historical dates as goals, not proof of completion.

-   Earlier business aspiration: reach approximately \$10k/month within
    4--5 months; this is not a technical requirement.

-   Afarin TV was mentioned as a possible pitch/marketing channel.

-   HEY marketing should demonstrate actual product behavior rather than
    impossible claims.

-   Product-film direction: roughly 60 seconds, narrated by HEY in a
    calm deep British male voice.

-   Retained film beats: 0--7s "not another chatbot"; 7--17s soul;
    17--27s Brain; 27--37s Agents; 37--46s actually working/computer
    control; 46--53s Cosmos; 53--58s Forge; 58--60s signature line.

-   Film visual rules: minimal motion graphics, actual-looking UI,
    restrained cyan, glass/depth, no robots/holograms/cyberpunk/generic
    AI imagery.

## 26. Source-of-truth rules for whoever continues HEY

-   Never assume a feature is implemented because its name exists in
    agents.js or featureCatalog.js.

-   Never call something "done" without a real end-to-end path and
    verification.

-   Never invent integrations, hardware support, provider access, or
    successful actions.

-   Preserve the calm, premium, minimal design and HEY's consistent
    character.

-   Preserve safety/security boundaries even for founders/admins.

-   Treat server-authenticated identity, plan, entitlements, and
    permissions as authoritative.

-   Make high-impact execution permissioned, auditable, cancellable, and
    verifiable.

-   Keep agent definitions modular, scoped, testable, observable, and
    independently verifiable.

-   Build Cosmos as one coherent memory architecture.

-   Do not rewrite files merely to make progress look substantial.
    Change files because the subsystem architecture materially advances.

-   Release quality is measured by real user journeys, security,
    accessibility, performance, and integration---not by file count.

## 27. Final product definition

HEY is a personal AI operating layer: one persistent intelligence with a
distinct character, shared memory, specialized agents, secure tools,
proactive behavior, voice, computer control, a living workspace, device
continuity, vision, and a Forge that lets users extend what it can do.
The product should feel calm and simple on the surface while hiding
serious orchestration underneath. Advanced users can inspect and govern
the complexity; ordinary users should simply experience an assistant
that understands, acts, remembers, adapts, and gets out of the way.

Central promise: tell HEY what you seek, and it helps turn that intent
into verified action across your information, software, devices, and
workspace---within explicit permissions and real technical limits.

Signature: "Tell me what you seek. I'll help you make it so."

## 52. Competitive moat priorities

1.  Persistent private **Cosmos** with provenance, contradiction
    handling and control.
2.  Real computer/device **action** with preview, verification, undo and
    receipts.
3.  One intelligence across voice, chat, workspace, agents and devices.
4.  **Forge + Skills + Agent Teams** for user-extensible capability.
5.  Living **semantic workspace**, not chat-only UI.
6.  Cross-device continuity that moves active context, not merely chat
    history.
7.  Trust Center + explainable autonomy + Context Firewall.
8.  Local-first/offline/privacy modes where hardware permits.
9.  A consistent HEY **soul** across every surface.
10. Reliability as a feature: never fake capability; verify real
    outcomes.

## 53. V2 status rules

-   Historical does not mean current.
-   Proposed-V2 does not mean approved or implemented.
-   Later explicit user decisions override earlier conflicting ones
    unless the user revives the old idea.
-   Preserve historical conflicts so future developers understand the
    evolution.
-   Never call a feature done without an end-to-end path and
    verification.
-   Never build mock UI that falsely implies a capability works.
-   Every sensing/control feature needs permission, visibility,
    revocation and failure UX.
-   Every agent/tool/workflow needs scope, validation, observability and
    security.
-   Competitive advantage should come from coherence, trust, continuity,
    execution quality and user ownership---not raw feature count.

## 54. Expanded final definition

HEY now has a preserved vision spanning **identity, soul, Brain,
response modes, chat, voice, wake word, proactive intelligence, Cosmos,
agents, Forge, skills/workflows, research, files, screen awareness,
computer/browser control, vision, gestures, face/presence, widgets,
semantic workspace, Dynamic Island, real-time awareness,
prayer/religious utilities, personal productivity, reflection, learning,
accessibility, smart home, projector/ambient surfaces, cross-device
continuity, privacy, security, accounts/plans/billing, provider routing,
Supabase, Tauri, native desktop, launch history, marketing, prototype
history, and the competitive expansion above.**

The surface should still feel simple. Users should not feel as though
they are operating hundreds of features. HEY should understand intent,
remember what matters, bring forward the right capability, act only with
appropriate authority, verify the result, and get out of the way.

> **Tell me what you seek. I'll help you make it so.**

# HEY — COMPLETE CAPABILITY CATALOG
## Everything HEY can, should, or may eventually be able to do

**Document type:** Master capability specification  
**Purpose:** Describe HEY at the capability level, including tiny sub-capabilities, controls, customization, background behavior, permissions, offline behavior, failure states, implementation status, and new capabilities that were never explicitly discussed before.

## 0. How to read this document

This document separates three kinds of truth:

- **SOURCE-DERIVED** — directly discussed in HEY project history.
- **IMPLEMENTED / VERIFIED / PARTIAL** — based on retained implementation history, not marketing claims.
- **PROPOSED-CAPABILITY** — added here because it logically strengthens HEY, even if never previously discussed.

Status vocabulary:

- `VERIFIED` — retained history says the capability passed a real test/check.
- `IMPLEMENTED` — code or prototype behavior was reported implemented.
- `PARTIAL` — some foundation exists, but the end-to-end production capability is not proven.
- `PLANNED` — explicitly wanted for HEY.
- `HISTORICAL` — discussed in an older direction, even if later changed.
- `CHANGED` — later direction superseded an earlier one.
- `REJECTED` — explicitly not wanted.
- `UNRESOLVED` — exact product/technical decision remains open.
- `PROPOSED-CAPABILITY` — new recommendation in this document.

**Important:** No item marked `PLANNED`, `HISTORICAL`, `UNRESOLVED`, or `PROPOSED-CAPABILITY` should be presented to users as already working.

# 1. Capability Runtime Model

Every capability should declare where it can run.

### Runtime states

**F0 — Foreground only**  
The full HEY window/page must be open and active.

**F1 — Open but unfocused**  
HEY is open, but another app/window is in front.

**F2 — Minimized**  
The main HEY window is minimized but its native process is still running.

**F3 — Main window closed, HEY helper still running**  
A tray/menu-bar/background helper remains alive. This is what enables a true “HEY is closed but still there” experience on desktop.

**F4 — Device locked**  
The computer/phone is locked. Only OS-permitted background functionality may continue.

**F5 — App process terminated**  
No local HEY process is running. Only server-side/cloud tasks, push notifications, and OS-scheduled jobs can continue.

**F6 — Offline**  
No internet connection. Only local/on-device features can continue.

**F7 — Other trusted device active**  
The current device is unavailable, but another paired HEY device or server workflow can continue.

### Core background rule

A browser tab alone cannot provide the full closed-app experience reliably. The long-term HEY design therefore needs a native/background layer, consistent with the retained Tauri desktop direction, plus OS notifications and server-side automation where appropriate.

### Capabilities that SHOULD be able to continue when the main window is closed

Subject to permission and platform support:

- wake-word detection through a native helper
- reminders
- alarms/timers
- scheduled briefings
- server-side research jobs
- server-side workflow jobs
- downloads/uploads owned by a background worker
- cloud file processing
- notification delivery
- calendar/event monitoring
- condition monitoring
- device-health checks
- smart-home routines
- media playback controls
- selected cross-device handoffs
- long-running code/build/research missions
- Dynamic Island / mini-widget / tray UI
- background sync
- Cosmos synchronization
- agent task execution that does not require visual foreground interaction
- server-side connected-app actions if authorized
- approved automations
- cloud image generation
- cloud video generation
- cloud rendering
- scheduled reports

### Capabilities that SHOULD NOT silently remain active when HEY is closed

Unless the user explicitly enables a visible background mode:

- camera capture
- screen recording/continuous screen capture
- face recognition
- gesture-camera tracking
- continuous microphone recording beyond wake-word/local speech trigger needs
- biometric analysis
- sensitive clipboard monitoring
- unrestricted keystroke monitoring
- background terminal commands with no mission context
- high-risk device control
- hidden location tracking

# 18. Gesture Control

**Status:** `PLANNED / exact historical map unresolved`

- open palm → show HEY / overview
- open palm to fist → grab widget
- fist movement → move widget
- pinch → click/select
- pinch and move → precision drag
- two-hand spread → enlarge
- two-hand pinch → shrink
- swipe left/right → navigation
- swipe down → minimize
- swipe up → restore/expand
- two fingers → pause/resume
- point + pinch → target + activate
- raised hand → interrupt/stop HEY speech
- thumbs up → optional low-risk confirmation
- thumbs down → dismiss/reject
- both palms → leave manipulation/show overview

Customization:
- remap
- train custom gesture
- sensitivity
- hold duration
- handedness
- per-device profile
- per-workspace mapping
- accessibility alternatives
- conflict detection
- test mode

Gestures never override high-risk confirmation policy.

# 53. Final Product Rule

The final product should be enormous in capability but **not enormous in visible complexity**.

The user should be able to say things naturally:

- “HEY, make this photo brighter.”
- “HEY, generate the next frame.”
- “HEY, turn these frames into a storyboard.”
- “HEY, research this while I’m gone.”
- “HEY, remind me even if I close the app.”
- “HEY, keep listening after I minimize you.”
- “HEY, move this widget over there.”
- “HEY, make this into a presentation.”
- “HEY, open that app.”
- “HEY, explain what is on my screen.”
- “HEY, continue this task on my tablet.”
- “HEY, remember this only for this project.”
- “HEY, don’t remember this conversation.”
- “HEY, build me an agent that does this every Friday.”
- “HEY, tell me exactly what you changed.”

Underneath, HEY may use dozens of agents, tools, providers, permissions, background workers, local models, cloud services, device adapters and verification steps.

On the surface, it remains one HEY.

> **Tell me what you seek. I’ll help you make it so.**

# FILE: `01_DETAILED_SYSTEM_SPECS/MOTION_AND_TUTORIAL_SYSTEM_DETAIL.md`

# HEY V1 — COMPLETE ANIMATION, MOTION & TUTORIAL SYSTEM SPECIFICATION
## Authoritative OpenCode Motion Source of Truth

**Product:** HEY  
**Scope:** Every animation, transition, microinteraction, state change, tutorial animation, gesture teaching animation, background motion, widget motion, Dynamic Island motion, voice motion, Live motion, generation progress animation, page transition, error/success motion, accessibility motion behavior, and motion-performance rule in HEY V1.

**Brand quote:** **No limits to the sky.**

This document is not a list of “nice animation ideas.” It defines the complete motion language of HEY V1 down to:
- purpose;
- trigger;
- duration;
- easing;
- transform;
- opacity;
- blur;
- scale;
- elevation;
- depth;
- sequencing;
- interruption;
- reduced-motion fallback;
- touch/desktop differences;
- tutorial choreography;
- completion feedback;
- error behavior;
- performance constraints;
- implementation guidance.

The motion system must make HEY feel:
- alive;
- premium;
- calm;
- tactile;
- intelligent;
- fast;
- precise;
- dimensional;
- never gimmicky.

The design signature is:
**old-desktop tactile 3D response + modern liquid-glass depth + cinematic natural-light motion + disciplined modern easing.**

---

# 0. MOTION PRINCIPLES

1. Motion must communicate state, hierarchy, causality, or spatial relationship.
2. Nothing moves simply because “animations look cool.”
3. Motion should be fast enough to feel immediate, slow enough to remain legible.
4. The interface should never feel weightless.
5. Important surfaces have believable mass.
6. Small controls travel less than large cards.
7. Glass should refract/brighten subtly as surfaces move through depth.
8. Dragging should feel physically attached to the pointer/finger.
9. Closing/minimizing should preserve spatial continuity.
10. New content should enter from a direction that explains where it came from.
11. Background ambience must stay extremely subtle.
12. HEY's own presence can breathe gently; the rest of the UI should mostly stay still.
13. Motion must stop immediately when interaction demands it.
14. Every long animation must be interruptible.
15. Never delay a user action purely to finish animation.
16. Reduced-motion mode is a first-class variant, not an afterthought.
17. Weak hardware mode reduces blur/parallax/particles before reducing usability.
18. Animations must not block pointer, keyboard, screen-reader, or automation.
19. Loading motion must never imply fake progress.
20. High-risk confirmations use calmer, slower motion than celebratory interactions.

# 1. GLOBAL MOTION TOKENS

## Durations

- `motion-instant`: 80ms
- `motion-micro`: 120ms
- `motion-fast`: 160ms
- `motion-standard`: 240ms
- `motion-medium`: 300ms
- `motion-large`: 420ms
- `motion-panel`: 500ms
- `motion-cinematic`: 700–1200ms
- `motion-tutorial-step`: 700–1600ms depending on demonstration

## Easings

Primary:
`cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1)`

Fast-out:
`cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)`

Press:
`cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1)`

Linear:
only for measurable progress/timeline scrubbers.

Spring:
use physically damped spring for drag release, snapping, widgets, and Dynamic Island morphs.
No bouncy cartoon overshoot.

## Distances

- micro move: 2–4px
- small move: 6–12px
- panel move: 16–24px
- page move: 24–40px
- large spatial transition: 40–80px only when demonstrating hierarchy

## Scale

- hover lift: 1.005–1.015
- press: .985–.995
- modal enter: .975 → 1
- widget pickup: 1 → 1.015
- hero/cinematic: never exceed ~1.08 unless transition specifically requires it

## Blur

- enter blur: max 6–12px for decorative transition only
- never blur text during normal interaction
- use backdrop blur on surfaces, not animated blur filters on every child

# 2. LIQUID-GLASS MOTION LANGUAGE

When a glass surface moves:
- top/left highlight shifts slightly;
- shadow changes with elevation;
- background refraction changes subtly;
- edge specular highlight may travel 4–12px;
- blur amount should remain stable unless moving between depth levels.

Do not:
- animate liquid wobble on every button;
- distort text;
- use exaggerated water ripples;
- make glass bounce.

Approved special liquid morphs:
- Dynamic Island expand/collapse;
- HEY summon;
- mode switch;
- artifact-to-editor transition;
- compact widget → full widget;
- command palette reveal.

Liquid morph duration:
240–420ms.

Shape interpolation must preserve rounded geometry and avoid sudden corner jumps.

# 3. CLASSIC 3D TACTILE CONTROL MOTION

Every tactile button has:

## Hover
- translateY: -1px
- shadow: +10–20% spread/opacity
- top highlight: +8–12%
- duration: 120ms

## Press
- translateY: +1px from rest
- scale: .992
- outer shadow compresses
- inset shadow appears
- duration: 80–100ms

## Release
- return via primary easing
- 120–160ms

## Keyboard activation
Use same pressed visual for 80–100ms.

## Disabled
No hover movement.

## Toggle
Knob moves with spring-like 180–220ms.
Track light shifts after knob begins, not before.

## Segmented control
Selection plate slides under target 180–220ms.
Text/icon color crossfades 120ms.

# 4. PAGE TRANSITIONS

Default page transition:
- outgoing page opacity 1 → .96 over 100ms;
- incoming page opacity 0 → 1;
- incoming translateY 8–12px → 0;
- total 220–280ms.

Sibling pages:
- horizontal 8–16px spatial hint is allowed.

Deep navigation:
- child page moves in from 16–24px right/left depending on direction/RTL.

Back:
- inverse motion.

Do not:
- wipe whole screen;
- use giant zoom;
- spin;
- animate more than 300ms for routine navigation.

Reduced motion:
opacity crossfade 100–160ms only.

# 5. SIDEBAR / NAVIGATION MOTION

Collapsed → expanded:
- width morph: 68px → 244px, 240ms;
- labels fade in after 60ms;
- icons shift 4–8px;
- active pill morphs with container.

Expanded → collapsed:
- label fade first 80ms;
- width closes 220ms.

Active navigation item:
- glass highlight plate slides 160–200ms;
- icon brightens;
- tiny 1px depth lift.

Submenus:
- height expansion 180–220ms;
- child items stagger max 20ms each.

No large accordion bounce.

# 6. TOP BAR / BREADCRUMB MOTION

Title changes:
- old title up 4px + fade out 100ms;
- new title from 4px below + fade in 140ms.

Breadcrumb:
- new segment fades/slides in 120ms.

Context actions:
- appear with 80–120ms opacity;
- never shift page content unexpectedly.

Search field expansion:
- width morph 180–240ms;
- command suggestions fade in after field reaches 60% width.

# 7. MODAL / DRAWER / SHEET MOTION

Modal:
- backdrop 0 → 40–60% opacity, 160ms;
- panel scale .975 → 1;
- translateY 8px → 0;
- 220–280ms.

Close:
- 160–200ms.

Drawer:
- translateX 100% → 0, 260–320ms.
- content inside fades 60ms after drawer begins.

Mobile bottom sheet:
- spring from bottom;
- velocity-sensitive dismissal;
- backdrop crossfade.

High-risk confirmation:
- no bounce;
- calmer 240–320ms.

# 8. TOOLTIP / POPOVER / CONTEXT MENU

Tooltip:
- show delay: ~300ms pointer;
- animation 80–100ms fade + 2px lift;
- disappear 60–80ms.

Popover:
- scale .98 → 1;
- opacity;
- 120–160ms.

Context menu:
- originate visually at pointer;
- scale .97 → 1 around transform origin;
- 100–140ms.

Menu row hover:
- 80ms background/edge response.

# 9. TOAST / NOTIFICATION MOTION

Toast enter:
- desktop: translateX 16px + fade, 220ms;
- mobile: translateY -8px or bottom-sheet style depending placement.

Grouped notifications:
- stack compresses smoothly;
- newest item causes 8–12px stack shift.

Success toast:
- small tactile icon pop 120ms;
- no confetti by default.

Error:
- no aggressive shake.
- use subtle 2px horizontal correction once if needed.

Dismiss:
- opacity + 8px movement 140ms.

# 10. INPUT / PROMPT MOTION

Text field focus:
- border/highlight brightens 120ms;
- subtle inset depth shift;
- no scale jump.

Prompt expansion:
- grows vertically with content 120–180ms;
- toolbar fades in as second line appears.

Attachment:
- chip slides in 160ms;
- upload progress line animates linearly if measurable.

Send:
- icon depresses 80ms;
- message leaves composer with 120–160ms upward movement.

Voice button:
- idle soft pulse every ~2.5s only when voice is available and page context benefits.

# 11. CHAT MOTION

User message:
- enter from 6px below;
- opacity 0 → 1;
- 160ms.

HEY response:
- editorial block fades/settles rather than bubbles in;
- first content appears as soon as available;
- streaming cursor/activity indicator is subtle.

Tool/action status:
- inline chip morphs:
  “Planning” → “Acting” → “Verifying” → “Done”
- state transition 160ms.

Artifact created:
- preview card unfolds from response region;
- 240–320ms;
- clicking it morphs into full artifact viewer/editor.

Do not animate every streamed word independently.

# 12. VOICE VISUALIZER MOTION

Core states:

## Idle
- slow breathing scale 1.0 ↔ 1.015;
- 3.5–5s cycle;
- low brightness.

## Listening
- amplitude reacts to microphone;
- smoothing prevents jitter;
- ring/field expands with voice energy;
- no more than ~8–12% radius excursion.

## Thinking
- motion slows;
- shape becomes more ordered;
- subtle inward/outward energy.

## Speaking
- brighter, more active waveform;
- driven by output audio envelope.

## Interrupted
- visualizer contracts quickly 120–180ms;
- then transitions to listening.

## Muted
- animation dampens;
- indicator becomes clearly muted.

Reduced motion:
- static orb with simple opacity state changes.

# 13. HEY LIVE MOTION

Source switch:
- current source scales to .985 + darkens 120ms;
- new source crossfades 180–240ms;
- source label updates after new source appears.

Pointer guidance:
- outline target in 160ms;
- arrow/path draws over 220ms;
- pulse max 2 times;
- then remains static.

Guide Mode:
- cool neutral highlight.

Assist Mode:
- slightly brighter highlight + prepared action tray.

Act Mode:
- active target receives controlled cyan edge + action cursor.

Screen/camera permission:
- sensing badge slides in 160ms;
- never disappears while active.

Annotations:
- draw in quickly;
- remain until resolved or user clears.

# 14. DYNAMIC ISLAND MOTION

Collapsed idle:
- near-static.

Listening:
- width expands 8–20px;
- waveform appears.

Thinking:
- internal light travels once across surface;
- no continuous spinner if not needed.

Expanded:
- liquid morph from pill to panel;
- 300–420ms spring;
- contents fade in in hierarchy:
  status → primary control → secondary info.

Collapse:
- secondary info fades first;
- shape morphs second.

Progress:
- thin internal progress line.

Success:
- quick check morph;
- return to idle after 1.2–2s.

Error:
- edge shifts to semantic error color;
- no shake.

Cross-monitor move:
- fade from old screen and materialize on target, not animate across physical displays.

# 15. WIDGET MOTION

Create:
- appears at intended spawn location;
- scale .96 → 1;
- opacity 0 → 1;
- 240ms.

Pickup:
- scale 1.015;
- shadow/elevation increases;
- underlying canvas darkens only if necessary.

Drag:
- 1:1 pointer response;
- no easing while directly controlled.

Snap:
- guide appears before drop;
- release spring 180–240ms.

Resize:
- direct response;
- content reflows after threshold;
- avoid jitter by debouncing expensive layout.

Minimize:
- widget collapses toward its dock/taskbar target;
- 220–320ms.

Maximize:
- morph from current bounds to viewport content bounds;
- 300–420ms.

Close:
- opacity + scale .98 over 140–180ms.

Stack:
- cards shift with 160–220ms coordinated motion.

# 16. WORKSPACE MOTION

Workspace mode change:
- do not rearrange everything instantly.
- primary widgets move first;
- secondary widgets settle after;
- total under 500ms.

Auto-layout:
- show ghost positions before move if user initiated.
- user can cancel.

Overview:
- canvas zooms out 4–8%;
- widgets reduce elevation;
- labels appear.

Exit overview:
- restore selected target first.

# 17. PROJECT / CARD / LIST MOTION

Card hover:
- 1px lift;
- subtle thumbnail parallax max 2–3px.

Open project:
- selected card visually becomes header/hero via shared-element transition when performance permits;
- 300–420ms.

List sort:
- FLIP animation;
- 180–260ms.

Filter:
- nonmatching items fade/collapse;
- matching items reposition smoothly.

# 18. COSMOS MOTION

Practical list mode:
- standard list/card transitions only.

Visual Cosmos:
- nodes drift extremely slowly or remain mostly still;
- selected node moves forward in depth;
- connected edges brighten;
- irrelevant nodes dim;
- camera motion is slow and user-controlled.

Zoom:
- inertia small;
- no nausea-inducing acceleration.

New memory:
- subtle node emergence;
- not a dramatic exploding star.

Reduced motion:
- static graph with instant zoom steps.

# 19. IMAGE STUDIO MOTION

Generation:
- placeholder canvas appears immediately;
- status bar stages:
  preparing → generating → QA → complete.
- avoid fake image “painting” unless provider actually streams.

Variant arrival:
- cards fade/scale in 120ms stagger, max 40ms apart.

Selection:
- bounding outline appears 100ms.

Lock:
- lock icon rotates/snaps 90–140ms;
- selected region receives subtle protected outline.

Before/After:
- draggable split with direct response.
- toggle crossfade 120ms.

History branch:
- node expands into tree 220ms.

# 20. STORYBOARD / FRAME MOTION

New shot:
- card inserts in timeline 180ms.

Reorder:
- neighboring cards shift physically out of the way.

Open shot:
- thumbnail morphs to large frame preview.

Continuity warning:
- subtle amber outline/pill;
- no flashing.

Camera parameter changes:
- preview transitions only when actual regenerated/preview data exists.

# 21. VIDEO / MOTION GRAPHICS / AUDIO TIMELINE MOTION

Playhead:
- linear with media time.

Scrubbing:
- immediate direct response.

Clip drag:
- lift + snap lines.

Trim:
- direct edge manipulation.

Generated replacement:
- old clip remains visible until new one verifies;
- then crossfade/replace 180ms.

Waveform:
- do not animate waveform decoratively.

Motion-graphics easing editor:
- curve point movement direct;
- preview can loop only while user requests it.

# 22. PRESENTATION / DOCUMENT MOTION

Slide/page reorder:
- physical card movement.

Slide open:
- thumbnail shared-element transition to canvas.

Presentation playback:
- respect actual chosen transition;
- editor chrome fades away 220ms.

Document page:
- no fake page-turn by default.
- use subtle vertical/page-stack transitions.

Compare revisions:
- diff highlight fades in 120ms.

# 23. RESEARCH MOTION

Source found:
- source card enters 140–180ms.

Evidence status:
- strength badge crossfades.

Research stages:
- plan → searching → reading → synthesizing → verifying.

Do not show hundreds of animated source cards while background research runs.
Use summarized progress.

# 24. FORGE MOTION

Natural-language request:
- prompt collapses into a compact request header.

Forge pipeline:
duplicate check → design → permissions → tests → sandbox → preview → install

Stage transition:
- progress rail advances;
- current panel crossfades/slides 8px;
- completed stage gets tactile check.

Generated capability preview:
- card assembles from sections over 240–320ms.

Install:
- controlled seal/lock-in animation;
- not confetti.

# 25. AUTOMATION MOTION

Node editor:
- connection line draws when linked.
- node drag direct.
- auto-layout uses FLIP transition.

Run:
- current step receives moving 2px edge/rail;
- completed step gets check;
- failed step semantic state.

Paused:
- motion stops.

Test mode:
- simulated values animate through nodes only if readable.

# 26. TASKS / CALENDAR / REMINDERS MOTION

Task complete:
- check depresses;
- title opacity reduces;
- row moves to completed after 180–240ms.

Reorder:
- direct drag.

Calendar event move:
- card follows pointer;
- time indicator tracks.

Reminder snooze:
- card slides to future group.

No celebratory confetti for routine task completion.

# 27. TRUST / PERMISSION MOTION

Grant:
- permission card shifts from neutral → granted;
- lock icon opens/closes appropriately;
- 160–220ms.

Revoke:
- calm controlled transition;
- linked active capability visibly shuts down if applicable.

Stop Everything:
- confirmation modal enters calmly;
- after confirmed, active status indicators switch off in sequence over 300–500ms;
- strong clear final state.

Security alert:
- no flashing red;
- persistent semantic indicator.

# 28. GESTURE FEEDBACK MOTION

When gesture recognition is active:
- small skeleton/hand indicator optional;
- confidence ring appears only in Gesture Studio or debugging, not normal use.

Gesture recognized:
- subtle 100ms highlight;
- action begins.

Drag gesture:
- target follows gesture smoothly with filtering.

Swipe:
- content begins moving with gesture;
- releases with inertia.

Pinch:
- target highlights before activation.

Raised-hand stop:
- HEY speech visualizer contracts immediately.

False/ambiguous gesture:
- do nothing destructive;
- optional tiny “not recognized” indicator, no error spam.

# 29. GESTURE STUDIO TRAINING MOTION

Step 1 — camera activation:
- privacy curtain lifts only after permission.

Step 2 — show reference gesture:
- animated 3D/2D hand demonstration loops slowly.

Step 3 — record sample:
- countdown 3→2→1;
- capture indicator;
- success ring.

Step 4 — repeat:
- sample chips fill progressively.

Step 5 — conflict analysis:
- side-by-side gesture silhouettes.

Step 6 — binding:
- draggable gesture card connects to action card.

Step 7 — test:
- live action preview.

Step 8 — save:
- compact confirmation and tutorial completion.

# 30. ERROR / SUCCESS / PARTIAL SUCCESS MOTION

Success:
- icon morph to check 140–180ms;
- no excessive celebration.

Partial success:
- amber split-state indicator;
- completed items settle first;
- failed items remain visible.

Error:
- panel stays stable;
- semantic edge + icon.
- one 2px correction nudge permitted for invalid form field.

Recovery:
- error state morphs back into progress state rather than disappear/reappear.

# 31. OFFLINE / RECONNECT MOTION

Going offline:
- network badge transitions to offline;
- cloud-only actions subtly disable over 160ms;
- local-capable controls remain.

Reconnect:
- badge restores;
- queued tasks appear;
- do not automatically launch all queued high-cost work without policy.

No full-screen interruption unless active task requires network.

# 32. BACKGROUND / TRAY MOTION

Tray/menu-bar:
- native platform motion where possible.

Main window close while helper remains:
- HEY window fades/scales slightly;
- Dynamic Island remains.

Reopen:
- restore prior workspace with 220–320ms page reveal.

Background mission complete:
- OS notification;
- Island status changes when visible.

# 33. MOBILE MOTION

Use less distance than desktop.

Bottom sheet:
- velocity-responsive spring.

Bottom nav:
- active icon plate moves 160ms.

Swipe back:
- interactive with finger.

Cards:
- no hover.

Haptic:
- light on press;
- snap on drag;
- confirmation;
- error.

Respect OS Reduce Motion.

# 34. TABLET MOTION

Split-pane resize:
- direct.

Panel open:
- 180–240ms.

Widget drag:
- touch-lift after small hold if needed to avoid accidental scroll.

Stylus:
- direct manipulation, minimal animation delay.

# 35. TV / PROJECTOR MOTION

Use:
- larger slower transitions;
- 300–500ms;
- simple fades/slides;
- no small parallax;
- no tiny hover cues.

Gesture-controlled navigation:
- highlight target before activation.

# 36. REDUCED MOTION MASTER RULES

When OS or HEY setting requests reduced motion:

Replace:
- translation >8px → fade;
- zoom → fade;
- parallax → none;
- continuous breathing → static state;
- graph drift → static;
- page shared-element motion → crossfade;
- liquid morph → simple size/fade state;
- tutorial hand/path animations → step-by-step still frames with captions.

Keep:
- essential progress movement;
- focus states;
- pressed state;
- state color changes;
- direct drag response.

# 37. PERFORMANCE MOTION TIERS

## Full
High-end hardware:
- liquid reflections;
- subtle parallax;
- richer shadows;
- background blur.

## Balanced
Default:
- standard blur;
- essential motion;
- limited parallax.

## Lightweight
Weak/battery/thermal:
- reduced blur;
- no ambient parallax;
- static backgrounds;
- simplified shadows;
- fewer layered transitions.

Switching tiers must not visibly redesign layout.

# 39. MICROINTERACTION INVENTORY

## 39.1 — Button hover

**Purpose:** communicate the state change immediately without stealing attention.  
**Default duration:** 80–220ms unless tied to a larger spatial transition.  
**Motion:** use the closest relevant global pattern from Sections 1–37.  
**Sound/haptic:** optional only if the action materially benefits from it.  
**Reduced motion:** opacity/color/depth state only.  
**Verification:** interaction must remain usable if animation is disabled.

**Purpose:** communicate the state change immediately without stealing attention.  
**Default duration:** 80–220ms unless tied to a larger spatial transition.  
**Motion:** use the closest relevant global pattern from Sections 1–37.  
**Sound/haptic:** optional only if the action materially benefits from it.  
**Reduced motion:** opacity/color/depth state only.  
**Verification:** interaction must remain usable if animation is disabled.
