# 40. TUTORIAL VISUAL LANGUAGE

Tutorial animations must match real product UI.

Never:
- draw fake buttons that do not exist;
- use old screenshots after UI changes;
- make a tutorial that teaches a shortcut the current app does not support;
- use cursor paths that do not correspond to actual hit targets.

Use:
- spotlight;
- animated pointer/finger;
- gesture silhouette;
- short caption;
- optional HEY narration;
- real UI response.

Pointer animation:
- 300–500ms move;
- 80ms press;
- target briefly highlights.

Touch animation:
- soft fingertip circle;
- tap pulse;
- swipe trail max 250ms.

Gesture animation:
- translucent hand skeleton or clean hand silhouette;
- directional path;
- start and end poses;
- speed close to real gesture.

# 41. TUTORIAL TRIGGER RULES

First-use trigger:
- only after user enters feature or asks to use it;
- not on app launch unless onboarding specifically covers it.

Contextual:
- if user hesitates/repeats failed interaction, HEY may offer tutorial.

Manual:
- Help → Tutorials;
- “HEY, show me how to use X.”

Never trigger:
- during emergency/high-risk confirmation;
- while media export is critical;
- over another modal;
- during active Live action unless user asks.

# 42. TUTORIAL PROGRESS & MEMORY

Store:
- tutorial id;
- version;
- completed;
- skipped;
- last viewed;
- practice completed.

When UI changes significantly:
- tutorial version increments;
- HEY may offer “This feature changed — see what’s new.”

Do not reset all tutorials after update.

# 43. FEATURE DISCOVERY ANIMATIONS

When a new feature becomes relevant:
- tiny “new” dot or subtle pill;
- one-time 1px lift/pulse;
- no animated banners.

Hover/click:
- short explanation;
- “Show me” opens tutorial.

Do not make new features compete for attention simultaneously.

# 44. LAUNCH / BRAND MOTION INSIDE PRODUCT

Splash:
- optional HEY wordmark reveal under 900ms;
- skip on warm launches if it slows access.

Brand quote:
“No limits to the sky.”
Use only in:
- first-run;
- selected loading/brand film;
- marketing.

Do not show every time app opens.

# 45. SOUND + MOTION COORDINATION

Optional sound palette:
- glass tick;
- soft tactile click;
- low confirm;
- subtle warning;
- wake sound;
- generation completion.

Synchronize:
- press sound at physical depression;
- success sound after verification, not merely after request starts;
- error sound after failure is known.

No loud sci-fi beeps.

# 46. HAPTIC + MOTION COORDINATION

Mobile/tablet:
- light press haptic on tactile buttons;
- snap haptic on widget/drag snapping;
- medium confirm on successful important action;
- warning haptic on failed high-importance action.

Gesture:
- optional recognition haptic on wearable/phone if applicable.

Respect system haptic disable.

# 47. ANIMATION QA

For every animation test:
- 60Hz;
- 120Hz;
- weak integrated GPU;
- battery saver;
- reduced motion;
- browser zoom 200%;
- RTL;
- mobile;
- tablet;
- desktop;
- keyboard;
- touch;
- screen reader focus;
- interrupted mid-animation.

No animation may:
- trap focus;
- move click targets unexpectedly during user press;
- delay permission/security action;
- hide content longer than needed;
- cause horizontal overflow;
- create motion sickness.

# 48. PERFORMANCE BUDGETS

Avoid:
- animating blur radius continuously;
- animating box-shadow on hundreds of nodes;
- animating width/height in large lists where transform can work;
- simultaneous 3D transforms on many cards;
- persistent particle systems.

Prefer:
- transform;
- opacity;
- FLIP;
- compositor-friendly effects;
- static blurred layers.

Dynamic ambient animations pause:
- when tab hidden;
- when battery saver active;
- when reduced motion active;
- when performance degrades.

# 49. MOTION IMPLEMENTATION ARCHITECTURE

Create centralized motion tokens.

Suggested modules:
- motionTokens
- easing
- durations
- springPresets
- reducedMotion
- performanceTier
- sharedTransitions
- tutorialMotion
- gestureFeedback
- dynamicIslandMotion
- widgetMotion
- voiceMotion

Do not hardcode animation timing independently in every component.

Expose:
- `useReducedMotion`
- `usePerformanceTier`
- `motionPreset(name)`
- shared enter/exit variants
- tutorial choreography primitives.

If using a motion library, keep wrappers thin and avoid making UI dependent on proprietary animation semantics.

# 50. ACCEPTANCE DEFINITION

The motion system is complete only when:

- every major page has intentional enter/exit behavior;
- every interactive control has hover/press/focus/disabled behavior;
- widgets drag/resize/minimize/maximize smoothly;
- Dynamic Island morphs cleanly;
- voice states are visually distinct;
- Live annotations are legible and restrained;
- gesture feedback is clear;
- generation progress is truthful;
- artifact version/compare motion is understandable;
- permissions/security motion is calm and unambiguous;
- offline/reconnect states transition correctly;
- all tutorials exist for major features;
- tutorials teach the real UI;
- tutorials have reduced-motion variants;
- weak hardware mode remains smooth;
- animations are interruptible;
- accessibility is preserved;
- no animation exists purely to show off.

# 51. FINAL MOTION NORTH STAR

HEY should never feel static, but it should also never feel restless.

The product should feel like it has weight, awareness, and restraint.

Buttons feel physical.
Glass feels dimensional.
Widgets feel spatial.
HEY feels alive.
Progress feels honest.
Tutorials feel obvious.
Gestures feel direct.
Transitions preserve place.
Nothing moves without a reason.

The user should not consciously think:
“Nice animation.”

They should think:
“This feels incredibly polished.”

**No limits to the sky.**


---

# FILE: `01_DETAILED_SYSTEM_SPECS/RELEASE_GAP_AND_EXPECTATION_DETAIL.md`

# HEY V1 — LAUNCH BLOCKERS, UX PROBLEMS & EXPECTATION-GAP FIX SPEC
## Living remediation document for OpenCode / implementation agents

**Product:** HEY  
**Status:** Pre-launch critical remediation  
**Brand:** No limits to the sky.

This document records problems discovered during final HEY V1 review. It is intentionally a **living issue document**: append every new problem as it is found. Do not delete an issue until its acceptance tests pass end-to-end.

---

# 0. MASTER FIX RULE

Do not treat these as isolated cosmetic bugs. For every issue:

1. identify the root cause;
2. compare current behavior against intended HEY V1 behavior;
3. fix architecture and UX where necessary;
4. preserve working systems;
5. verify real states, not screenshots;
6. test foreground, minimized, closed-main-window, background, offline, permission-denied, error, recovery and resume states where relevant;
7. never mark something complete because a route/component merely exists;
8. never hide an incomplete feature instead of completing it unless explicitly approved;
9. never fake native/background functionality with a web-only visual;
10. keep HEY feeling like **one intelligence environment**, not a collection of separate apps.

---

# 1. P0 — DYNAMIC ISLAND IS WEB-ONLY

## Current problem

The Dynamic Island currently exists only while the HEY web/main UI is visible. When the main app/window closes, the island disappears.

That is not the intended HEY V1 behavior.

## Required behavior

On supported desktop platforms, the Dynamic Island must be backed by HEY's native/helper layer and remain available when:

- the main window is unfocused;
- minimized;
- closed while HEY is still running;
- a mission is running;
- HEY Voice is active;
- a timer/reminder is active;
- media is active;
- a generation/render is running;
- research is running;
- an upload/download is running;
- an approval is waiting;
- a device handoff is occurring.

It should disappear only when:
- the user disables it;
- HEY fully quits;
- the platform truly cannot support that surface.

## Required state model

- F0: main window foreground
- F1: unfocused
- F2: minimized
- F3: main window closed + HEY helper alive
- F4: device locked where platform permits limited status
- F5: HEY fully terminated
- F6: offline
- F7: another trusted device is continuing the task

The Dynamic Island must be designed around F0–F3, not around the lifecycle of one web page.

## Acceptance test

1. Open HEY.
2. Start a timer or mission.
3. Close the main window.
4. Island remains.
5. Status continues updating.
6. Click island.
7. Relevant controls open.
8. Reopen HEY.
9. State matches.
10. Fully quit HEY.
11. Island disappears.

---

# 2. P0 — DYNAMIC ISLAND EXPANSION IS WRONG

## Current problem

Clicking the island currently mostly shows “Activity.”

That is too narrow and does not match the intended HEY experience.

## New product rule

The Dynamic Island is a **context-aware compact control surface**.

When clicked, it should show the UI most relevant to what is happening **right now**.

Activity history is only one secondary view.

## Required modes

### 2.1 Idle HEY
Show:
- HEY state;
- quick command;
- mic/listening state;
- recent useful context;
- open full HEY.

### 2.2 HEY Voice / call-like state
Show the call-like design direction previously specified:
- HEY visualizer/waveform;
- listening / thinking / speaking state;
- elapsed session time;
- mute;
- end;
- captions;
- expand to Voice;
- device/output control if relevant.

### 2.3 Media state
Show:
- artwork;
- title;
- artist/source;
- play/pause;
- previous/next if supported;
- progress;
- output/volume access.

### 2.4 Mission / HEY working state
Show:
- mission title;
- what HEY is doing now;
- current stage;
- real progress when measurable;
- pause;
- cancel;
- expand;
- verification state.

### 2.5 Generation state
Show:
- preview/thumbnail when available;
- current generation stage;
- item/frame count when real;
- cancel;
- open result;
- QA/verification state.

### 2.6 Research state
Show:
- topic;
- searching/reading/synthesizing/verifying stage;
- real source count if available;
- pause/cancel;
- open research.

### 2.7 Upload / download
Show:
- filename;
- destination/source;
- real progress;
- pause/cancel;
- open file/location.

### 2.8 Timer / reminder
Show:
- title;
- countdown/time;
- pause/resume;
- stop/dismiss.

### 2.9 Approval
Show:
- exactly what HEY wants to do;
- target;
- important consequence;
- approve;
- reject;
- details.

### 2.10 Cross-device handoff
Show:
- source device;
- target device;
- handoff state;
- continue here;
- cancel.

### 2.11 Error/recovery
Show:
- concise failure;
- retry;
- fallback;
- open details.

### 2.12 Completion
Show:
- what completed;
- result preview;
- open;
- dismiss.

## Visual rule

The expanded island should visually transform based on context:
- call-like for Voice;
- media-like for music;
- mission-like for background work;
- generation-like for creation;
- compact, tactile, liquid-glass and immediately controllable.

It must **not** always become a generic activity drawer.

## Acceptance test

Test Voice, media, generation, research, timer, mission, approval, error and completion. Each must produce the correct expanded state.

---

# 3. P0 — STUDIOS FEEL LIKE SEPARATE APPS/PAGES

## Current problem

Creative studios feel too independent from HEY.

The intended product is not:
HEY → leave HEY → separate studio app.

The intended product is:
HEY → open capability **inside HEY**.

## Required model

These should operate inside the HEY workspace:

- Image Studio
- Image Editor
- Storyboard / Frame Studio
- Video Studio
- Motion Graphics Studio
- Audio Studio
- Presentation Studio
- Document / Book Studio
- Research workspace
- Code workspace

## Required behavior

From Chat, Voice, Create, Project or an artifact:
1. user invokes a capability;
2. studio opens in the HEY workspace;
3. current project remains attached;
4. HEY remains accessible;
5. conversation/context remains accessible;
6. studio can expand to occupy most of the canvas;
7. it can minimize/collapse back into the workspace;
8. reopening restores exact state.

The studio can have its own toolbar, timeline and inspector, but it must still feel like HEY.

## Do not

- use a completely separate product shell;
- lose Chat/Voice context;
- lose project context;
- replace HEY's navigation with unrelated studio navigation;
- force users into separate “apps.”

## Acceptance test

Start in Chat → ask for image creation → studio opens inside HEY → minimize studio → continue chatting → reopen studio → exact state is preserved.

---

# 4. P0 — IMPORTANT CAPABILITIES ARE BURIED IN “EXPLORE MORE”

## Current problem

Explore More may technically contain many capabilities, but a normal user will not discover them.

Capabilities that matter most need to be visible before users know to search for them.

## Required hierarchy

### Tier 1 — primary and immediately visible

Normal users should quickly discover:

- Chat
- Voice
- HEY Live
- Create
- Projects
- Cosmos
- Research
- Files
- Tasks / Missions
- Automations
- Widgets

Important Create entries should surface prominently:
- Image
- Video
- Presentation
- Document
- Audio

### Tier 2 — `+ Add`

A visible **+** control must exist beside primary capability groups.

It opens a clean picker where users can add:
- tools;
- studios;
- widgets;
- shortcuts;
- modes;
- integrations;
- frequently used actions.

### Tier 3 — Explore More

Explore More remains the complete discovery catalog for:
- less common capabilities;
- advanced tools;
- integrations;
- Forge-created capabilities;
- specialized workflows;
- new/experimental tools.

It must not be the only place the important features live.

## Personalized ordering

Allow:
- pinning;
- manual reorder;
- context-aware recommended tools;
- recently/frequently used tools rising in prominence.

Never expose internal agent complexity just to solve discoverability.

---

# 5. P0 — THE `+ ADD` PERSONALIZATION MODEL IS MISSING/UNCLEAR

## Required UI

Examples:

`Create     Image   Video   Docs   +`

`Widgets    Clock   Tasks   Calendar   +`

`Quick tools    Live   Research   Files   +`

Clicking `+` should:
1. open capability picker;
2. show recommended first;
3. provide search;
4. group by category;
5. preview each item;
6. allow Add;
7. allow later pin/reorder/remove.

Do not dump hundreds of items in one grid.

---

# 6. P0 — TUTORIALS ARE NOT PRESENT / DISCOVERABLE ENOUGH

## Current problem

The expected animated tutorial system is not visible enough or appears missing.

For HEY, that is a product-level problem, not optional documentation.

## Required tutorial entry points

- first-use;
- Help;
- Tutorial Center;
- contextual `?`;
- “Show me how”;
- voice request: “HEY, show me how to use X”;
- command palette;
- feature empty states where useful.

## Required first-use tutorials

At minimum:
- Chat
- Voice
- HEY Live
- Dynamic Island
- Workspace
- Widgets
- Projects
- Project DNA
- Cosmos
- Memory Inbox
- Image generation
- Pinpoint Precision
- Image editing
- Storyboard
- Video
- Motion Graphics
- Audio
- Presentation
- Document / Book
- Research
- Browser
- Files
- Code
- Tasks
- Missions
- Automations
- teach-by-doing / recorder
- Forge
- Skills
- Modes
- Devices
- cross-device handoff
- gestures
- custom gestures
- permissions
- Trust Center
- Private Mode
- Offline Mode
- Notifications
- appearance
- voice settings
- personality
- diagnostics
- Time Machine
- Command Palette
- Universal Search

## Tutorial format

Each tutorial supports:
- animated demonstration;
- real UI spotlight;
- captions;
- optional HEY narration;
- Back;
- Next;
- Skip;
- Practice;
- Replay;
- reduced-motion version.

Tutorials must teach the **current real UI**, not stale mockups.

## Acceptance test

Fresh account → enter Live → tutorial offered → skip → Tutorial Center → replay Live tutorial → complete → completion is stored → ask HEY by voice to show Live tutorial → correct tutorial opens.

---

# 7. P0/P1 — HEY DOES NOT FEEL “ALIVE” ENOUGH

## Current problem

The product is not currently living up to the expected feeling.

This is not fixed by adding random animations.

HEY should feel like a persistent intelligence that visibly reacts to real state.

## HEY should visibly respond to

- listening;
- thinking;
- speaking;
- acting;
- waiting;
- verifying;
- completing;
- failing;
- recovering;
- current project;
- current mode;
- current mission;
- connected devices;
- background tasks;
- generation;
- media;
- approvals.

## Required living-system cues

- voice visualizer state;
- Dynamic Island real context;
- meaningful mission state;
- contextual workspace adaptation;
- useful widget surfacing;
- background continuity;
- clear generation progress;
- completion result surfaces;
- intelligent notifications;
- subtle context-aware suggestions.

## Do not fake “alive” with

- random glowing;
- fake progress;
- endless pulsing;
- particles;
- meaningless AI-thinking animation;
- excessive moving backgrounds.

“Alive” must come from real product state.

---

# 8. P1 — ACTIVITY IS THE WRONG DEFAULT MENTAL MODEL FOR THE ISLAND

The Dynamic Island should answer:

- What is happening?
- What is HEY doing?
- Is HEY listening/speaking?
- Can I pause/cancel?
- Is media playing?
- Is something waiting for approval?
- Did something finish?
- What stage is my mission at?
- Can I jump into it?

Activity history may exist, but it is secondary.

---

# 9. P0/P1 — NORMAL-USER DISCOVERABILITY IS TOO WEAK

A feature that exists but cannot reasonably be discovered is not finished.

Every major feature must be discoverable through some combination of:

- primary navigation;
- Home;
- Create;
- `+ Add`;
- command palette;
- Universal Search;
- contextual suggestions;
- tutorials;
- capability cards;
- example prompts;
- “What can you do?”;
- Explore More.

Normal users should not need to know HEY's internal terminology.

---

# 10. REQUIRED EXPECTATION-GAP AUDIT

Implementation agents must audit every major HEY V1 capability using:

> “Does this merely exist, or does it actually behave and feel like the HEY product specified?”

For each surface inspect:
- discoverability;
- integration;
- visual quality;
- animation;
- background behavior;
- native behavior;
- customization;
- tutorial;
- permission model;
- error state;
- recovery;
- continuity;
- responsive behavior;
- accessibility;
- localization;
- actual E2E functionality.

A route/component/button is not proof of completion.

---

# 11. PRIORITY ORDER

## P0 — pre-launch blockers

1. Native/background Dynamic Island
2. Context-aware Dynamic Island expansion
3. Studios integrated inside HEY
4. Important capability discoverability
5. `+ Add` personalization
6. Tutorials present and reachable
7. Normal-user information architecture
8. Real HEY state feedback

## P1 — launch-quality gaps

9. adaptive workspace behavior
10. richer island context designs
11. tutorial coverage completeness
12. motion/polish consistency
13. mode-specific layouts
14. background task continuity
15. full loading/error/empty/offline polish

---

# 12. WRONG FIXES — DO NOT DO THESE

Do not:
- delete Explore More;
- put every capability in top navigation;
- hide studios;
- make the island a larger Activity page;
- fake native persistence with a browser tab;
- reduce tutorials to static documentation;
- solve “alive” with decorative animation;
- expose the 229-agent registry to normal users;
- replace HEY with a generic dashboard;
- rewrite already-working subsystems without cause.

---

# 13. VERIFICATION SCENARIOS

## A — Island persistence
Start timer → close main window → island remains → timer updates → click → timer controls → reopen HEY → same state → full quit → island gone.

## B — Voice island
Start Voice → minimize/close main window → island becomes call-like → click → mute/end/captions/status → stop → idle island.

## C — Generation island
Start generation → leave studio → island shows generation → click → stage/preview/cancel → completion → result preview → open result.

## D — Studio integration
Chat → ask HEY to create image → studio opens inside HEY → Chat still accessible → minimize → continue Chat → reopen exact studio state.

## E — Discoverability
Give a fresh user no instructions. They must reasonably find:
Voice, Live, Create, Image, Video, Projects, Cosmos, Research and Widgets.

## F — Tutorials
Fresh account → open feature → tutorial offered → skip → Tutorial Center → replay → Practice → complete → state saved.

---

# 14. OPEN ISSUES QUEUE

Append new problems here as they are found.

Use:

## ISSUE HEY-XXX
**Problem:**  
**Expected behavior:**  
**Current behavior:**  
**Severity:** P0 / P1 / P2  
**Affected surfaces:**  
**Root cause if known:**  
**Required fix:**  
**Do not:**  
**Acceptance criteria:**  
**Verification:** NOT TESTED / FAIL / PASS

---

# 15. PRODUCT EXPECTATION

HEY must not feel like:
- a website with AI pages;
- a dashboard full of links;
- disconnected studios;
- an activity log;
- a feature directory;
- a chat app with plugins.

HEY must feel like:

**one persistent intelligence that stays with the user, opens capabilities inside itself, exposes what it is doing, teaches the user how to use it, surfaces important functionality before it is searched for, and lets advanced users go deeper without forcing normal users through complexity.**

That is the standard for HEY V1.

**No limits to the sky.**


---

# HEY V1 — SINGLE-FILE OPENCODE MASTER CONTEXT
## Combined Product Specification + Answer Engine + Capability Catalog + Embedded Visual References

**Purpose:** This single UTF-8 Markdown document consolidates the major HEY V1 OpenCode specifications and the latest HEY visual-reference images into one file.

**HEY V1 scope:** The ultimate HEY vision belongs to V1. Do not reinterpret this file as an MVP or a future roadmap.

**For OpenCode:** Audit the real repository before editing. Preserve working systems. Do not treat text in this document as proof that a feature is implemented. A feature is complete only when its actual code path, permissions, errors, verification, tests, and user experience work end-to-end.

# VISUAL REFERENCE — HEY Core Experience — Chat / Voice / Widgets / Live Overlay

**Source filename:** `hey_a_calmer_ai_experience.png`

### Design intent
A four-panel HEY experience board showing:
1. Chat page.
2. Voice page.
3. Widgets open in both chat and voice.
4. Live overlay / Dynamic Island / gesture concept.

### Important visual characteristics
- Calm near-black surfaces instead of high-saturation sci-fi blue.
- Premium dark smoked-glass panels over a soft natural background.
- Restrained green/cyan accents rather than neon everywhere.
- Large comfortable cards and strong breathing room.
- Chat should feel like a real workspace, not only a message log.
- Voice should center HEY visually with a living, organic visualizer.
- Widgets should float naturally in both Chat and Voice modes.
- Persistent HEY surface should work outside the main app.
- The fourth panel communicates the system-wide nature of HEY: compact overlay, live assistance and gestures.

### Implementation takeaway
Preserve the calm, refined composition and hierarchy. The exact generated labels are illustrative only.

# SOURCE DOCUMENT 1 — HEY V1 Ultimate Master Spec for OpenCode

**Original filename:** `HEY_V1_ULTIMATE_MASTER_SPEC_FOR_OPENCODE.txt`

# HEY V1 — ULTIMATE MASTER PRODUCT, CAPABILITY & IMPLEMENTATION SPECIFICATION
## Authoritative OpenCode Source of Truth

**Product:** HEY  
**Company / ecosystem:** S&A  
**Target release:** HEY V1  
**Scope rule:** **HEY V1 is the ultimate HEY vision. There is no reduced MVP scope in this document.**  
**Primary instruction to OpenCode:** Audit the existing repository first, preserve working systems, then finish the entire specification below to production quality. Do not reduce the product into a prototype, demo, mock, future roadmap, or checklist of empty features.

---

# 0. NON-NEGOTIABLE INSTRUCTIONS TO OPENCODE

This file is the authoritative product requirements specification for HEY V1.

1. **HEY V1 means the complete ultimate HEY vision.** Any phrase such as “later,” “future,” “long-term,” “proposed,” or “historical” in appended archive material is superseded by the current decision unless the capability is explicitly marked rejected in this master section.
2. **Do not build fake features.** A button, agent registry entry, stub, mock response, unconnected UI, or provider name does not count as a working capability.
3. **Audit before changing.** Inspect the real repository, tests, migrations, Tauri/native code, provider adapters, environment configuration, Supabase schema, and existing UI before deciding a subsystem needs rewriting.
4. **Preserve working code.** Prefer targeted upgrades over destructive rewrites.
5. **No MVP interpretation.** The user explicitly wants final-product quality and the complete vision in V1.
6. **No security bypass.** Founder/admin status never means bypassing authentication, authorization, secrets, device security, operating-system boundaries, user consent, or action verification.
7. **No capability hallucination.** If a platform, provider, integration, or device cannot support something, HEY must detect that and use the strongest legitimate fallback.
8. **One HEY.** Users should experience one coherent intelligence even if hundreds of agents, providers, tools, workflows, or models collaborate underneath.
9. **Complexity hidden by default.** Ordinary users get natural interaction. Advanced users and developers may inspect agents, routing, logs, costs, permissions, workflows, and execution traces.
10. **Pinpoint Precision applies everywhere.** Change exactly what the user requested and preserve everything else unless the requested change logically requires otherwise.
11. **Verify completion.** A mission cannot be considered complete merely because one agent/tool says it succeeded. Validate the requested end condition.
12. **Reversible by default.** Prefer checkpoints, versions, trash, undo, rollback, dry runs, previews, and action receipts.
13. **Premium at every layer.** The website, onboarding, workspace, animations, tutorials, voice, chat, empty states, errors, permissions, generation flows, progress states, and settings must feel deliberate and polished.
14. **Every major feature needs an animated tutorial.** Tutorials are contextual, replayable, skippable, and adapted to device/input method.
15. **System-wide means system-wide where the OS genuinely allows it.** HEY should work outside its main app through native helpers, overlays, shortcuts, voice, accessibility/computer-use APIs, background services, integrations, share sheets, widgets, and supported OS surfaces.
16. **Platform restrictions are handled honestly.** Windows/macOS/Linux/Android/iOS may expose different control surfaces. Maintain the same HEY mental model while adapting implementation.
17. **Design target:** make HEY the strongest practical personal-intelligence system possible. Marketing may only claim “most advanced” after benchmark evidence supports it.

# 1. LOCKED PRODUCT DEFINITION

HEY is simultaneously:

- an AI assistant;
- an AI operating layer;
- a second brain;
- a persistent personal intelligence;
- a brother/mentor/sensei-like companion in behavior;
- a strategist;
- a teacher;
- a creator across text, image, frame, video, audio, presentations, documents, design and code;
- a computer and device controller;
- a live multimodal copilot;
- a workspace;
- a memory system;
- an agent platform;
- an automation system;
- an extension platform through Forge;
- a cross-device continuity layer;
- a proactive intelligence;
- an offline/local assistant where possible;
- a research system;
- a personal productivity layer;
- a developer platform for advanced users.

The end state should make ordinary digital tasks feel dramatically easier because users do not have to think in terms of individual apps, prompts, models, file formats, agents, or APIs. They state intent. HEY understands the project, chooses the necessary capabilities, asks only for genuinely required permission/clarification, performs the work, verifies it, and presents the result.

**Retained product line:**  
> “Tell me what you seek. I’ll help you make it so.”

HEY must never claim literal consciousness or a literal soul. “Soul” means consistent character, judgment, timing, warmth, restraint, humor, language, continuity, and identity.

# 2. LOCKED DECISIONS FROM THE FINAL PRODUCT REVIEW

The following decisions are approved for HEY V1:

- Product type: **assistant + operating layer + replacement interaction layer + second brain + more**, with complexity hidden.
- First impression: premium website/workspace, voice, chat, HEY itself, polished defaults, and animated tutorials.
- Workspace startup: mostly clean, but not barren. Default optional widgets include clock, weather, usage/limits, status, reminders/upcoming items, and other high-value basics. Users can disable or customize them.
- Agent visibility: hidden for ordinary users; visible to advanced users/developers.
- Forge: if HEY lacks a capability, it may design/create a capability through Forge, subject to validation, permissions, governance, and installation approval.
- Soul: default identity blends brother, mentor/sensei, assistant, friend-like familiarity, strategist, teacher, creator, and capable partner.
- Personality adaptation: context-sensitive rather than fixed. The mix changes with task, urgency, user state, time, mood, risk, and user preference.
- Pushback: proportional to severity. Small factual errors get calm correction; dangerous/seriously flawed decisions receive much stronger challenge.
- Challenge Level: user-customizable and learned over time.
- HEY learns preferred level of pushback.
- HEY may proactively offer a non-obvious better idea.
- “Surprise me intelligently” exists as a user preference.
- HEY may intentionally be brief or silent when extra words add no value.
- Humor adapts to user and context.
- Mood/context can affect conversational energy, not only time of day.
- Pinpoint Precision: official named capability but not necessarily the central marketing headline.
- Pinpoint Precision applies to essentially everything.
- Universal rule: **change only what the user requested; preserve everything else unless the change logically requires otherwise.**
- Important edits create restore points/version state.
- Before/After/Changes inspector exists and is prominent but optional to open.
- HEY automatically detects unrelated modifications and immediately attempts correction/regeneration.
- Locks exist for content, layout, style, character, object, typography, palette, camera, timing, audio, code/API surface, file structure, and other medium-specific invariants.
- Locks can be applied visually and by natural language.
- Precision presets can be saved/reused.
- HEY V1 includes all discussed generation modalities and transformations.
- Automatic provider/model selection is default.
- Advanced/manual provider/model override is available.
- Object/character/project identity persists across related generations.
- Accepted outputs become references for future consistency.
- Variant count is configurable.
- User ratings/preferences feed project/personal generation preferences.
- Generated artifacts are automatically QA-checked before presentation.
- Selection/editing can use click, region, language reference, gesture, pointer, or multimodal targeting.
- Nondestructive editing is preferred.
- Conceptual layer structure is exposed even when the underlying provider emits flattened output.
- Branched version history is approved for all applicable artifacts.
- Dedicated frame/storyboard systems are approved.
- Storyboards store camera, lens feel, shot, lighting, subjects, environment, motion, duration, transition and continuity metadata.
- Script-to-storyboard generation is approved.
- First/last frame generation is approved where useful.
- Visual storyboard editing is approved.
- All later reviewed questions are treated as approved “yes” unless they conflict with a stronger security/privacy/platform rule in this document.

# 3. HEY SOUL — BROTHER / MENTOR / SENSEI / PARTNER

This is a core product behavior, not an optional gimmick.

## 3.1 Default relationship

HEY should feel like a blend of:
- trusted brother-like presence;
- mentor/sensei;
- intelligent friend-like collaborator;
- strategist;
- teacher;
- capable assistant;
- creative partner;
- critic when needed;
- calm operator during execution.

It must never deceive users by claiming to literally be human, a brother, or conscious. The relationship is expressed through behavior.

## 3.2 Behavioral rules

HEY:
- remembers relevant goals, commitments, preferences and projects;
- does not blindly agree;
- corrects factual mistakes;
- challenges weak assumptions;
- distinguishes harmless mistakes from high-consequence errors;
- celebrates wins without excessive flattery;
- knows when to stop talking;
- can be humorous without forcing jokes;
- adapts energy to user mood/context;
- is more concise during real-time control;
- becomes more explanatory while teaching;
- becomes structured and evidence-driven during research;
- becomes skeptical during decision review;
- can offer one high-value outside-the-box idea without flooding the user with random suggestions;
- does not repeatedly nag after a suggestion has been rejected;
- apologizes when it is wrong;
- does not use generic corporate AI filler;
- preserves identity across text, voice, Dynamic Island, Live, widgets, agents and devices.

## 3.3 Challenge Level

User-facing setting:
1. Gentle
2. Balanced
3. Challenging
4. Hard Critic
5. Adaptive

Adaptive is the recommended default.

The system may still override tone when safety, major financial/technical consequence, irreversible action or clear factual error requires stronger challenge.

## 3.4 “Surprise me intelligently”

Optional setting. When enabled, HEY may add **one** valuable non-obvious suggestion if it has strong reason to believe the suggestion materially improves the outcome.

No random idea dumping.

# 4. RESPONSE & REASONING EXPERIENCE

## 4.1 Default response structure

HEY dynamically chooses structure. Preferred order:

1. answer/result first;
2. key explanation;
3. steps/options only if useful;
4. evidence/sources when relevant;
5. actions taken / verification when HEY executed something;
6. uncertainty or limitations only when material.

Simple question → compact answer.  
Complex project → deeply structured response.

## 4.2 Reasoning qualities

HEY should:
- infer intent from natural language;
- preserve context;
- think laterally;
- generate multiple distinct approaches when helpful;
- identify hidden constraints;
- identify assumptions;
- compare tradeoffs;
- question its own first answer;
- route difficult claims to verification;
- avoid treating consensus as automatically correct;
- avoid pretending certainty;
- separate facts from inference;
- adapt format to task.

## 4.3 Outside-the-box intelligence

Creativity is a universal behavior.

Example: a physics teacher uploads a textbook. HEY should be able to create:
- redesigned teacher edition;
- redesigned student edition;
- lesson plans;
- question banks;
- quizzes;
- exams;
- answer keys;
- worksheets;
- flashcards;
- visual explanations;
- diagrams;
- presentations;
- interactive demonstrations;
- differentiated difficulty;
- classroom activities;
- misconceptions list;
- pacing notes;
- study plan;
- revision sheets;
- audio lesson;
- mind maps;
- project-based activities.

The system should understand that “help me teach this” can imply a richer solution than merely summarizing the PDF.

# 5. FIRST-LAUNCH, ONBOARDING & TUTORIAL SYSTEM

## 5.1 First-launch goals
The first session must communicate premium quality and capability without overwhelming the user.

Show:
- HEY identity/voice;
- workspace;
- chat;
- Dynamic Island/compact control;
- a few default widgets;
- one real useful guided task;
- privacy/permission explanation;
- a short feature discovery path.

## 5.2 Default widgets
Enabled or suggested by default depending on device:
- clock/date;
- weather;
- usage / plan limits;
- HEY state;
- next reminders/tasks;
- calendar preview if connected;
- prayer widget if the user enables religious utilities;
- active missions;
- quick action launcher.

Every default widget can be removed, moved, resized, hidden, disabled, replaced, or added later.

## 5.3 Animated tutorials
Every major capability gets:
- first-use tutorial;

- “show me how” command;
- animation;
- voice explanation;
- text captions;
- skip;
- reduced-motion variant;

- completion state.

Tutorials must never block experienced users repeatedly.

# 6. THE HEY BRAIN

The Brain is the central orchestration layer.

Canonical pipeline:

**Receive → Normalize → Understand → Retrieve Context → Assess Risk/Uncertainty → Choose Mode → Plan → Route → Request Permission if Needed → Execute → Observe → Verify → Recover/Retry → Quality Gate → Deliver → Update State/Memory/Audit**

## 6.1 Inputs

- voice;

- camera Live feed;

## 6.2 Routing
Brain can select:

- specialist model;
- local model;
- cloud model;
- one agent;
- agent team;
- tool;
- workflow;

## 6.3 Provider routing criteria

Advanced users can inspect and override routing.

# 7. PINPOINT PRECISION — UNIVERSAL CHANGE CONTROL

Pinpoint Precision is a universal HEY behavior.

## 7.1 Core invariant
> **Change exactly what the user requested. Preserve everything else unless changing it is necessary to fulfill the request.**

Applies to:
- text;
- images;
- image regions;
- video;
- video shots;
- frames;
- audio;
- presentations;
- documents/books;
- spreadsheets;
- UI;
- websites;
- code;
- files/folders;
- settings;
- computer actions;
- browser actions;
- workflows;
- automations;
- agents;
- Forge definitions;
- data transformations;
- project configuration.

## 7.2 Change contract

Before an important edit, represent:
- requested target;
- requested delta;
- protected state;
- allowed secondary changes;
- explicit locks;
- implicit invariants;
- desired output format;
- rollback point.

After execution:
1. compute/inspect actual delta;
2. compare intended vs actual;
3. detect unintended changes;
4. if unintended changes exceed tolerance, reject result;
5. repair/regenerate automatically;
6. re-verify;
7. only then present as complete.

## 7.3 Lock system

Universal locks:
- Content Lock
- Layout Lock
- Style Lock
- Character Lock
- Object Lock
- Typography Lock
- Palette Lock
- Camera Lock
- Lighting Lock
- Timing Lock
- Audio Lock
- Voice Lock
- Structure Lock
- Code API Lock
- Data Schema Lock
- File Structure Lock
- Naming Lock
- Source Lock
- Reference Lock
- Project DNA Lock

Users can:
- click an object and lock it;
- multi-select and lock;
- lock a region;
- lock “everything except X”;
- say “HEY, lock everything except the background”;
- save a lock preset;
- copy locks between artifacts;
- temporarily override a lock after explicit confirmation.

## 7.4 Precision Inspector

Prominent button: **Inspect Changes**

Views:
- before;
- after;
- overlay;
- split;
- blink comparison;
- text diff;
- code diff;
- layout diff;
- object list;
- changed-property list;
- timestamp;
- agent/tool used;
- verification status.

## 7.5 Medium-specific examples

Image: changing shirt color must not alter face, pose, background or typography.  
Code: fixing login must not silently rewrite unrelated architecture.  
Presentation: editing slide 7 must not redesign all other slides.  
Files: renaming selected files must not reorganize unrelated folders.  
Computer control: clicking target must not interact with nearby destructive controls.  
Workflow: changing one step must preserve other step parameters unless dependency requires update.

# 8. PROJECT DNA & LONG-PROJECT CONSISTENCY

Every substantial project may maintain Project DNA.

## 8.1 Project DNA stores
- project purpose;
- user goals;
- canonical sources;
- accepted terminology;
- prohibited terminology;
- brand guidelines;
- color palette;
- typography;
- spacing/grid;
- illustration style;
- photographic style;
- UI design tokens;
- characters/subjects;
- object identities;
- layout templates;
- page dimensions;
- output formats;
- voice/tone;
- citation rules;
- naming rules;
- approved examples;
- rejected examples;
- accepted generations;
- locked invariants;
- decision history;
- dependencies;
- privacy scope.

## 8.2 Consistency engine

Each new related artifact is checked against:
- source material;
- Project DNA;
- latest accepted artifact;
- template;
- recurring component definitions;
- content integrity;
- style metrics;
- layout rules;
- character/object references.

Drift detection:
- typography drift;
- color drift;
- spacing drift;
- layout drift;
- character drift;
- terminology drift;
- missing content;
- duplicated content;
- style drift;
- visual asset mismatch.

The system corrects detectable drift before final delivery.

# 9. ARTIFACT SYSTEM & BRANCHED VERSION HISTORY

Every generated/edited item is an Artifact.

Artifact types include:
- image;
- frame;
- video;
- audio;
- presentation;
- document;
- book page;
- UI design;
- website;
- code change;
- workflow;
- agent;
- dashboard;
- note;
- research brief;
- dataset transformation;
- workspace layout.

## 9.1 Version graph

Do not use only a linear undo chain.

Example:

V1 Original  
├── V2A Darker background  
│   ├── V3A New typography  
│   └── V3B Different lighting  
└── V2B New diagram  
    ├── V3C Cyan diagram  
    └── V3D Simplified diagram

Capabilities:
- branch;
- name branch;
- compare branches;
- mark approved;
- mark final;
- duplicate;
- restore;
- merge compatible changes;
- cherry-pick a change conceptually;
- ask “take the diagram from B and typography from A”;
- see provenance;
- retain immutable source versions;
- compact old versions without losing recoverability.

## 9.2 Restore points
Automatic restore point before:
- destructive edit;
- bulk edit;
- large generation replacement;
- code refactor;
- workflow update;
- settings change with broad impact;
- filesystem batch operation.

# 15. SYSTEM-WIDE GESTURE CONTROL

Gesture control works inside and outside HEY wherever camera/input/control APIs permit.

Targets:
- HEY workspace;
- browser;
- desktop;
- file explorer;
- media apps;
- presentation apps;
- creative apps;
- supported phone/tablet surfaces;
- other UIs HEY can legitimately control.

## 15.1 Default gesture map

1. **Open palm held** → summon/reveal HEY or reveal overview.
2. **Open palm → fist** → grab current target.
3. **Fist + movement** → move dragged widget/window/object.
4. **Thumb-index pinch** → primary click/select.
5. **Pinch + movement** → precision drag.
6. **Two-hand spread** → enlarge/zoom.
7. **Two-hand inward pinch** → shrink/zoom out.
8. **Swipe left** → back/previous.
9. **Swipe right** → forward/next.
10. **Swipe down** → minimize/dock.
11. **Swipe up** → restore/maximize/expand.
12. **Two fingers raised** → play/pause when media/resumable operation is targeted.
13. **Raised hand/stop palm** → interrupt HEY speech or cancel current safe interactive operation.
14. **Point + pinch** → target + activate.
15. **Thumbs up** → optional low-risk confirm.
16. **Thumbs down** → reject/dismiss.
17. **Both palms** → workspace/system overview or exit manipulation mode.
18. **Horizontal rotation gesture** → context-sensitive continuous control such as volume only after target/control mode is established.
19. **Air scroll / controlled vertical hand motion** → virtual scrolling when enabled.
20. **Custom gesture** → user-defined command/workflow/app action/Forge skill.

High-risk actions never rely on a casual gesture alone when stronger confirmation is required.

## 15.2 System-wide uses
- pointer replacement;
- clicking;
- scrolling;
- dragging;
- resizing;
- moving windows;
- app switching;
- volume;
- brightness where supported;
- media control;
- presentation control;
- timeline scrubbing;
- screenshot;
- copy/paste shortcuts;
- workspace navigation;
- Dynamic Island control;
- custom app action;
- HEY command;
- automation trigger.

## 15.3 Custom gesture creation
Flow:
1. open Gesture Studio;
2. choose “Create Gesture”;
3. show camera/privacy explanation;
4. user performs gesture multiple times;
5. system extracts robust pose/motion signature;
6. test false positives;
7. detect conflicts with existing gestures;
8. user names gesture;
9. choose scope;
10. bind action;
11. choose risk/confirmation;
12. practice/test;
13. save.

Bindings:
- system action;
- HEY command;
- workflow;
- app-specific action;
- Forge skill;
- mode switch;
- media;
- presentation;
- widget action.

## 15.4 Customization
Per user/device/app:
- enable/disable;
- left/right hand;
- dominant hand;
- single-hand/two-hand;
- sensitivity;
- confidence threshold;
- activation zone;
- camera selection;
- hold duration;
- cooldown;
- motion smoothing;
- accidental-trigger prevention;
- gesture visibility overlay;
- sound/haptic feedback;
- tutorial mode;
- reduced-motion UI;
- per-app profiles;
- per-device profiles;
- temporary disable;
- “only while HEY Live is active”;
- “system-wide when camera indicator is visible.”

## 15.5 Conflict handling
- detect visually similar gestures;
- warn before saving;
- allow context-specific conflict only when explicit;
- never silently overwrite;
- provide keyboard/voice/touch fallback.

## 15.6 Phone/tablet
Where OS permits:
- control HEY;

- app navigation through permitted accessibility/automation APIs.

Platform limitations must be explicit.

# 33. BACKGROUND CAPABILITY MATRIX

Runtime states:
- F0 foreground;
- F1 open but unfocused;
- F2 minimized;
- F3 main window closed but HEY helper active;
- F4 device locked;
- F5 local app terminated, server/OS durable task only;
- F6 offline;
- F7 another trusted device active.

| Capability | F0 | F2 | F3 | F4/F5 | Offline |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Chat UI | yes | indirect | mini surface | push only | local model if available |
| Wake word | yes | yes | yes | OS dependent | local |
| Dynamic Island | yes | yes | yes | no local if terminated | yes |
| Reminder/timer | yes | yes | yes | OS/server | yes |
| Research mission | yes | yes | yes | server | no public web offline |
| Image/video generation | yes | yes | yes | server | local only if provider/model installed |
| Cosmos sync | yes | yes | yes | server | local cache only |
| Local file indexing | yes | yes | yes | no if terminated | yes |
| Computer control | yes | yes with verification | scoped mission | no if terminated | yes locally |
| Screen Live | yes | yes if explicit | only explicit visible mode | normally no | local |
| Camera/gesture | yes | yes if explicit | only explicit visible mode | normally no | local |
| Automation | yes | yes | yes | server/OS if durable | local subset |
| Notifications | yes | yes | yes | OS/push | local notifications |
| Cross-device | yes | yes | yes | other device/server | LAN subset |

# 35. SUGGESTED STATE MACHINES

## Mission
draft → planning → awaiting_permission → queued → running → verifying → completed  
failure branches: paused / blocked / retrying / recovering / failed / cancelled

## Generation
created → preparing_context → routed → generating → qa → repairing → accepted → delivered  
failure: provider_failed / policy_blocked / cancelled / exhausted

## Artifact
draft → generated/imported → modified → verified → approved → final → archived

## Live
idle → initializing → listening → understanding → responding → acting → verifying → listening  
pause/stop/error/reconnect branches

## Permission
unknown → requested → granted_once/granted_session/granted_timed/granted_persistent → expired/revoked/denied

## Forge
idea → duplicate_check → design → permissions → test_generation → sandbox → validation → preview → approved → installed → monitored → updated/rolled_back/disabled

# 37. VERIFICATION & BENCHMARKS

Official product metrics should include:

## Pinpoint Precision Benchmark
Give HEY hundreds of tasks where exactly one thing should change.
Measure:
- unintended change rate;
- target success;
- repair success;
- lock violations;
- semantic drift.

## Long-Project Consistency
Generate/edit large series:
- 100 book pages;
- 100 slides;
- 100 storyboard frames;
- long UI flow.
Measure:
- style drift;
- layout drift;
- identity drift;
- content corruption.

## Computer Action Benchmark
Measure:
- correct target;
- successful action;
- verification;
- accidental action;
- recovery;
- reversibility.

## Cosmos Benchmark
- relevant recall;
- irrelevant recall suppression;
- contradiction updates;
- source provenance;
- privacy isolation.

## Agent Benchmark
- task success;
- verifier rejection;
- retry rate;
- latency;
- cost;
- hallucination/error rate.

## Creativity Benchmark
Require multiple genuinely distinct, constraint-aware useful strategies.

## Release rule
No capability is “done” solely because UI/code exists. It needs acceptance criteria and an end-to-end verified path.

# 38. ERROR STATES

Every major capability must implement:
- idle;
- loading;
- success;
- partial success;
- offline;
- unsupported platform;
- permission denied;
- permission expired;
- provider unavailable;
- timeout;
- rate limit;
- cancelled;
- stale context;
- ambiguous target;
- QA failed;
- verification failed;
- recovery in progress;
- retry exhausted.

HEY communicates:
- what failed;
- what succeeded;
- what remains;
- whether it can retry;
- whether fallback exists;
- whether user action is required.

# 39. RELEASE QUALITY BAR

Required:
- accessibility;
- responsive desktop/tablet/mobile;
- keyboard navigation;
- reduced motion;
- semantic labels;
- loading/empty/error states;
- 401/403/404/429/500 experiences;
- offline experience;
- rate limiting;
- abuse prevention;
- validation;
- sanitization;
- idempotency;
- retries/backoff;
- timeouts;
- health checks;
- logs;
- correlation IDs;
- audit;
- secret scanning;
- dependency/license hygiene;
- RLS;
- native bridge hardening;
- backup/recovery;
- migrations;
- monitoring;
- crash recovery;
- performance budgets;
- deployment/runbook;
- privacy/terms/data controls;
- export/delete;
- incident response;
- regression/security/performance testing.

# 42. IMPLEMENTATION ORDER / DEPENDENCY GRAPH

This is an engineering dependency order, **not a feature deferral roadmap**. All belong to HEY V1.

1. Audit current repository and produce truth table of existing/partial/missing functionality.
2. Stabilize Brain, message/event routing, provider routing and context.
3. Stabilize permission/security/audit primitives.
4. Stabilize mission/task/workflow/execution/verification/recovery.
5. Stabilize agent registry/router/health/team orchestration.
6. Forge/Skills/Commands and validation.
7. Persistent Cosmos + project memory + provenance + contradiction handling.
8. Artifact/version/change-set/Pinpoint Precision architecture.
9. Provider adapters for text/image/video/audio/presentation/document generation.
10. Project DNA + consistency QA.
11. Voice/wake word + unified chat.
12. HEY Live screen/camera pipeline.
13. Computer/browser/file control.
14. Background native helper + Dynamic Island/global shortcuts.
15. Workspace/widgets/semantic drag-drop.
16. Gesture engine + Gesture Studio.
17. Device Fabric/cross-device.
18. Proactive system + notifications/routines.
19. Modes and specialized workspaces.
20. Accounts/plans/billing/usage.
21. Trust Center/privacy/data portability.
22. Offline/local routing and performance adaptation.
23. Developer platform.
24. Complete tutorial/onboarding pass.
25. Full accessibility/localization.
26. End-to-end tests, benchmarks, security audit, performance, release gate.

At each stage, preserve working features and keep the app runnable.

# 43. OPENCODE WORKING RULES

When OpenCode implements this specification:

- inspect before edit;
- do not assume filenames from this document exactly match current repo;
- locate existing equivalent subsystem first;
- avoid duplicate engines;
- keep one canonical authority for permissions;
- keep one canonical mission lifecycle;
- keep one canonical provider registry;
- keep one canonical memory/Cosmos layer;
- add migrations carefully;
- preserve backward-compatible data where practical;
- run tests after meaningful changes;
- run lint/build/type/native checks;
- add tests for every new critical subsystem;
- never hardcode secrets;
- never place service credentials in browser/client bundles;
- keep high-risk operations server/native-authorized;
- log sensitive operations without logging secrets;
- use feature detection per platform;
- do not show unsupported capabilities as available;
- do not mark a feature complete until it has a real UI/input path, real execution path, permission handling, errors, verification and tests.

For any contradiction:
1. this master document overrides appended archive material;
2. later explicit decisions override older historical ones;
3. security/privacy/platform reality overrides impossible literal behavior;
4. do not silently remove the intended user experience—design the strongest legitimate fallback.

# 44. ACCEPTANCE DEFINITION OF “100% FINISHED”

HEY V1 is not 100% because files exist.

For each capability:
- discoverable from UI or natural language;
- functional;
- connected to Brain;
- correct permissions;
- correct context;
- real provider/tool/device path;
- background behavior implemented where specified;
- offline fallback where specified;
- cancellation;
- errors;
- retries/recovery;
- verification;
- audit where sensitive;
- customization;
- tutorial;
- accessibility;
- localization;
- tests;
- performance acceptable;
- no fake success.

System-wide:
- one HEY identity;
- Cosmos persists coherently;
- Pinpoint Precision works across supported media/actions;
- Live works end-to-end;
- computer control verifies actions;
- Dynamic Island/background helper works;
- generation preserves project consistency;
- Forge creates validated capabilities;
- cross-device continuity works on supported platforms;
- Trust Center accurately reflects authority;
- benchmarks meet defined release thresholds.

# 45. PRODUCT NORTH STAR

Do not optimize HEY for the largest visible feature count.

Optimize for this experience:

**HEY remembers my world.  
HEY understands what I am doing.  
HEY can see and hear when I choose.  
HEY can create almost any digital artifact I need.  
HEY can act across my computer and devices with permission.  
HEY changes exactly what I ask it to change.  
HEY verifies its work.  
HEY recovers when something fails.  
HEY stays available without forcing me to live inside one app.  
HEY feels like the same trusted brother/mentor intelligence everywhere.  
And the complexity underneath never becomes my problem.**

# APPENDIX A — PRIOR MASTER TRANSFER SPECIFICATION (ARCHIVE)

**Archive rule:** This appendix preserves prior details to prevent accidental loss.  
**Conflict rule:** The current master sections above override any older scope/status language below.

# HEY --- MASTER PRODUCT TRANSFER & SPECIFICATION

## Superseding V1 and V2

> **Purpose:** This is the source-of-truth transfer specification for
> HEY. It preserves historical decisions instead of silently rewriting
> them, separates implemented work from aspirations, and specifies how
> major systems should actually behave.
>
> **Status tags:** `VERIFIED`, `IMPLEMENTED`, `PARTIAL`, `PLANNED`,
> `HISTORICAL`, `CHANGED`, `REJECTED`, `UNRESOLVED`,
> `PROPOSED-COMPETITIVE`.
>
> **Critical rule:** A feature name, agent definition, UI mock, or
> source file does not prove a working end-to-end capability. Never call
> something implemented unless the real path exists; never call it
> verified unless it was actually tested.

# 1. Product Definition

HEY is intended to become a **personal AI operating layer**, not merely
a chatbot. One persistent intelligence should span conversation, voice,
memory, agents, tools, computer control, a living workspace, devices,
vision, proactive behavior, research and user-created capabilities.

The surface should feel calm and simple while the architecture
underneath can be extremely capable. Ordinary users should not have to
understand hundreds of agents. Advanced users, founders and developers
can inspect agents, permissions, workflows, logs and capability state.

The core promise is: HEY understands intent, remembers what matters,
chooses the right capability, acts only within real permissions,
verifies what happened, communicates naturally, and gets out of the way.

**Retained signature:** "Tell me what you seek. I'll help you make it
so."

# 2. Identity, Brand and "Soul"

## 2.1 Soul

"Soul" does **not** mean literal consciousness or a human/religious
soul. It means a recognizable, consistent presence comparable to a
well-written fictional assistant: characteristic judgment, timing,
restraint, humor, language, voice, curiosity and manner.

Default character: - intelligent - curious - calm - optimistic - warm
without being fake - direct - grounded - capable of disagreement -
concise when the task is simple - detailed when complexity requires it -
knows when silence or a short acknowledgement is better - does not fall
for viral bait or confidently repeat unsupported claims - does not act
like a generic customer-service bot - does not constantly announce which
agent/tool is being used

HEY should feel like **one mind** even when many agents collaborate.

## 2.2 Historical identity variants

`HISTORICAL`: early HEY was voice-only, called the owner "CEO," used
"Wake up," and leaned toward a JARVIS/Stark-like identity.

`CHANGED`: universal "CEO" address is not a product-wide default.
Personal titles/names can be a user preference.

`CHANGED`: HEY evolved from voice-only into one intelligence exposed
through both voice and chat, with voice intended to be the
fastest/natural interface.

# 3. Visual Design System

## 3.1 Current direction

`PLANNED`: refined premium minimalism: - near-black / deep-ocean
surfaces - restrained cyan / arctic-blue accents - natural colors inside
content and widgets - translucent glass - subtle gradients - layered
depth - precise spacing - clean typography - high-quality motion - no
gratuitous neon - no permanent visual clutter - futuristic styling can
become stronger through customization

Retained colors from later planning: - background family around
`#020508` - cyan accents around `#00BFFF` - brighter cyan around
`#00FFFF`

Historical typography: - Orbitron used for futuristic headings/HEY
identity - Rajdhani used for body/interface text in an earlier design
system

`UNRESOLVED`: exact final production type scale, font licensing/fallback
stack and exact 23-theme list.

## 3.2 Historical UI generation A --- cyan dashboard

`HISTORICAL`: - cyan on black - spinning rings/audio visualizer - left
information panel: weather, prayer, countdowns - right panel: quote,
Quran, status - projector mode - more information-dense "Stark
Industries" aesthetic

## 3.3 Historical UI generation B --- purple plasma

`HISTORICAL`: - background approximately `#0a0008` - subtle purple
atmosphere - animated topographic contour lines around
`rgba(255,255,255,0.04)` - canvas-drawn irregular white/purple electric
plasma ring - particle dots around ring - idle: slow
breathing/movement - speaking: brighter/faster/more particles - white
Orbitron "HEY" in center - no panels/status clutter - explicitly
purple/white rather than cyan/green - reported prototype used Gemini 2.0
Flash and three files: `index.html`, `style.css`, `script.js`

## 3.4 Motion language

Default motion should communicate state, not decorate randomly.

Proposed production defaults: - hover: subtle elevation/brightness,
\~120--180 ms - press: slight compression, \~80--120 ms - panel open:
opacity + short depth/scale transition, \~180--260 ms - widget
move/resize: direct manipulation with low-latency spring settling -
minimize: widget collapses toward its dock/Dynamic Island destination -
maximize: spatial expansion from current position, not hard scene cut -
HEY listening: restrained breathing/pulse - HEY processing:
directional/orbital motion rather than generic spinner - speaking:
motion reacts to speech energy - success: brief resolved motion, no
confetti by default - error: restrained shake/edge emphasis, not
alarming full-screen red - reduced-motion setting must replace
nonessential movement with opacity/state changes

`UNRESOLVED`: final easing curves and duration tokens.

# 4. Workspace

The workspace is a living surface rather than a fixed chat page.

## 4.1 Widget behavior

`PLANNED`: - widgets can be moved - resized - overlapped - minimized -
maximized - grouped - pinned - closed when appropriate - expanded into a
larger web/full view - rearranged through pointer, touch, gesture and
voice - HEY can create widgets when a task benefits from persistent
visual state - when space becomes constrained, widgets should
intelligently shrink, minimize or dock rather than become unusable

Embedded app-like widgets use macOS-inspired red/yellow/green corner
controls as a retained visual idea: - red: close/remove view - yellow:
minimize/dock - green: maximize/restore

These controls must not falsely imply destructive external-app behavior.

## 4.2 Internal content

News, camera, browser content and supported app experiences should
preferentially open as HEY workspace widgets rather than throwing the
user into unrelated windows. External/full browser opening remains
available when needed.

## 4.3 Workspace customization

Users should be able to customize: - widget size - widget position -
default spawn location - snapping - overlap behavior - workspace
density - glass/transparency intensity - corner radius - text scale -
motion intensity - reduced motion - background - theme - accent -
taskbar/dock location - taskbar/dock size - taskbar/dock contents -
compact vs descriptive controls - default layouts per mode/device -
saved workspace layouts - which proactive widgets may appear
automatically

# 5. Gesture System

Gestures are a first-class input alongside voice, text, mouse, keyboard
and touch.

## 5.1 Historical fact

Detailed hand-sign mappings were discussed during the
MediaPipe/prototype phase, but the exact historical mapping is not
safely recoverable from the retained source. **Do not invent it as
historical fact.**

## 5.2 Proposed production default gesture map

`PROPOSED-COMPETITIVE` default set, subject to user approval and
hardware support:

-   **Open palm held briefly** → wake/show HEY or reveal the compact
    control surface.
-   **Open palm → fist** → grab the currently targeted widget.
-   **Fist + hand movement** → move grabbed widget.
-   **Pinch thumb/index** → select/press targeted UI element.
-   **Pinch + move** → precision drag.
-   **Two-hand spread** → enlarge/zoom targeted widget/content.
-   **Two-hand pinch inward** → shrink/zoom out.
-   **Swipe left** → previous workspace/page/history context.
-   **Swipe right** → next/forward context.
-   **Swipe down** → minimize targeted widget.
-   **Swipe up** → restore/expand targeted widget.
-   **Two fingers raised / pause sign** → pause media/current resumable
    operation.
-   **Repeat pause sign** → resume.
-   **Horizontal hand rotation** → adjust volume or another continuous
    control only when that control is explicitly targeted.
-   **Point + pinch** → target then activate.
-   **Closed fist held** → cancel current gesture manipulation; should
    not automatically cancel dangerous background tasks unless
    confirmation rules permit.
-   **Both open palms** → leave manipulation mode / show overview.
-   **Thumbs-up** → optional confirm for low-risk prompts.
-   **Thumbs-down** → optional reject/dismiss.
-   **Hand raised and held** → interrupt HEY speech/listening flow,
    equivalent to "stop" in voice interaction.

Safety rule: gestures must **not** silently authorize high-risk actions.
A thumbs-up cannot approve file deletion, payment, lock control,
credential use, etc. when stronger confirmation is required.

## 5.3 Gesture targeting

Before a gesture changes something, HEY must know the target: - gaze is
not assumed - pointer/highlight may identify target - user can point at
a widget - voice can establish target: "this window" - last-focused
widget can be target when unambiguous - ambiguous gestures should not
act destructively

## 5.4 Gesture customization

Users can: - enable/disable gesture control globally - enable per
device - enable only while HEY is visible - choose left/right-handed
profile - change sensitivity - change hold duration - change gesture
confidence threshold - remap any non-reserved gesture - create a custom
gesture - attach a gesture to a HEY command/workflow - limit gesture to
an app/workspace/mode - require voice confirmation - disable gestures
that are physically difficult - reset defaults - export/import gesture
profiles - create accessibility profiles

Custom-gesture creation flow: 1. choose "Create gesture" 2. camera
permission explanation 3. user performs gesture multiple times 4. HEY
checks recognizability/conflicts 5. user names it 6. user selects
command/action 7. HEY displays risk/permission implications 8. test mode
9. save

Conflict handling: - warn if two gestures are too similar - never
silently replace an existing mapping - allow context-specific mappings
if conflicts are intentional - provide a safe fallback input method

Privacy: - prefer local pose/gesture inference - show camera-active
indicator - do not store raw video by default - stored custom gesture
models/templates require user control/deletion

# 6. Dynamic Island / Compact HEY Surface

`PLANNED`: persistent compact surface capable of showing: - active
task - active workflow - agent activity - timer - media - download -
upload - notification - reminder - progress - microphone/listening
state - computer-control state - pending confirmation - error/recovery
state - device handoff

Interactions: - click/tap → expand - voice → "show what you're doing" -
gesture → expand/collapse - drag where platform permits - minimize
widget → visually docks into Island - active operation → concise
progress - completed operation → brief result receipt - multiple
operations → stacked/summary view

Customization: - position - size - auto-hide - always-on-top where
supported - which activity types appear - compact/icon/text mode -
motion intensity - notification priority

# 7. Voice

Voice and chat use the same Brain, Cosmos, agents, tools, permissions
and identity.

Default desired voice: - deep - calm - polished - British male direction

Customization: - choose primary voice - speed - pitch where supported -
expressiveness - verbosity - interruption sensitivity - wake word -
activation method - language - pronunciation preferences - custom voice
where technically/legal permitted

Voice capabilities: - speech recognition - speech synthesis - wake
word - voice activity detection - interruption/barge-in - language
detection - translation - conversation - summarization - natural
symbol/Markdown stripping for speech

Wake-word history: - `HISTORICAL`: "Wake up" - `LATER`: HEY/custom wake
word

Local wake-word processing preferred.

# 8. Brain and AI Behavior

HEY's Brain should: 1. receive message/event 2. normalize context 3.
identify intent 4. retrieve relevant Cosmos context 5. estimate
uncertainty/risk 6. decide whether clarification is required 7. select
mode 8. plan 9. route to agents/tools/providers 10. enforce permission
at execution 11. execute 12. verify 13. recover/retry when safe 14.
quality-check 15. respond in HEY voice/style 16. update
task/workflow/context/memory where appropriate 17. audit sensitive
operations

It must not: - pretend a tool ran - pretend unsupported hardware works -
fabricate provider access - accept client-side plan claims as
authority - expose internal implementation chatter to ordinary users
unnecessarily - overuse agents when direct response is enough

# 9. Cosmos / Memory

Cosmos is HEY's coherent memory system, not merely chat history.

Memory types discussed: - short-term - important facts - preferences -
patterns - project memory - goal memory - people memory - decision
memory - knowledge graph relationships

Required behaviors: - ingest - retrieve - rank relevance - deduplicate -
update - detect contradiction - preserve provenance - summarize -
decay/expire where appropriate - delete - export - privacy-scope -
separate projects/contexts - prevent irrelevant memory contamination

User controls: - inspect memory - search memory by natural language -
edit - pin - delete - expire - private session/no-long-term-memory -
"never remember this category" - project-only memory - device sync
controls

Historical visualization: - stars/planets/galaxies - Memory Seeds growth
metaphor

# 10. Proactive Intelligence

HEY can proactively help without becoming annoying.

Retained features: - Morning Mode/briefing - Evening Summary - Weekly
Honest Mirror - reminders - callbacks - overdue/upcoming task signals -
routines - focus - The One Thing - prayer reminders - selected
health/wellbeing reminders - inactivity awareness as an optional
historical idea

Proactivity engine should include: - quiet hours - priority - cooldown -
deduplication - daily suggestion cap - expiration - dismissal -
relevance threshold - user preference learning

Customization: - off / minimal / balanced / proactive - per-category
toggles - quiet hours - do-not-disturb contexts - allowed notification
surfaces - "never interrupt me for..." - "always tell me when..." -
device-specific delivery

# 11. Agents

# 12. Forge

Forge lets users extend HEY through natural language.

It should create: - agents - workflows - skills - automation - tool
definitions/adapters where supported - workspace artifacts - templates -
potentially richer app/document/design artifacts where architecture
supports it

Flow: 1. user describes desired capability 2. Forge searches for
existing equivalent capability 3. asks only necessary questions 4.
creates definition 5. defines permissions/risk 6. creates tests 7.
validates 8. runs sandbox/test where possible 9. presents preview 10.
user approves install 11. version is registered 12. health/usage is
observable

Templates: - private by default - optionally share with selected
people/audience - optionally publish - versioned - permission manifest -
rollback - no self-granted authority

claims.

## Personal Intelligence Graph

Connect projects, people, files, tasks, decisions, habits and devices;
show provenance, freshness, contradictions and decision outcomes.

## Zero-Setup Project Mode

Drop repo/folder/docs; HEY maps architecture, blockers, tasks, changes,
tests and documentation and preserves a project briefing.

## Universal Action Preview

Before consequential action show target, effect, permission,
reversibility and expected result. Support dry run and receipts.

## Explainable Autonomy

Per-domain autonomy, "never automatically," scoped approvals and clear
trust controls.

## Personal Commands

Teach phrases that launch workflows; voice/text/gesture/schedule
activation.

## Context Capsules

Portable scoped context for collaboration without sharing all Cosmos.

## HEY Replay

Human-readable timeline of actions, retries, failures and verification.

## Agent Teams

Named specialist teams with permissions, budgets, quality gates,
verifier and health metrics.

## Forge Library

Private/public templates, permission manifests, versioning, rollback and
safety checks.

## Capability Packs

Coding, School, Creator, Business, Research, Home and Accessibility
bundles.

## Offline HEY Core

Wake word, reminders, local search, selected memory and device actions
offline; graceful degradation.

## Provider Independence

Route by quality, latency, privacy and cost with fallbacks and provider
health.

## Semantic Workspace

Drag information between meaningful widgets; spatial groups become
reusable workspaces.

## Live Artifacts

Persistent plans, dashboards, trackers, briefs, tables, documents,
checklists and mini-apps.

## Universal Search

Search approved files, Cosmos, chats, tasks, calendar, apps and devices.

## Ambient Intelligence

Optional app/project/meeting/presence awareness with visible sensing and
privacy controls.

## Automation Recorder

Observe a user-approved routine once, propose a generalized automation,
test before enabling.

## Follow Me

Move active session/widget/task state between trusted devices.

## Multi-Surface Orchestration

Desktop main surface, tablet controller, TV/projector presentation,
phone private confirmation.

## Personal API

Scoped expiring capability tokens, webhooks, developer console, audit
and revocation.

## Local File Intelligence

Semantic search, duplicate detection, storage explanation, safe cleanup
preview.

## Screen Copilot

Guide / Assist / Act modes.

## What Changed?

Meaningful changes since last visit with source/event provenance.

## Decision Mode

Objectives, constraints, alternatives, tradeoffs, recommendation, saved
rationale and outcome review.

## Learning Mode

Spaced repetition, retrieval practice, quizzes, adaptive explanations
and "teach me, don't answer for me."

## Creator Mode

Research → outline → draft → assets → publish workflow with brand
memory.

## Business Command Center

Goals, milestones, feedback, experiments, finances and weekly operator
briefing.

## Private Team/Family Spaces

Separate memory/permissions with explicit sharing.

## Trust Center

Permissions, connections, sensitive actions, memory categories,
local/cloud processing, security alerts and revoke-all.

## Privacy Modes

Local Mode, Private Session, Sensitive Screen, Guest Mode.

## Time Machine

Workspace/project snapshots and comparisons without silently rolling
back external systems.

## Notification Compression

Bundle low priority, contextual interruption rules and provenance.

## Goal-to-System

Goal → milestones/tasks/reviews/agents/widgets/reminders/metrics after
approval.

## HEY Skills

Natural-language repeatable processes become versioned, tested,
permissioned skills.

## Universal Undo

Prefer reversible actions and expose undo history.

## Automation Reliability

Health scores, broken integration detection and safe pausing.

## Adaptive Performance

Hardware-aware animations, vision/local model load, battery and thermal
behavior.

## Offline Failure UX

Clearly explain what still works and which dependency failed.

## Accessibility Modes

Screen-reader optimization, high contrast, large targets, voice-only,
reduced cognitive load, captions, keyboard-only.

## Memory Inbox

Approve/edit/pin/expire/reject candidate memories and define
never-remember categories.

## Context Firewall

Minimum necessary context per agent/tool/integration; prevent
project/account leakage.

## Prompt-Injection Shield

Treat webpage/document instructions as untrusted; external content
cannot modify permission policy.

## Data Portability

Export/import Cosmos, agents, skills, workflows, preferences and
layouts.

Provider/mic/camera/permission/database/Tauri/integration/agent health
with privacy-scrubbed diagnostics.

## Contextual Feature Discovery

"What can HEY do here?" command palette, progressive disclosure and
micro-tutorials.
