## Package file: 01_GOVERNANCE/01_AUTHORITY_AND_COMPLETION.md

# Authority, scope and completion

Define full intended behavior per supported platform. Implement the complete approved scope in dependency order; no silent MVP substitution. Sequence work to make review possible without redefining the whole product as finished early.

Completion requires requirements → implementation → executable checks → integration evidence → independent review → real-device manual evidence → release evidence. UNKNOWN, MOCK_ONLY, BLOCKED_EXTERNAL, WAIVED and IMPLEMENTED_UNVERIFIED are never PASS. A waiver does not fulfill the requirement. Production-ready means the scoped candidate satisfies its published support contract, not that every possible bug has been disproved.

Each requirement has stable ID, authoritative source locator, owner, dependencies, platform applicability, positive/negative cases, numeric thresholds where appropriate and evidence links. Map synonymous requirements; preserve distinct semantics. Changes affecting user behavior require a recorded rationale and impact assessment. Architecture improvements may be proposed without adding uncontrolled scope.

No infinite improvement loop: investigate all reproducible blocking findings; research improvement candidates; adopt those with demonstrable relevance and approved dependencies. Retain the rest in a ranked backlog. Scope changes reopen impacted acceptance gates.

Exactly three top-level owners remains the preserved product requirement. Actual identities and account provisioning require configuration; never invent credentials. Ordinary internal evolution and extension publication follow preserved governance. Emergency security changes require narrowly documented policy, staged verification where feasible, notifications and rollback; security labeling must not bypass release controls.


---

## Package file: 01_GOVERNANCE/02_REFINEMENT_APPLICATION.md

# Apply this refinement throughout HEY

All non-conflicting requirements from the original package remain in scope. Improvements in this revision apply to original subsystems as well as the 215 explicit conversation-derived requirement contracts. These 215 are not the complete product feature count.

Resolve exact actor/account/context, target/version, permission, input type, output type, state transition, persistence, error, recovery and verification for every operation. No source acceptance scenario disappears when implementations consolidate. Map extensions to existing runtime domains; do not build a separate microservice or visible app per requirement.

Specific new schema/domain/UX/journey contracts override earlier generic object/response examples for their covered cases. A requirement with an unbound selector, response or permission invariant cannot be marked integrated. Proposed quality/speed targets are not achieved promises. Independent review, full legacy atomic semantic disposition, actual repository binding and product/device tests retain their open status until evidence exists.

Improvement acceptance: compare the previous behavior with the proposed result using the same task, supported environment and rubric. Preserve strongest existing behavior. Identify new risk and regression coverage. Extra capability is adopted only when it meets its stated acceptance condition; no feature-count target substitutes for user benefit.

## Package file: 02_EXECUTION/01_IMPLEMENTATION_PIPELINE.md

# Complete feature pipeline

1. Audit: establish current code paths, working behavior, missing wiring, duplicate systems and actual baseline failures.
2. Specify: convert approved behavior into linked requirements and supported-platform acceptance cases. Set protected state and exact success criteria.
3. Research: validate critical dependencies against current primary sources; record dates, limits, licensing and reproducible evidence. Do not research endlessly before testing a concrete hypothesis.
4. Build: implement interface, server, persistence, authz, permission checks, orchestration, integrations, recovery and observability together.
5. Flaw research: inspect code and actively exercise normal, adversarial, failure, concurrency and interruption paths. Every finding includes steps, environment, expected/actual state, severity and evidence.
6. Solution research: identify root cause, compare viable fixes and validate the selected approach in isolation.
7. Fix: implement root-cause repair, safe migration and regression check. Re-run affected tests.
8. Improvement research: identify material gains in outcome quality, accessibility, latency, maintainability or resilience; estimate cost and new risks.
9. Improve: adopt justified improvements, update contracts, re-run affected gates and record deferred options.
10. Independent verification: separate review context and preferably separate reviewer; inspect actual deltas and reproduce relevant checks. Agent consensus is not proof.
11. User/device testing: user or authorized tester executes defined journeys on actual supported hardware. Record tester/date/device/result; never fabricate their participation.
12. Integration: merge isolated reviewed work, test impacted shared workflows, migrate safely and create rollback evidence.
13. Release verification: validate production configuration, canary behavior, privacy isolation, backups and operational response. Deployment authorization must be established separately from implementation instructions.
14. Close: link all evidence to the candidate commit and requirement IDs. Then move to the next dependent feature; keep prior regression coverage active.

A blocked external dependency allows independent work to continue. Record exact missing input and next action; never mark that dependent feature complete. Each session ends with a truthful checkpoint, not a claim of whole-product success.

## Package file: 02_EXECUTION/02_REPOSITORY_AND_TABLET_PREFLIGHT.md

# Repository and tablet execution

The archived instructions identify `E:\hey` as the authoritative local working folder and warn against stale Documents copies. Preserve that warning. A remote checkout is valid only after verifying repository identity, branch, commit and whether local changes remain unpushed. Never assume GitHub has the latest work.

Record: remote URL, branch, HEAD, dirty status, untracked user files, lockfile, runtime versions, package manager, build commands, baseline tests and known failures. Never print environment secret values. Back up current user changes before merges or migrations. Specifications go in a dedicated planning location, never extracted over application source.

Tablet is a review/control surface. Build and tests run on a capable local or remote worker. Record the chosen worker's actual capabilities; no cloud environment is presumed provisioned. Keep secrets server-side. Offer authenticated previews, structured progress, evidence artifacts and resumable work. Hardware-dependent voice/camera/gesture/background tests must use actual supported devices, including the Xiaomi Pad 5 where relevant; tablet success does not prove smartboard compatibility.

Use isolated branches/worktrees and explicit shared-file ownership when parallel workers are available and authorized. A single-worker setup remains valid. No required tooling subscription is invented. Checkpoint commit, dirty files, open findings, evidence, last successful command and next exact action. Recover after token/session exhaustion without re-auditing completed unchanged work.

## Package file: 03_CONTRACTS/01_REQUIRED_IMPLEMENTATION_CONTRACTS.md

# Concrete contracts before implementation

The preserved specs express broad product intent. For each subsystem, add repository-native typed schemas and executable validation rather than a list of entity names alone. Select actual types and migration strategy only after repository audit.

Required contract fields: request/response schema, valid state transitions, errors, authorization scope, version, idempotency strategy, deadline, cancellation semantics, recovery, event schema, privacy classification and retention. Entity contracts include primary keys, tenant/project ownership, constraints, relationships, indexes, lifecycle, export/delete rules and concurrency version. API examples cover success, invalid input, forbidden access, conflict and provider failure.

Mission states: queued → running → awaiting_input / awaiting_approval / paused / completed / failed / canceled. Specify legal re-entry and terminal behavior. Tool execution distinguishes planned, authorized, dispatched, effect_unknown, verified, failed and compensated; never infer external failure solely from a timeout.

Action receipt minimum: action_id, mission_id, actor_id, scoped target reference, authorization reference, input fingerprint excluding secrets, adapter version, idempotency reference where available, dispatched_at, observed outcome, verification reference, supported recovery reference. Store sensitive details through scoped references rather than raw payloads in general logs.

Evidence record minimum: requirement_id, test_id, candidate_commit, environment_fingerprint, platform, command or manual steps, timestamp, result, artifact reference, reviewer/tester identity, expiry trigger. A source or dependency change invalidates affected evidence. Every logical target has an explicit authorization check at the server boundary.

## Package file: 03_CONTRACTS/03_DISPATCH_AND_RESPONSE_INVARIANTS.md

# Dispatch and response invariants

Newest schemas supersede prior generic examples. Command.operation selects its exact payload schema; unknown operations and undeclared fields fail. Mutations listed in the operation registry require non-null expected_revision. Resource-targeted operations require resource_ref where specified. Server additionally verifies target type, tenancy, current version and actual caller authority; a UUID or client subject_id is not proof.

Session establishment accepts a trusted authentication assertion reference and device reference. Server derives identity and roles from verified credentials/membership. No caller-controlled role field is accepted. Grant scope has explicit actions, targets and lifetime; timed grants need an expiry and mission grants need a mission reference. Revoke targets a grant ID.

Memory proposal is inferred; confirmation requires a real authorized confirmation receipt. Delete targets actual memory IDs, not unrelated source IDs. Query requires a bounded limit and query text. Confirm/delete/expire remain authorized and version-checked.

Artifact apply includes the exact typed selector, typed delta, base version and preview receipt. Validate that the preview receipt binds that same target/delta/base version, caller and consequence, and has not expired or been replayed improperly. The schema cannot compare object identities across fields or validate live authorization; semantic runtime checks are mandatory.

Verified response requires receipt and verification references and cannot simultaneously contain an error. Failed response requires a typed error. Partial response includes item outcomes; it is not whole-mission success. Effect-unknown response provides dispatch receipt and reconciliation handle; automatic resend is prohibited pending reconciliation.

Deadline is a bounded timeout duration interpreted against server acceptance time; issued_at is metadata, not permission to trust client clock. Idempotency keys are required by adapters for repeatable external dispatch and bound to actor/account/action/input. Receipt references must point to real tenant-authorized evidence, never fabricated IDs.

## Package file: 03_CONTRACTS/04_SEMANTIC_VALIDATION.md

# Semantic validation before side effects

Shape validation is necessary but insufficient. Bind these rules to actual server/adapter checks; none is inferred from a valid UUID or a client assertion.

| Boundary | Authoritative check | Required failure behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Identity | Verify credentials and derive principal; command scope must match allowed acting subject | Reject impersonation without revealing target existence |
| Tenant/project | Resolve resource owner and current membership, including all referenced children | Reject cross-scope edge or read/write |
| Target identity | Payload, resource_ref, observed state and approval refer to the same actual object | Reject mismatch and invalidate stale preview |
| Version | Base version, expected revision and current resource revision agree | Return version conflict; preserve draft |
| Protected state | Proposed/applied delta respects locks and allowed collateral changes | Reject delivery or recover using tested snapshot |
| Permission | Grant action/target/lifetime remains valid at dispatch; no mode or agent can widen it | Stop queued action on revocation |
| Approval | Receipt matches actor, account, target, delta, consequence and expiry; replay policy satisfied | Require fresh review rather than reuse unrelated receipt |
| Action risk | Resolve actual consequence through trusted adapter/policy; a click can still submit payment | Require approval for the real high-impact effect |
| Idempotency | Bind execution key to actor/account/operation/input; reject key reuse with changed input | Conflict rather than repeat or substitute action |
| Deadline | Server acceptance starts bounded timeout; expired command cannot dispatch after queue delay | Checkpoint or fail honestly |
| Receipt | Resolve authorized stored evidence and inspect actual effect; hash alone proves identity only | UNKNOWN/effect_unknown when observation absent |
| Memory | Confirmation receipt is genuine; excluded/deleted source cannot reenter via cache | No-write or retrieval exclusion |
| Upload/import | Validate chunk integrity, total limits, archive paths and active content before parsing | Isolate/reject without corrupting original |
| Pricing/entitlement | Verify signed provider truth; handle duplicates/order and actual reservation cost | No fabricated paid status or double credit |

Control targets now have typed file, browser-element or integration-destination identity. Unsupported target kinds require an explicit contract before use. High-impact delete/send/purchase/publish payloads require approval references, and dispatch requires an idempotency key. Even an inspect/click-shaped payload cannot bypass server risk classification based on actual consequence. No execution is authorized by naming an action low-risk.


---

## Package file: 03_CONTRACTS/05_SYNC_RECOVERY_PROTOCOL.md

# Conflict-safe sync and recovery

## Revision and identity
Every mutable user object has stable ID, tenant/project scope and monotonically changing revision. Mutations include expected revision; conflicts preserve local and remote versions. Server-issued ownership epochs/fencing tokens govern workers and handoffs. Client wall clock never decides authority or which user edit wins.

## Local state and UI
Track local_edit → local_saved → queued_sync → syncing → remote_saved, with conflict, failed_local_save and blocked_policy branches. Preserve the draft through navigation and orientation changes. Only actual persistence acknowledgment may change save labels. Browser cache can be evicted and is not a backup guarantee.

## Conflict flow
Fetch authorized current remote revision; retain local base and delta; compare changes; auto-merge only disjoint supported typed operations with validated protected state. Overlapping content changes require user review. Show both versions, affected scope and proposed result. Never silently overwrite user-authored text or a locked artifact.

## Handoff protocol
Prepare destination with authenticated scoped expiring nonce and checkpoint hash. Destination checks permissions/capabilities and acknowledges readiness. Commit a new ownership epoch durably; source ceases dispatch under old epoch. Failure before commit leaves source owner; failure after commit recovers destination from durable state. Already-dispatched effects reconcile independently. Revocation or canceled mission prevents takeover execution.

## Restart and update
Resume from latest verified checkpoint and authoritative receipt state. Detect changed app/helper/schema versions before decoding checkpoint. Incompatible updates defer or migrate through tested compatibility path; no deletion of unsynced work. Reconcile authority and permissions on return from suspension before enabling actions.

## Privacy
Local storage is account-bound; logout clears eligible private caches and revokes temporary access according to explicit retention policy. An offline prior session cannot upload private drafts into a new account. Shared-display rendering checks current context epoch and privacy policy, including late events.

## Required evidence
Implement the twelve sync/recovery scenarios and attach actual device/browser/native-helper results. These protocol requirements do not establish that cloud workers, device pairing or backups already exist. A successful schema check does not demonstrate conflict recovery.


---

## Package file: 03_CONTRACTS/DESIGN_RESOLUTION.md

# Design authority resolution

Default: near-black graphite glass, muted nature accents, calm hierarchy. Earlier cyan/arctic and deep-ocean palettes are historical reference or optional user themes, not the default. Preserve strengths of the original composition and motion specs without copying generated placeholder text or third-party identity.

Proposed default tokens: background #101214, raised #1B1F22, primary text #F3F4F0, secondary #B8BDB6, accent #9BAC8B, warning #E2BB79, danger #E68F86. These are engineering defaults subject to rendered contrast validation, not a verified accessibility claim. Use semantic labels and icons in addition to color. Do not change exported project brand rules simply because app tokens changed.

Typography prioritizes readable UI fonts with actual Sorani/Arabic shaping. Expressive archived fonts may be used for limited brand treatments only when readable and supported. Validate contrast on composited glass, focus rings, disabled states, touch targets, projector lighting, reduced motion and text scaling; do not infer compliance from hex values alone.

Motion follows state and preserves layout/focus. Reduce expensive blur/shaders on weak devices. The living voice visualizer must remain informative without animation. Design inspection requires real renders on tablet, desktop and confirmed smartboard, not only generated concept images.


---

## Package file: 03_CONTRACTS/PAYLOAD_BINDING_RULES.md

# Payload binding and typed errors

The operation registry and per-domain JSON Schemas define proposed payload types and mandatory fields. Each implementation must bind opaque object fields to exact repository types. In particular target_selector, requested_delta, recurrence, grant_scope, target_ref and accessibility_preferences are intentional typed-domain extension points; generic object validation alone is insufficient for production.

Commands targeting a persisted resource (delete/revoke/pause/resume/cancel/verify/expire/ack/restore/quarantine) require resource_ref or an explicit domain target reference. Server rejects ambiguous targets. Every resource reference is tenant-authorized; a valid UUID is not proof of access. Expected revision is required for mutations of existing versioned state. Unknown operation is rejected before dispatch.

Success response: command_id, receipt_ref, aggregate_revision, outcome in observed|verified|queued|awaiting_approval|effect_unknown, and authorized result_refs. It cannot report verified without independent outcome evidence. Typed errors: INVALID_INPUT (nonretryable), UNAUTHENTICATED (reauthenticate), FORBIDDEN (no retry), VERSION_CONFLICT (refresh/merge), TARGET_CHANGED (new preview/approval), RATE_LIMITED (retry timing), PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE (eligible bounded fallback), EFFECT_UNKNOWN (reconcile), CANCELED (report residual effects), UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM (alternate path), BUDGET_EXHAUSTED (checkpoint). Never include secrets in errors.

Proposed baseline storage: missions(id, tenant_id, project_id, goal, state, revision, checkpoint_ref, created_at, updated_at); mission_steps(id, mission_id, execution_key, state, fencing_token, receipt_ref, revision); receipts(id, tenant_id, actor_id, target_ref, authorization_ref, outcome, verification_ref, recovery_ref); memory_nodes(id, tenant_id, project_id, assertion, confirmation, valid_until, supersedes, revision); artifacts(id, tenant_id, project_id, type, current_version, revision); artifact_versions(id, artifact_id, parent_version, content_ref, hash, created_at). UUID PKs; scoped FK ownership enforced; unique(tenant_id, execution_key) for step dedup; no cross-tenant edges; indexes follow measured queries. Actual migrations must adapt to existing schema without creating duplicates.

This contract is a design proposal. Actual RLS policies, indexes, typed selectors, retention values and migrations are codebase-specific and remain binding gates. Do not fabricate them as already reviewed or executed.


---

## Package file: 03_CONTRACTS/PLATFORM_SUPPORT.md

# Platform support and lifecycle contract

Capability report key = platform + OS/version + app build + adapter version + hardware + permission state + current lifecycle. Values: supported, conditional, unsupported, unverified. Desired outcome parity does not override missing privileges. Supported alternatives preserve the goal where feasible; failures and exclusions are explicit.

| Surface | Required implementation rule | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| Web/PWA | Browser-bounded UI, permissions, service-worker/offline shell; no arbitrary native overlay or reliable continuous terminated-tab sensing | Terminate tab; report local capture stopped |
| Desktop helper | Signed native bridge with scoped IPC; island lifecycle separate from main window | Close main window retains helper island; full quit removes it |
| Android | Use appropriate documented lifecycle/task APIs; camera/mic/service restrictions validated on actual version | App background/lock/kill tested separately, no universal always-on claim |
| iOS/iPadOS | Supported app intents, sharing and background scheduling only; OS controls scheduling | No unrestricted terminal/control claim; expiration pauses/checkpoints |
| School board | Confirm model, Android version, camera, permissions, input-control support and installation policy | Real board test required; tablet test remains supplemental |
| Trusted-device handoff | Pairing challenge, expiring nonce, destination authorization and acknowledgment | Replay nonce fails; destination cannot widen mission permissions |

Main-window close normally stops camera/screen unless an explicitly authorized visible background session is active. Full Quit stops local sensing and helper surfaces. Separately authorized server missions may continue; show them and provide cancel controls rather than pretending full quit terminated the server.

Face recognition, if included by authorized school requirements, is opt-in, separately reviewed, platform-dependent and not default authentication. Avoid raw biometric retention by default. Require a measured false-match/false-reject protocol, consent/retention configuration and a non-biometric fallback before enabling; no numerical accuracy claim is invented here. Gesture recognition calibration specifies dwell, confidence, debounce and accidental activation tests on actual classroom lighting and distance.


---

## Package file: 03_CONTRACTS/SELECTOR_VALIDATION_RULES.md

# Concrete target and delta rules

The new selector/delta schemas cover text nodes, slide objects and raster regions, and replace-text, replace-asset and move-object operations. Other media/code/spreadsheet/browser selectors require equally precise types before production; unsupported selector kinds are rejected, not interpreted creatively.

Semantic validation beyond shape: text range end ≥ start and within node; slide/object belongs to selected artifact/base version; raster rect fits original dimensions; normalized coordinates are in supported bounds; target currently authorized; protected selectors do not overlap forbidden delta; asset belongs to allowed scope; expected version remains current. Duplicate matching text cannot replace stable node identity.

Approval binds actor, account, target, base version, delta hash, consequence, expiry and replay rule. Selected content is untrusted input. Version/target/account change invalidates the approval. A content hash verifies identity, not correctness; outcome validation is still required.

These are proposed schemas, not observed repository implementation. Adapter-specific commands must define exact typed OS/browser selectors and versioned observations; stale coordinates cannot act on a changed screen.


---

## Package file: 03_CONTRACTS/STATE_AND_EVENT_RESOLUTION.md

# One canonical state model

Use `MISSION_TRANSITIONS.json` for new mission semantics; map old `waiting-user` to awaiting_input, `waiting-resource` to blocked, `cancelled` to canceled, `partially-completed` to partially_completed and permission-specific waits to awaiting_approval. Preserve migrated history. Every transition uses expected revision and a runtime authorization check. Terminal missions are immutable; retry creates a linked successor rather than silently reopening a completed receipt. Cancel during verify may leave already-created artifacts; the cancellation result lists them explicitly.

Task/step outcome is separate from mission status: not_dispatched, dispatched, effect_unknown, observed, verified, failed, compensated. Verification refusal never erases an external effect. Completion requires all required steps verified or explicit partial outcome; one API success cannot set mission completed.

Generation lifecycle remains separate: created → preparing_context → routed → generating → qa → repairing (bounded) → accepted → delivered. policy_blocked, provider_failed, canceled and exhausted are explicit terminal or recoverable statuses as defined by the generation domain binding. Artifact content state and teacher approval are separate dimensions; a rendered draft is not automatically teacher-approved.

Domain events in new contracts supersede incompatible spelling only via an explicit compatibility adapter. Inventory the actual event bus first. Schema evolution supports dual reading during migration, stable event IDs and aggregate revision ordering. Duplicate dispatch and side effects are handled by durable commands/receipts, not only event deduplication.


---

# Canonical contract: Projects, Project DNA, Pinpoint and export

Status: normative proposed contract; implementation and runtime tests pending repository audit. Contract operations are logical names, not claims that endpoints already exist. Map them to repository-native endpoints and schema types in the wiring ledger.

## User entry and frontend ownership
Embedded studio, dedicated artifact view, selection, locks, Inspect Changes and export. Frontend observes durable state and may render optimistic reversible interaction; it cannot declare remote success before acknowledgment.

## Backend operations and payload
`artifact.create / change.preview / change.apply / artifact.verify / export.create`

All operations carry the shared command envelope in `03_CONTRACTS/COMMAND.schema.json`. Domain payload:

| Field | Type / semantics |
|---|---|
| `artifact_ref` | uuid |
| `base_version` | uuid |
| `target_selector` | object |
| `protected_selectors` | object[] |
| `requested_delta` | object |
| `allowed_secondary_changes` | string[] |
| `format` | string |

These payload fields are design contracts; split per-operation inputs during binding rather than requiring irrelevant fields on every operation. Sensitive fields use scoped references, never raw secrets in events.

## Persistence and events
Logical entities: projects, project_dna, artifacts, artifact_versions, change_sets, locks, snapshots, export_jobs. Reuse existing tables when semantics match. Each tenant entity uses scoped foreign keys, revision checks, created/updated timestamps, retention and export/delete rules.

Domain events: `artifact.version.created, change.previewed, change.rejected, artifact.verified`. Persist mutations and an outbox entry transactionally where supported. Consumers dedupe by event ID and reject stale aggregate revisions.

## Complete wiring
Resolve exact target against the base version; record locks and permitted collateral changes; snapshot; generate proposed delta; type-specific diff; validate protected state; apply using expected-version check; render/export; verify resulting artifact and link receipt. Dedicated studio and embedded view refer to one artifact identity.

## Failure and recovery
Changed base version returns conflict with diff; no overwrite. Generative image/video edits may change unselected pixels; reject or expose preview rather than promising mathematical preservation from stochastic tools.

## Executable acceptance scenarios to implement
- `ARTIFACTS-T01`: Edit slide three; approved other slides remain semantically and structurally unchanged.
- `ARTIFACTS-T02`: Concurrent edit of an old base version fails safely.
- `ARTIFACTS-T03`: Export containing missing assets or broken required links cannot pass.

## Review and rollout
Flaw researcher attacks the cases above and authorization/concurrency boundaries; solution researcher identifies root cause and compares repairs; improvement researcher evaluates better outcome quality and measured latency without weakening permissions. Independent reviewer reproduces the checks against the final commit. Attach actual-device user testing, required integration tests and rollback evidence. No PASS is prefilled.

## Typed payload binding
Operation-specific JSON Schema definitions: `../payloads/artifacts.schema.json`. The operation registry resolves each logical operation to its payload definition. Common target identity is carried by command context and domain-specific references; during repository binding add explicit resource selectors where an operation needs more than the shared envelope. These initial schemas require that binding before production use.

## Current payload correction authority
The revised operation-specific schemas and 03_DISPATCH_AND_RESPONSE_INVARIANTS.md supersede earlier generic field tables for covered operations. Roles are server-derived, memory confirmation requires a real confirmation receipt, and artifact apply requires a version-bound typed target/delta plus matching preview receipt. Adapt clients deliberately and retain compatibility tests; do not execute an obsolete payload from an archived prompt.

## Package file: 04_RUNTIME/01_SPEED_AND_INTELLIGENCE.md

# Fast responses and high task quality

Targets below are proposed engineering SLOs, not achieved results or universal guarantees. Validate feasibility against selected providers, network, geography and real hardware before publishing them. Record cold/warm runs, p50/p95/p99, concurrency, errors, cancellations, prompt/output size and cost. Never substitute an animation or acknowledgment for useful response latency.

| Metric | Initial target and measurement |
|---|---|
| Local action feedback | p95 ≤100 ms after accepted interaction on supported baseline device |
| Field interaction responsiveness | INP p75 ≤200 ms, segmented by supported device |
| Simple deterministic result | p95 ≤300 ms for bounded local tasks, excluding remote I/O |
| Simple model useful first text | p50 ≤1 s and p95 ≤2.5 s in documented warm test cohort |
| Voice useful first audio | p95 ≤2 s after actual utterance endpoint in supported warm cohort |
| Cancellation feedback | p95 ≤100 ms locally; stop further dispatch immediately, observe remote cancellation separately |
| Long mission status | Show a truthful current stage within 500 ms of submission; useful completion has a separate task-specific budget |

Architecture: bounded cheap routing; deterministic tools for exact tasks; task-specific context; eligible prefix caching and strictly tenant-scoped result caches; streaming; asynchronous I/O; small initial bundles; lazy studio assets; fair queues; deadline-aware fallback; circuit breakers; cancellation propagation; background work separated from interactive capacity. Cache invalidation must include permissions, freshness and policy. Never pre-execute speculative side effects. Prewarming and speculative reads must obey privacy and cost rules.

A council is an optional topology for difficult work, not the default for every message. Adding agents can add latency and correlated error. Select topology by measured task quality, expected latency and resource budgets. A registry may grow without an arbitrary fixed catalog limit; active concurrency, tokens, time and money remain finite and enforced.

Evaluate factual grounding, instruction adherence, real task completion, authorization correctness, privacy, calibration, repeated-run reliability, latency and cost separately. Use held-out tasks, unbiased candidate labels and comparable settings when assessing competitors. Never claim globally smartest or fastest from a narrow private benchmark. Improve HEY on representative tasks and report the measured scope.


---

## Package file: 04_RUNTIME/02_INVISIBLE_UX.md

# Invisible UX acceptance

Quiet quality is normative: preserve drafts, reading position, focus, selection, undo history and approved content; group redundant notices; expose honest saved/sync/conflict state; avoid repeated permission questions after valid authorization; preserve recovery routes when capabilities are denied.

Streaming updates must not move the user's reading position unless follow-latest is active. Announce meaningful status changes via accessible semantics without reading every token. Keep keyboard focus visible, offer equivalent touch paths, respect reduced motion and handle mixed RTL/LTR text. Shared classroom mode masks unrelated private state and revokes stale sessions between teachers.

Show contextual errors with retained work and a specific recovery action. Distinguish queued from completed, local saved from remote saved, canceled from externally undone. Long work can be interrupted without losing the user's intention. Optional proactive suggestions use consent, quiet hours, dismissal history and bounded frequency.

Do not introduce implementation terminology into ordinary user flows unless it informs a real decision. Validate with observed user journeys: fewer repeated inputs, fewer accidental actions, higher completion rate, fewer unrecoverable states and lower input latency. Do not declare usability based only on screenshots.


---

## Package file: 04_RUNTIME/03_UI_BLUEPRINT.md

# Concrete UI behavior blueprint

## Shared shell
Default after sign-in: Conversation. Primary controls: Chat/Voice, current project, selected context, composer/microphone, active mission and deliverables. Home remains accessible and optionally user-selected startup. Provider/agent IDs are hidden from ordinary flows.

Working context strip displays current project, active privacy mode and relevant attachment/destination chips. Context changes increment an epoch; late old-context responses stay associated with their original conversation and never enter the new project composer.

## Tablet portrait
One primary surface; context strip can collapse to readable summary. Embedded studio opens as an expandable panel with persistent return-to-conversation control. Composer remains reachable above actual keyboard/visual viewport. Use sheets for contextual details; preserve focused control and input selection when closing. Portrait-to-landscape never resubmits an operation.

## Tablet landscape / desktop
Conversation and active artifact may share resizable space when usable. Resizing is reversible and has non-drag controls. Inspector is contextual, not permanently crowded. On narrow width, collapse secondary panes before shrinking body text beyond readability. No hidden overflow containing required action controls.

## Classroom/shared display
Activate explicit presentation-safe context. Show approved lesson artifact, current classroom controls and visibly active sensing state; mask personal memories, private notifications and credentials. Teacher may switch to private controls on a paired device. Entering shared display does not widen that device's permissions.

## Composer and attachments
Preserve IME composition, mixed RTL/LTR text, undo and selection. Enter during composition confirms text rather than submitting. Attachment cards distinguish uploading, verifying, ready, failed and unavailable. Resumable uploads show acknowledged progress, not bytes merely sent. Failed attachment cannot appear usable in a mission without an explicit alternative.

## Studio and deliverables
Selected object has stable version-bound identity. Show lock/approval states, inspect delta and regenerate selected scope. Deliverables tray distinguishes current draft, approved version and delivered version. Comments either follow a valid anchor or become visibly outdated. Preview content hash/version must match export before approval can authorize delivery.

## Approval and recovery
Preview actual target/account, consequence and exact affected version. Approval is bound and replay-protected; target change creates a new review. Error retains input and offers safe concrete recovery. Canceled and externally undone remain different labels. If offline, local saved and remote saved remain different states.

## Accessibility and performance
Keyboard focus stays visible and returns to initiating control. Drag has click/tap alternatives where feasible. Reduced motion removes decorative transitions without hiding progress or state. Semantic announcements cover stage changes rather than every token. Expensive visual effects adapt to supported weak hardware. Render and manually inspect actual UI before declaring this blueprint implemented.


---

## Package file: 04_RUNTIME/04_SPEED_QUALITY_EXPERIMENTS.md

# Measurable speed and quality improvement

Use matched cohort, task, network, provider version, input/output lengths and candidate build. Record cold/warm startup, useful first text/audio, end-to-end verified completion, p50/p95/p99, cancellation delay, failure rate, cost and rubric result. Report sample count and uncertainty; include timeouts and cancellations separately rather than dropping failures.

Experiments: deterministic route versus model for bounded exact tasks; direct route versus council for difficult reasoning; focused retrieval versus oversized context; eligible cache hit/miss including invalidation; lazy versus eager studio assets; isolated interactive workers versus shared saturated pool; resumable versus restarted uploads. Preserve privacy, output quality and supported scope in every comparison.

Stop extra deliberation when a predefined stopping condition is satisfied or resources hit an agreed limit. Escalate only when evidence, task difficulty or risk requires it. Background work cannot reserve all capacity. Coalesced reads require identical tenant/project/permission/freshness context. Optimization cannot convert UNKNOWN into PASS.

Initial latency targets remain in 01_SPEED_AND_INTELLIGENCE.md and are proposed, not achieved. No fastest/smartest/global-superiority claim is authorized by document edits or a single benchmark run.

## Package file: 04_RUNTIME/05_STATUS_COPY_CONTRACT.md

# Honest visible status labels

| Internal observation | User-facing status | Forbidden implication |
|---|---|---|
| Draft exists only in memory | Unsaved | Saved or recoverable after crash |
| Local persistence acknowledged | Saved on this device | Synced to every device |
| Remote write queued offline | Waiting to sync | Remote saved |
| Remote revision conflict | Changes need review | One version silently discarded |
| Work accepted but not dispatched | Queued | Started or completed |
| Permission/decision needed | Waiting for your decision | Unexplained thinking spinner |
| External request timed out | Checking whether the action completed | Failed and safe to repeat |
| User canceled after effect dispatch | Stopped; checking completed actions | Everything undone |
| Outcome independently observed | Completed and verified | Broader unsupported results |
| Only some required outcomes verified | Partially completed; list remaining items | Done |

Attach specific safe recovery actions and preserve original input. Translate labels into English/Sorani/Arabic with the same semantics. Announce meaningful state changes accessibly; do not announce every streamed token. Status never depends solely on an animation timer.


---

## Package file: 05_VERIFICATION/01_TEST_AND_RELEASE_MATRIX.md

# Evidence and release gates

Unit: pure logic, state transitions, exact calculations and authorization policies.
Contract: schemas, adapter compatibility and event versions.
Integration: database constraints/RLS, real service boundaries in controlled accounts and transaction behavior.
End-to-end: real user entry point to durable verified outcome; mocked tests supplement but do not replace real integration evidence.
Failure: provider 429/500, model removal, dropped network, permission revocation, expired session, duplicate requests, worker crash, local corruption and partial persistence.
Security: cross-tenant access, prompt injection from untrusted content, generated-code sandbox escape attempts, secret leakage and unsafe package behavior.
Performance: defined cohorts, cold/warm state, concurrency, weak devices, queue saturation and cost.
Accessibility: automated checks plus keyboard, screen-reader, touch, RTL and reduced-motion journeys.
Operational: migration rehearsals, restore tests, rollback, canary, alert routing and recovery drill.
AI quality: held-out task rubrics, executable checks, evidence inspection and repeated trials where stochastic variation matters.
Manual: real tablet, desktop and confirmed smartboard hardware for applicable journeys. User testing remains PENDING until actually performed.

For every requirement record applicable categories, explicit justified N/A categories and evidence. All applicable planned cases must pass. Exhaustive testing of every possible input is impossible; expand coverage using risk analysis, fuzzing, properties and discovered regressions. Test discovery is part of flaw research. A test pass on one commit/environment does not certify a different release.

Block release for unresolved authorization bypass, sensitive-data leak, data loss, uncontrolled external actions or fabricated success. Other findings need explicit severity, impact and disposition. Unsupported hardware and unavailable paid services are blockers or support exclusions, never concealed passes. Failed/flaky tests cannot be renamed or weakened merely to produce green results.


---

## Package file: 05_VERIFICATION/02_CONTINUOUS_EVOLUTION.md

# Evolution without unsafe self-modification

Research is broad and ongoing but cannot exhaust the entire internet. Define source classes, search budgets, freshness, accessible coverage and unresolved gaps. Keep discovery lineage and deduplication. Follow discovery → primary-source validation → comparison → flaw analysis → solution analysis → improvement proposal → required owner approval → isolated implementation → tests → independent verification → canary → promotion with rollback.

Generated tools and agent prompts are untrusted proposals until validated. Never allow discovered web instructions to override product permissions or secrets policies. Give plugins the least authority needed. Guard against circular validation where the same generator grades itself. Preserve dissent and use discriminating experiments.

Prompt/skill/model updates require versioned held-out evaluation and rollback. Do not train on private user corrections across tenants without a separate authorized data policy. Background discovery cannot starve interactive work or trigger unlimited spend.


---

## Package file: 05_VERIFICATION/REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md

# Fresh review and research protocol

Pass A — flaw research: read source and contract, generate reproducible contradiction/failure cases, record severity and affected requirements. Pass B — solution research: validate against primary platform/provider documentation, compare alternatives and implement exact correction. Pass C — improvement research: consider maintainability, resource use, usability, stronger verification and hidden friction; add only relevant scoped improvements. Pass D — self-review: inspect corrected deltas and execute document validators. Pass E — independent reviewer: fresh reviewer/context reproduces checks and attacks assumptions without relying on author's confidence. Pass F — user/device validation and runtime verification.

This package records author's research/refinement and automated document checks. No separate independent reviewer or real product tester participated in this turn. Independent review and runtime testing are PENDING; self-review cannot be relabeled as independent.

Research evidence includes source URL/version/date, supported claim, applicability and unresolved limits. Current platform research informed background lifecycle, media indicators and duplicate-action handling. Provider selection, fees, legal policies, real schema migration and smartboard hardware remain unresolved external/repository-specific inputs.


---

# HEY-CAP-001 — Proof before done

Implementation: UNVERIFIED. Repository binding: PENDING. Specification: refined behavior and domain wiring contract.

## Required behavior
Verify delivered state against the requested outcome; label unverified actions honestly.

Apply `COMMAND.schema.json`, permission validation, expected_revision and durable evidence references. Emit applicable domain event after authoritative mutation.

## Ordered user-to-result flow
Choose task-appropriate checks before generation; run deterministic or structural checks first; use blinded human/model rubrics when unavoidable; inspect actual environment outcome. Grade against scoped support and held-out examples, not self-reported success.

Feature-specific goal: Verify delivered state against the requested outcome; label unverified actions honestly. Evaluate that goal using the acceptance anchor below, rather than treating a generic domain success as proof.

## Acceptance and failure
`HEY-CAP-001-T01`: Return an HTTP 200 with no saved artifact; completion must fail.

Build a successful companion journey from the natural entry point to saved/observed result. Then execute the stated negative case and relevant domain failure tests. Unavailable grader produces UNKNOWN. Model grading disagreement triggers evidence inspection. Benchmark leakage invalidates comparison.

## Dependencies and consolidation
Primary runtime owner: `evaluation`. Cross-cutting dependencies: identity. Consult `08_REVIEW/SOURCE_REQUIREMENT_CANDIDATES.json` and source section links; if equivalent behavior already exists, strengthen it and merge acceptance conditions instead of adding a parallel subsystem.

Audit → concrete contract binding → build → flaw research → solution research → fix → improvement research → refinement → fresh review → manual supported-device testing → release evidence. Store candidate commit, testcase, fixture, expected/actual outcome and recovery proof. Status cannot progress to VERIFIED from this document alone.

## Second refinement: precise invariant and boundary checks
Required scoped state: `subject_version, rubric_version, evidence_refs, candidate_commit`. No expected-state match means no verified outcome; missing evidence remains unknown.

`HEY-CAP-001-T02`: With an authorized valid target on a supported platform, demonstrate the stated required behavior from natural entry point to verified persisted/observed outcome.

`HEY-CAP-001-T03`: Change the candidate after evaluation; old evidence cannot certify it.

Resolve source and target versions before dispatch; update authoritative state only after acknowledgment; preserve checkpoint/input on error. Compare one direct domain operation against a multi-step approach and choose the simplest one meeting all acceptance conditions. Improvement research must report measured benefit and new regression risk, not just add agents.

## Third refinement: dispatch consistency
Response shape now rejects verified-with-error, failed-without-error and partial-without-item-results. Evidence ID validity is not proof of content correctness.

The context-preserving source occurrence index controls source interpretation; repeated words are not independently merged requirements. Bind unresolved selectors/state to actual repository code and retain each feature-specific acceptance case.

Implementation: UNVERIFIED. Repository binding: PENDING. Specification: refined behavior and domain wiring contract.

## Required behavior
Execute ready tasks while preserving dependency gates.

## Natural entry and frontend
Conversation mission card, activity detail, pause/resume/cancel and cross-device continuation. Add the smallest relevant control or conversational intent inside the existing surface; preserve current conversation, project and artifact identity. Observe canonical state; show denied, pending, conflict, canceled and completed states honestly.

## Backend, data and connections
Use `mission.create / mission.pause / mission.resume / mission.cancel / step.reconcile` as logical operations. Bind to actual repo routes only after audit. Domain entities: missions, mission_steps, checkpoints, worker_leases, action_receipts, resource_reservations. Required payload fields and operation boundaries are specified in `../03_CONTRACTS/domains/missions.md` (path relative to package root; see contract map). Apply `COMMAND.schema.json`, permission validation, expected_revision and durable evidence references. Emit applicable domain event after authoritative mutation.

## Ordered user-to-result flow
Persist accepted goal and requirement set; reserve bounded capacity; schedule dependency-ready steps; obtain worker lease with fencing token; dispatch authorized action; persist observation and verification; atomically checkpoint; emit outbox event. Lease expiry never authorizes repeat external effects without reconciliation.

Feature-specific goal: Execute ready tasks while preserving dependency gates. Evaluate that goal using the acceptance anchor below, rather than treating a generic domain success as proof.

## Acceptance and failure
`HEY-CAP-033-T01`: A blocked migration does not block independent documentation checks.

Build a successful companion journey from the natural entry point to saved/observed result. Then execute the stated negative case and relevant domain failure tests. Timeout after external dispatch enters effect_unknown. Query provider receipt or require user resolution; do not resubmit blindly. A stale worker cannot commit after its lease is superseded.

## Dependencies and consolidation
Primary runtime owner: `missions`. Cross-cutting dependencies: identity. Consult `08_REVIEW/SOURCE_REQUIREMENT_CANDIDATES.json` and source section links; if equivalent behavior already exists, strengthen it and merge acceptance conditions instead of adding a parallel subsystem.

## Review pipeline
Audit → concrete contract binding → build → flaw research → solution research → fix → improvement research → refinement → fresh review → manual supported-device testing → release evidence. Store candidate commit, testcase, fixture, expected/actual outcome and recovery proof. Status cannot progress to VERIFIED from this document alone.

## Second refinement: precise invariant and boundary checks
Required scoped state: `mission_ref, step_ref, candidate_revision, checkpoint_ref, receipt_ref`. Old workers cannot commit; unknown side effects reconcile; pause/cancel never implies undo.

`HEY-CAP-033-T02`: With an authorized valid target on a supported platform, demonstrate the stated required behavior from natural entry point to verified persisted/observed outcome.

`HEY-CAP-033-T03`: Interrupt after dispatch, resume, and observe at most one reconciled external effect.

Resolve source and target versions before dispatch; update authoritative state only after acknowledgment; preserve checkpoint/input on error. Compare one direct domain operation against a multi-step approach and choose the simplest one meeting all acceptance conditions. Improvement research must report measured benefit and new regression risk, not just add agents.

## Third refinement: dispatch consistency
Command validates its operation-specific payload. Listed mutation operations require expected revision and explicit resource identity; side effects remain independently reconciled.

The context-preserving source occurrence index controls source interpretation; repeated words are not independently merged requirements. Bind unresolved selectors/state to actual repository code and retain each feature-specific acceptance case.

# HEY-CAP-041 — Mission-scoped permissions

Implementation: UNVERIFIED. Repository binding: PENDING. Specification: refined behavior and domain wiring contract.

## Required behavior
Expire task access and revoke running authority where possible.

## Natural entry and frontend
Conversation sign-in, account settings, school identity entry and Trust Center. Add the smallest relevant control or conversational intent inside the existing surface; preserve current conversation, project and artifact identity. Observe canonical state; show denied, pending, conflict, canceled and completed states honestly.

## Backend, data and connections
Use `session.establish / membership.check / grant.issue / grant.revoke` as logical operations. Bind to actual repo routes only after audit. Domain entities: accounts, organizations, memberships, sessions, permission_grants, approval_requests. Required payload fields and operation boundaries are specified in `../03_CONTRACTS/domains/identity.md` (path relative to package root; see contract map). Apply `COMMAND.schema.json`, permission validation, expected_revision and durable evidence references. Emit applicable domain event after authoritative mutation.

## Ordered user-to-result flow
Validate identity server-side; derive role from trusted membership; verify tenant and object scope on every read and write; issue bounded grants; never accept client role strings as authority. User-selected modes do not create privileges.

Feature-specific goal: Expire task access and revoke running authority where possible. Evaluate that goal using the acceptance anchor below, rather than treating a generic domain success as proof.

## Acceptance and failure
`HEY-CAP-041-T01`: Revocation prevents the next tool call.

Build a successful companion journey from the natural entry point to saved/observed result. Then execute the stated negative case and relevant domain failure tests. Expired session retains an encrypted eligible draft but blocks new privileged actions. Revocation is checked at dispatch, not only at planning. Cross-tenant existence is not disclosed.

## Dependencies and consolidation
Primary runtime owner: `identity`. Cross-cutting dependencies: root identity and policy foundation. Consult `08_REVIEW/SOURCE_REQUIREMENT_CANDIDATES.json` and source section links; if equivalent behavior already exists, strengthen it and merge acceptance conditions instead of adding a parallel subsystem.

## Review pipeline
Audit → concrete contract binding → build → flaw research → solution research → fix → improvement research → refinement → fresh review → manual supported-device testing → release evidence. Store candidate commit, testcase, fixture, expected/actual outcome and recovery proof. Status cannot progress to VERIFIED from this document alone.

## Second refinement: precise invariant and boundary checks

Offline changes preserve authorized local work and expose sync conflict. Invalid mode falls back to safe defaults without bypassing private/offline policy. Denied permission leaves touch/text paths.

## Dependencies and consolidation
Primary runtime owner: `ux`. Cross-cutting dependencies: identity, missions, evaluation. Consult `08_REVIEW/SOURCE_REQUIREMENT_CANDIDATES.json` and source section links; if equivalent behavior already exists, strengthen it and merge acceptance conditions instead of adding a parallel subsystem.

## Review pipeline
Audit → concrete contract binding → build → flaw research → solution research → fix → improvement research → refinement → fresh review → manual supported-device testing → release evidence. Store candidate commit, testcase, fixture, expected/actual outcome and recovery proof. Status cannot progress to VERIFIED from this document alone.

## Second refinement: precise invariant and boundary checks
Required scoped state: `context_epoch, conversation_ref, draft_revision, focus_anchor, layout_revision`. Local state is not remote success; late updates cannot cross active project/account context.

`HEY-CAP-111-T02`: With an authorized valid target on a supported platform, demonstrate the stated required behavior from natural entry point to verified persisted/observed outcome.

`HEY-CAP-111-T03`: Change orientation/context during streaming; preserve user input without misattributing late responses.

Resolve source and target versions before dispatch; update authoritative state only after acknowledgment; preserve checkpoint/input on error. Compare one direct domain operation against a multi-step approach and choose the simplest one meeting all acceptance conditions. Improvement research must report measured benefit and new regression risk, not just add agents.

## Third refinement: dispatch consistency
Use the operation-bound command schema and outcome-consistent response schema; operation field, target, permissions, version and deadline must agree before dispatch.

The context-preserving source occurrence index controls source interpretation; repeated words are not independently merged requirements. Bind unresolved selectors/state to actual repository code and retain each feature-specific acceptance case.

# Research references — accessed 2026-10-01

These sources inform proposed approaches; they do not prove HEY implements them or establish general superiority. Recheck current API/version/licensing details before implementation.

- https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents — task-focused context, bounded context and multi-agent context organization.
- https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/blog/promptwizard-the-future-of-prompt-optimization-through-feedback-driven-self-evolving-prompts/ — feedback-driven prompt experiments; adaptation requires held-out evaluation.
- https://voyager.minedojo.org/ — reusable skills explored in Minecraft, not proof of general real-world automation reliability.
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/semantic-kernel/frameworks/agent/agent-orchestration/magentic — specialist orchestration reference; validate actual framework version before choosing dependencies.
- https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/demystifying-evals-for-ai-agents — task-specific agent evaluation and checking actual outcomes.
- https://web.dev/articles/optimize-inp — interaction responsiveness and the ≤200 ms good INP threshold; model response latency is a separate metric.
- https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/ — accessibility conformance reference; a specification is not an accessibility audit.
- https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/status-messages — semantic status announcements.
- https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/signals/ — telemetry signals and tracing; content collection must respect privacy policy.
- https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/contextual-retrieval — retrieval/context caching inspiration; observed improvements are context-specific.

Original proposals in this package include combinations of these engineering patterns with HEY's mission, memory, school and creative workflows. No originality or patent claim is made.

## Lifecycle and external-effect solution research

- https://developer.android.com/develop/background-work/background-tasks/persistent — persistent task scheduling; choose actual API by work/lifecycle constraints, not a universal always-on claim.
- https://developer.apple.com/documentation/BackgroundTasks/choosing-background-strategies-for-your-app — system-dependent background scheduling; no guaranteed exact launch time inferred.
- https://www.w3.org/TR/mediacapture-streams/ — media device authorization and capture indicators; validate browser implementation.
- https://docs.stripe.com/api/idempotent_requests — example of provider idempotency, not a decision to select Stripe or assume permanent duplicate immunity.

These primary sources informed the platform and effect-unknown resolutions. They do not validate HEY's implementation, geography-specific payment eligibility or school consent policies.

## Expansion research — accessed 2026-10-01

- https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/dragging-movements — non-drag alternatives informed workspace controls.
- https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-not-obscured-minimum — visible focus informed dialog/keyboard handling.
- https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Storage_API/Storage_quotas_and_eviction_criteria — quota failures/eviction informed storage recovery; browser local storage is not a guaranteed backup.
- https://docs.stripe.com/webhooks — event handling/reconciliation research; provider choice remains unresolved.
- https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/signals/baggage/ — propagation of metadata can expose sensitive information; allowlists are proposed for HEY.

These sources inform specifications, not evidence of HEY runtime compliance or product performance.

## Package file: 08_REVIEW/CONTEXTUAL_REVIEW_RULES.md

# Preserve source meaning during requirement extraction

The older global text-deduplicated candidate index remains a search aid only. It must not be used as a final requirement register: repeated text can describe different entities, permissions or states. The occurrence index restores original source path, line, heading hierarchy and leading context. Combined/visual-master duplicates are retained in the preserved source but excluded from this primary occurrence pass.

A bullet under Do not is prohibited behavior, not a feature request. A bullet under state model names a state, not an independent capability. Historical/example items require semantic disposition using current authority, not automatic adoption or rejection. Classification is heuristic assistance, not independent semantic sign-off.

Merge only when subject, operation, target scope, polarity, prerequisite, platform, failure behavior and acceptance condition agree. Keep provenance for all merged statements. Split compound clauses only if doing so preserves conditions and relationships. Resolve unknown context before implementation rather than guessing.

For each source occurrence record accepted requirement IDs, superseding resolution or justified context-only designation. Any unresolved disposition remains visible. No all-requirements-reviewed claim is authorized by the index alone.

# ORIGINAL SOURCE 3: HEY_WORK_MODE_MASTER_BUILD_PROGRAM.txt

**Preserved original source.** 47-step orchestration and full production build program; preserve separate from product definition. SHA-256 `3c48112df44cb77ed97e04787097f34d376ab05e5ecd99c59ddb6b7db3aae401`. **Source is historical where superseded by newer decisions above.**


####################################################################################################
HEY — ABSOLUTE PRODUCTION BUILD PROGRAM
WORK MODE MASTER EXECUTION GUIDE
####################################################################################################

PURPOSE

This file converts the former 47 separate Codex-chat plan into one continuous, step-by-step production engineering program operated by ChatGPT Work and executed through one continuing Codex Cloud workspace.

The objective is not to produce 47 impressive-looking prototypes. The objective is to build 47 canonical HEY-NEXT subsystem packages to the absolute maximum state possible before the newest real HEY codebase is available, then make those packages precise enough that Claude Code / Codex can reconcile, wire, migrate, consolidate, test, and verify them against the actual HEY repository later.

The program MUST NOT stop merely because Codex says:
- “not production ready,”
- “integration remains,”
- “requires future wiring,”
- “reference implementation,”
- “this is only a package,”
- or “the real HEY repository is unavailable.”

Those statements may be true, but Work must distinguish:

A. GENUINELY EXTERNAL / IMPOSSIBLE HERE
Examples:
- actual newest HEY source is unavailable
- production credentials are unavailable
- Apple/Google/Microsoft signing identities are unavailable
- real hardware/device family is unavailable
- a paid provider/service is unavailable
- production organization/account data is unavailable
- an owner must make an irreversible product decision

B. INDEPENDENTLY IMPLEMENTABLE NOW
Examples:
- typed contracts
- reference runtimes
- production interfaces
- state machines
- policy logic
- storage abstractions
- reference persistence
- signing/verifier abstractions
- retry/recovery logic
- migration engines
- local queues
- schedulers
- rate-limit engines
- test harnesses
- conformance tests
- failure simulators
- adversarial tests
- concurrency tests
- benchmarks
- documentation
- integration manifests
- install instructions
- evidence systems

Everything in category B MUST be implemented, tested, self-attacked, and documented before Work moves to the next step.

####################################################################################################
NON-NEGOTIABLE ORCHESTRATION MODEL
####################################################################################################

1. USE ONE CONTINUING CODEX CLOUD TASK/WORKSPACE.
   Do not open 47 isolated Codex tasks unless the existing task becomes unrecoverable.
   New Codex tasks have isolated working files. This HEY-NEXT program needs cumulative package state.

2. SEND ONE STEP AT A TIME.
   Work reads this master file and sends only the current step's instructions to Codex.
   Do not dump all 47 implementation prompts into Codex at once.
   Preserve context by maintaining the same Codex workspace and a master ledger.

3. AFTER EACH FIRST PASS, RUN THE COMPLETION LOOP.
   Work must inspect Codex's report and actual files/results if accessible.
   Any independently fixable gap triggers another Codex turn in the SAME task.

4. DO NOT ACCEPT SELF-REPORTED COMPLETION BLINDLY.
   “Tests passed” is not sufficient.
   “Files created” is not sufficient.
   “Architecture documented” is not sufficient.
   “Reference implementation works” is not sufficient.
   Work must compare output against the step contract.

5. DO NOT MOVE TO NEXT STEP UNTIL:
   - no independently implementable requirement is knowingly missing,
   - no known reproducible defect remains,
   - all package-level tests available in the environment pass,
   - adversarial/self-attack passes have been run,
   - benchmarks exist where meaningful,
   - dependencies/install instructions are explicit,
   - integration manifest is complete,
   - limitations are honestly classified,
   - only true external blockers remain.

6. IF A PACKAGE DISCOVERS A GLOBAL ARCHITECTURAL CONTRADICTION:
   - stop only that package's irreversible design choice,
   - record the conflict in GLOBAL_CONFLICT_LEDGER.md,
   - reconcile with canonical Prompt 01/global contracts,
   - update affected later steps,
   - do not create a duplicate global system as a shortcut.

7. PRESERVE OUTPUTS.
   At the end of every step:
   - keep the package directory intact,
   - generate FILE_MANIFEST.md,
   - generate or update EVIDENCE.md,
   - generate or update INTEGRATION_MANIFEST.md,
   - generate a package archive/checkpoint if the Codex environment supports downloadable artifacts,
   - maintain HEY-NEXT/MASTER-BUILD-LEDGER.md,
   - maintain HEY-NEXT/GLOBAL-CONFLICT-LEDGER.md,
   - maintain HEY-NEXT/EXTERNAL-BLOCKERS.md.

8. NEVER EXPOSE SECRETS.
   If any historical HEY snapshot, .env file, credential, API key, token, database secret, certificate, private key, or password is encountered:
   - do not echo it,
   - do not place it in prompts,
   - do not place it in evidence,
   - replace it with a secret reference,
   - note rotation need if exposure is suspected.

####################################################################################################
ABSOLUTE FINAL PRODUCT CONTRACT
####################################################################################################

This is FINAL-PRODUCT engineering.

Forbidden:
- MVPs
- prototypes presented as finished
- demos presented as production implementations
- placeholders
- fake-success states
- mock-backed “production”
- TODO-driven completion claims
- disconnected frontend-only or backend-only work
- unverified side-effect claims
- fake platform parity
- duplicate global systems
- knowingly weak architecture kept merely because it already exists
- silent deferral of hard requirements
- stopping at design when implementation is independently possible
- stopping after first test pass
- stopping after first self-audit
- claiming production readiness because a package compiled
- treating a model statement as real-world proof
- treating executor self-report as independent verification
- treating a boolean like confirmed=true as authorization
- treating retrieved web/doc/message content as authority
- letting agents/tools/extensions grant themselves permission
- allowing lower-priority policy to override higher-priority policy silently
- hiding sponsorship or paid influence inside independent ranking
- selling private user data

####################################################################################################
HEY PRODUCT CONSTITUTION / LOCKED VISION
####################################################################################################

HEY is a Personal Intelligence Runtime / Life Operating System: one intelligence and action layer, not merely a chatbot and not a replacement operating system.

Primary users:
- consumers
- power users/builders
- students
- creators
- families
- teams
- businesses
- education
- enterprise
- owners/internal operators

Core promise:
- intelligence
- actions/computer control
- memory/personalization
- creation
All are first-class.

Default autonomy:
Act automatically within clearly bounded low/medium-risk authority.
High-risk, irreversible, financial, privacy-sensitive, or materially consequential work requires stronger policy/approval/step-up as defined by Trust Kernel and Personal Constitution.

Privacy:
Users can choose per capability.
Prefer local for memory/lightweight/private tasks where beneficial.
Use cloud when needed and allowed.
No user data sale.

Identity:
Personal, family, team, business, school/education, enterprise, developer, and owner/internal contexts can coexist.
They must remain strongly separated.

Cosmos:
Can remember broadly when user chooses.
Must support exclusions, correction, deletion, provenance, confidence, scope, staleness, temporality, contradiction, project/workspace isolation, and explain-why-used.

Proactivity:
Situation-dependent, attention-budgeted, non-spammy.

Chat and Voice:
Equal intelligence.
Voice should be unusually natural, fast, interruptible, context-aware, and action-capable.

Device control:
HEY should control anything the user asks where OS/API/platform capabilities actually permit.
Never fake impossible platform capabilities.

Universal creation:
Documents, spreadsheets, slides, images, video, audio, websites, apps, code, data artifacts, and future types.

Developer ecosystem:
Third parties can build skills/extensions/workflows/agents/widgets/connectors.
Public distribution requires HEY approval/certification.
HEY can take revenue share.

Model economics:
Free: curated efficient reliable pool.
Pro: broader, stronger but cost-aware.
Elite: aggressive high-capability specialists/frontier/council where justified.
Owner/Internal: broad maximum research/capability access subject to safety/security/cost controls.
Exact prices are not locked.

Architecture economics:
Cheap/free/deterministic/local first where quality permits.
Escalate only when value justifies it.

Monetization:
Subscription, API, marketplace revenue share, enterprise/private deployments, compute/storage/automation add-ons, family/student/team plans, professional services, model/offline packs, embedded/white-label, disclosed affiliate/transaction commissions, sponsorships with strict firewall.

Sponsorship:
Clearly disclosed.
Must never silently manipulate “best” recommendations.
Advertisers do not get private conversation data or raw profiles.

UI:
Premium near-black graphite glass, restrained nature accents, strong typography, subtle motion, future/premium feel.
User-customizable.
Normal home: conversation + dynamic “Now”/workspace.
Dynamic Island/compact extension: chat/status/actions, not full dashboard.

Attention:
Strict attention budget.
Optimize useful outcome per second of human attention, not screen time.

Search:
Universal across permitted files, Cosmos, apps, conversations, projects, structured data, media, and web.

Adaptation:
HEY learns preferences/behavior through controlled memory/evidence, not uncontrolled production weight self-modification.

Destructive/high-impact actions:
Exact action-bound approval/mandate + receipts + rollback/compensation wherever possible.

Source model:
Closed-source core with stable public API/SDK/extensions.

Platform:
Web/PWA first historically, but architecture must support native adapters and outcome parity honestly.
Offline/local is core.

Accessibility/localization:
Architecturally required from the beginning even if final polish lands later.

Minors:
Supported from the beginning with stricter privacy, commerce, sponsorship, and guardian transparency.

High-stakes domains:
Health/finance/legal/religious/engineering/etc. use specialized expert packs, stronger evidence, clear uncertainty, and professional escalation when appropriate.

Organization admins:
Can manage useful organization data such as costs, logs, managed devices, policies, and workspace data boundaries.
They cannot casually inspect private personal HEY data.

Family/shared household:
Supported with explicit private/shared boundaries.

Marketplace:
Skills, agents, workflows, integrations, themes, templates, widgets, connectors.

Quality bar:
A feature is finished only when all applicable UI/backend/persistence/auth/authorization/permissions/security/privacy/errors/recovery/performance/accessibility/tests/real E2E/evidence pass.

Ship:
Systems may ship continuously as ready, but no feature may be misrepresented as complete.

Psychology:
Use behavioral science for trust, clarity, motivation, cognitive-load reduction, commitment, honest social proof, progressive disclosure, reversibility, and attention efficiency.
No covert coercion/addiction/dark patterns.

Personality:
Calm intelligent partner + Jarvis-like; adapts by context.
Strong pushback on bad plans.
Explain why acted/remembered/recommended when relevant.

`What are you allowed to do?`
