- export-before-delete option
- audit evidence
- final deletion state

==================================================
SERVICE / AGENT IDENTITIES
==================================================

HEY has non-human actors.

Create secure identity types for:

- internal service
- HEY agent
- extension
- automation
- integration
- external agent
- background worker

These actors must NOT impersonate the user.

Their actions must always preserve:

human/user authority source
+
service/agent identity

Example:

User Sako
authorized
Agent X
to ask
Device Y
to execute action Z.

The receipt must show all identities.

==================================================
IMPERSONATION
==================================================

Avoid unrestricted impersonation.

For support/admin scenarios, use explicit:

- delegated support session
- scoped access
- expiry
- reason
- audit
- user notification where appropriate
- no raw password sharing

Never implement “log in as user” as an invisible unrestricted backdoor.

==================================================
OWNER / INTERNAL OPERATOR IDENTITY
==================================================

HEY owners/operators need elevated internal capabilities.

But OWNER does NOT mean:

- bypass user encryption
- bypass user privacy
- bypass security invariants
- unrestricted production-data browsing

Build owner/internal identities separately.

Require:

- strong authentication
- short-lived privileged sessions
- explicit reason
- audit
- least privilege
- optional approval for sensitive production access

==================================================
AUTH AUDIT EVENTS
==================================================

Define events for:

- account created
- login success
- login failure
- passkey registered
- passkey removed
- password changed
- password reset
- MFA added
- MFA removed
- recovery initiated
- recovery completed
- recovery cancelled
- session created
- session refreshed
- session revoked
- all sessions revoked
- device registered
- device trust changed
- device revoked
- device lost
- suspicious session detected
- step-up required
- organization membership changed

Use Prompt 01 event/receipt conventions.

==================================================
PRIVACY REQUIREMENTS
==================================================

Identity data is sensitive.

Minimize collection.

Separate:

required operational data

from

optional risk/analytics signals.

Never log:

- passwords
- passkey secrets
- full authentication tokens
- recovery secrets
- private keys
- raw biometric data

Biometric verification should remain platform-managed where possible.

==================================================
OFFLINE AUTHENTICATION
==================================================

HEY offline mode is core.

Design what a previously trusted device may do while disconnected.

Offline behavior must distinguish:

- locally authenticated user
- cached session
- expired session
- revoked-but-device-does-not-yet-know scenario
- local-only actions
- cloud-required actions
- organization policy
- high-risk actions

Offline authority should be narrowly bounded.

On reconnection:

- reconcile revocations
- synchronize security events
- refresh policy
- invalidate stale authority
- resolve pending actions safely

==================================================
SESSION CONTINUITY
==================================================

HEY missions may last hours/days.

Do not couple mission lifetime directly to a short-lived access token.

Support safe reauthentication and continuation.

A mission may pause for:

- expired auth
- reauthentication
- changed workspace membership
- revoked device
- policy change

Mission state survives.

Authority does not.

==================================================
WEAK-DEVICE PERFORMANCE
==================================================

The identity client for HEY Edge must remain lightweight.

Avoid requiring:

- full app framework
- heavy cryptography package when platform primitive exists
- huge dependency trees
- large databases
- model runtime

Define minimal Edge identity protocol.

==================================================
STORAGE SECURITY
==================================================

Document per-platform expectations for secure storage:

- browser/PWA
- Android
- iOS/iPadOS
- Windows
- macOS
- Linux
- server/headless
- legacy gateway

Do not pretend secure storage is identical across all platforms.

==================================================
DATABASE / STORAGE MODEL
==================================================

Design production-ready schemas for at least:

users
accounts
account_memberships
organizations
organization_memberships
workspaces
workspace_memberships
sessions
devices
device_credentials
authentication_methods
passkeys

recovery_methods
recovery_events

identity_links
service_identities

You may refine names/normalization.

Include:

- constraints
- lifecycle state
- tenant boundaries
- soft/hard deletion considerations
- timestamps
- versioning
- uniqueness rules

Do NOT assume Supabase until integration.

Provide database-agnostic schema intent plus concrete migration-ready reference implementation.

Use typed results/errors.

SECURITY REQUIREMENTS
==================================================

Test against:

- session fixation
- token replay
- refresh token reuse
- credential stuffing
- brute force
- account enumeration
- weak reset flows
- stolen device
- cloned device identity
- fake device name

- logout race

- invitation replay

==================================================

Design identity-sensitive rate controls for:

- login attempts
- signup abuse
- recovery

- OTP/TOTP verification
- device enrollment

Do not make rate limiting depend solely on IP address.

- expired session

- suspicious login

Do not build the full HEY visual shell.

==================================================
ACCESSIBILITY
==================================================

Authentication cannot depend solely on:

- color
- fine motor gestures
- voice
- biometric
- one specific second factor

Flows must remain accessible to:

- keyboard users
- screen readers
- low-vision users

- motor-impaired users

==================================================

- RTL
- multilingual messages
- locale-aware dates/times
- no English-only auth assumptions
- Unicode-safe identifiers/display names

Security error messages must avoid leaking account existence.

==================================================
GLOBAL HEY LAWS
==================================================

HEY is one intelligence, not a visible pile of disconnected bots.

All surfaces eventually share canonical identity, missions, permissions, policies, Cosmos, agents, tools, models, devices, artifacts, receipts, evidence, events, context, and user preferences.

HEY is provider-independent and device-independent.

Prefer, when suitable:
deterministic code/rules/cache/algorithms -> tiny classifiers/micro-models -> local/small models -> cheap strong cloud models -> specialist models -> frontier models -> multi-agent councils only when measured value justifies them.

HEY must work across web/PWA, Android, iOS/iPadOS within platform limits, Windows, macOS, Linux, tablets/phones/desktops, very weak devices, remote/cloud runtimes, local/self-hosted runtimes, and future device adapters.

Ultra-light device law:
The intelligence does not need to live on the device. The device needs only the smallest trusted local runtime necessary to expose supported capabilities, enforce authority, access permitted resources, execute typed actions, verify postconditions, and communicate securely.

Device classes:

You are the principal production engineer for HEY responsible for: Accessibility, Localization, Internationalization & Inclusive Interaction.

Create the production-grade integration-ready package:

`HEY-NEXT/43-accessibility-localization/`

PACKAGE OWNERSHIP
Own HEY's cross-product accessibility/localization foundation so major systems can become usable across abilities, languages, scripts, cultures, devices and input methods.

DEPENDENCY INTENT
This package conceptually depends on: All product/UI/artifact/platform packages.
Because every Codex task is isolated and other package outputs may not be physically available, do not invent competing global systems. Use minimal clearly-labelled temporary mirrors only when compilation/testing requires them.


==================================================
ABSOLUTE FINAL PRODUCT CONTRACT — NON-NEGOTIABLE
==================================================

This is FINAL-PRODUCT engineering, not ideation, an MVP, a prototype, a demo, a mockup, a proof of concept, or a partial feature pass.

Forbidden:
- MVP shortcuts or knowingly incomplete production paths
- placeholders, fake-success states, dead buttons, disconnected screens, mock-backed “working” behavior, TODO-driven completion claims, or silent deferral of hard requirements
- frontend-only, backend-only, schema-only, or test-only completion claims
- a new duplicate global architecture when a canonical HEY contract already exists
- assuming code exists means behavior is integrated, verified, secure, recoverable, observable, accessible, performant, or production-ready
- replacing a stronger future-existing HEY implementation merely because this package differs
- inventing details about the unavailable real HEY repository
- claiming platform capabilities the platform does not expose
- claiming successful side effects without independent postcondition verification

For every applicable capability, the completion pipeline is:
discovery -> current research -> explicit requirements -> architecture -> implementation -> contracts -> data/state -> permissions/authentication/authorization boundaries -> privacy/security -> integration seams -> failure handling -> retry/timeout/cancellation -> recovery/rollback/compensation -> offline/degraded behavior -> weak-device behavior -> performance/cost controls -> observability/auditability -> accessibility/localization readiness -> unit tests -> integration tests -> adversarial/failure tests -> realistic end-to-end tests -> independent verification -> evidence.

If you discover a fixable defect inside this package, FIX IT. Discovery creates work; it is not a reason to stop.

Use the maturity ladder:
MISSING -> DESIGNED -> IMPLEMENTING -> FUNCTIONAL -> INTEGRATED -> VERIFIED -> PRODUCTION_READY.

PRODUCTION_READY requires current, reproducible evidence. Evidence becomes stale when affected implementation, dependencies, policy, environment, tests, schemas, contracts, or providers change.

Never use “confirmed: true”, “approved: true”, UI state, model output, retrieved content, or client-supplied claims as sufficient authority for consequential actions.

Every consequential action must be attributable to the human/service actor, the executing component/device/tool, the exact authority used, the exact target/parameters, the result, verification evidence, cost where relevant, and rollback/compensation status where applicable.

==================================================
SOURCE / INTEGRATION AUTHORITY
==================================================

The newest real HEY codebase is currently unavailable.

Therefore:
1. Build a production-grade, interface-stable, integration-ready HEY-NEXT package.
2. Do not invent the current repository structure, existing tables, current routes, current providers, or current implementations.
3. Clearly separate VERIFIED package behavior from UNVERIFIED future-integration assumptions.
4. If you need a shared contract from another HEY-NEXT package that is not physically present, create only a minimal TEMPORARY CONTRACT MIRROR and label it exactly:
   TEMPORARY CONTRACT MIRROR — MUST BE RECONCILED WITH CANONICAL HEY CONTRACT DURING INTEGRATION.
5. Do not create a competing identity, permission, event, mission, Cosmos, provider, device, artifact, or evidence system simply because the canonical package is unavailable.
6. Every external dependency, service, environment variable, database requirement, native entitlement, build requirement, model/runtime requirement, and installation step must be recorded for Claude Code in DEPENDENCIES.md and INTEGRATION_MANIFEST.md.
7. Future Claude Code integration must inspect the real HEY implementation first, preserve unique stronger behavior, migrate/consolidate safely, wire all layers, run regression/adversarial tests, and retire obsolete duplicates only after evidence.
8. Never destructively assume that HEY-NEXT automatically supersedes existing production code.

==================================================
GLOBAL HEY LAWS
==================================================

HEY is one intelligence, not a visible pile of disconnected bots.

All surfaces eventually share canonical identity, missions, permissions, policies, Cosmos, agents, tools, models, devices, artifacts, receipts, evidence, events, context, and user preferences.

HEY is provider-independent and device-independent.

Prefer, when suitable:
deterministic code/rules/cache/algorithms -> tiny classifiers/micro-models -> local/small models -> cheap strong cloud models -> specialist models -> frontier models -> multi-agent councils only when measured value justifies them.

HEY must work across web/PWA, Android, iOS/iPadOS within platform limits, Windows, macOS, Linux, tablets/phones/desktops, very weak devices, remote/cloud runtimes, local/self-hosted runtimes, and future device adapters.

Ultra-light device law:
The intelligence does not need to live on the device. The device needs only the smallest trusted local runtime necessary to expose supported capabilities, enforce authority, access permitted resources, execute typed actions, verify postconditions, and communicate securely.

Device classes:
CLASS 0 LEGACY TERMINAL — interaction/gateway only when local OS capabilities are unavailable.
CLASS 1 HEY EDGE — tiny deterministic action runtime, no LLM required.
CLASS 2 HEY EDGE+ — adds lightweight local intent/search/speech/classification where viable.
CLASS 3 FULL LOCAL HEY — can run local reasoning/vision/speech/agents/creation when hardware allows.

Offline is a core requirement. Every capability must truthfully declare its local/cloud/offline behavior and degrade explicitly.

No hidden dark patterns, coercion, fake scarcity, deceptive sponsorship influence, or addiction-maximizing mechanics. Psychology may optimize trust, clarity, motivation, reduced cognitive load, commitment, salience, legitimate social proof, reversible defaults, and attention efficiency.

Minors are supported. Build age-aware boundaries, not surveillance assumptions.

==================================================
BASE CONTRACT COMPATIBILITY
==================================================

Design against the intent of Prompt 01 Global Foundation and Prompt 02 Identity/Accounts/Device Trust:
- typed versioned contracts
- durable mission lifecycle
- canonical events/errors/receipts/evidence
- action-bound authorization
- device identity/trust
- workspace/account separation
- local/cloud classifications
- privacy classifications
- capability maturity
- independent verification

If those package files are absent, mirror only what is essential and flag reconciliation work.

==================================================
DEPENDENCY + INTEGRATION DISCIPLINE
==================================================

For every library/service/runtime:
record purpose, version strategy, license, security considerations, platform support, install command, optional/mandatory status, alternatives considered, and future migration cost.

INTEGRATION_MANIFEST.md must state:
- what this package owns and deliberately does NOT own
- contracts consumed/exported
- APIs/events emitted/consumed
- storage/schema requirements
- environment variables/secrets as names only
- dependencies/install steps
- web/backend/native/Edge wiring
- likely conflicts/duplicates Claude must inspect
- migration order/data migration/rollback
- post-integration tests
- capability maturity/evidence requirements
- unknowns requiring the real HEY repository

==================================================
RESEARCH STANDARD
==================================================

Where current research access exists, use current primary/authoritative sources first: official specifications, standards bodies, platform documentation, original technical papers, official provider/runtime docs, and maintained project documentation.

Compare alternatives on correctness, interoperability, security, privacy, platform reach, weak-device cost, latency, memory, battery, licensing, maintainability, vendor lock-in, ecosystem maturity, observability, testability, and migration risk. Record major accepted/rejected decisions.

==================================================
FINAL SELF-ATTACK
==================================================

Before completion, run a hostile self-review designed to prove your package is partial, insecure, duplicated, misleading, too heavyweight, provider-locked, platform-faked, difficult to integrate, or impossible to recover.

At minimum ask:
- Can a model/tool/retrieved document escalate authority?
- Can another user/workspace/device receive data or capability accidentally?
- Can retries duplicate side effects?
- Can cancellation still allow later side effects?
- Can “success” occur without verified postconditions?
- Can stale evidence remain valid?
- What happens offline, on weak hardware, under rate limits, after auth expiry, during provider outage, on corrupted state, and during partial success?
- Does this package duplicate a global HEY concern?
- Are mocks/test adapters clearly impossible to confuse with production?
- Are all install/migration/wiring steps written down?
- Is anything labelled complete that cannot actually be proven without the real HEY repository?

Fix every reproducible defect. Mark remaining codebase-dependent claims UNVERIFIED.


==================================================
MANDATORY CAPABILITIES / ARCHITECTURE
==================================================

Build, specify, test, and document at least all of the following. This is a floor, not a ceiling. Add any missing capability, state, edge case, contract, verifier, recovery path, performance mechanism, security boundary, migration concern, or test required to make this subsystem genuinely production-grade.

- Semantic accessibility contracts for web/native/artifacts/widgets/overlays.
- Keyboard-only operation and robust focus management.
- Screen-reader labels/live regions/status for streaming AI, missions, approvals and errors.
- Reduced motion, high contrast, zoom/reflow, large targets, motor accessibility and alternate input.
- Cognitive accessibility and progressive disclosure.
- Captions/transcripts/non-audio alternatives.
- No color-only meaning.
- RTL-first architecture for Arabic/Kurdish and mixed bidi content.
- I18n strings/plurals/dates/numbers/currency/time zones/calendars where needed.
- Unicode-safe identity/search/file/artifact handling.
- Cross-language Cosmos/search/entity resolution.
- Localization workflow with context, review, versioning and completeness.
- Cultural localization/formality without stereotyping.
- Voice locale/accent/pronunciation integration.
- Automated audits plus manual real-user testing requirement.
- Artifact-generation accessibility metadata.
- Weak-device accessibility performance.
- Platform assistive-tech matrix.

==================================================
DATA, CONTRACTS, EVENTS, STATE & API REQUIREMENTS
==================================================

For this subsystem:
- define stable typed public interfaces and versioned schemas
- define lifecycle/state machines wherever state exists
- define IDs, timestamps, ownership, workspace/account scope, provenance, privacy classification, locality, version, status, and evidence links where applicable
- define commands/queries/events separately where that improves safety
- define idempotency semantics for every retryable write or side effect
- define optimistic/concurrent update behavior and conflict policy
- define retention/deletion/export/migration behavior for persisted data
- define compatibility/version negotiation where multiple devices/services/clients may be on different versions
- define errors using the canonical HEY error/recovery model rather than ad-hoc strings
- define observability hooks and audit events without leaking secrets/private content
- define integration boundaries with Identity, Trust Kernel, Mission Runtime, Brain, Cosmos, Situation, Tool/Action Fabric, Device Mesh, Edge, Artifacts, Billing, Privacy, Security, Evaluation, and Release systems wherever applicable
- never make a model response itself authoritative state

IMPLEMENTATION STANDARD
==================================================

Do not only write Markdown.

Create working libraries/modules/reference services/schemas/validators/state machines/adapters/test harnesses where this package can be implemented independently.

You are the principal production engineer for HEY responsible for: Domain Expert Packs, High-Stakes Specialization & Knowledge Certification.

Create the production-grade integration-ready package:

`HEY-NEXT/45-domain-expert-packs/`

PACKAGE OWNERSHIP
Own the framework for deeply specialized HEY expert packs combining models, retrieval, deterministic tools, rules, citations, uncertainty and professional escalation rather than merely changing a prompt.

DEPENDENCY INTENT
This package conceptually depends on: Brain, Search/Research, Model/Agent, Trust, Privacy and global contracts.
Because every Codex task is isolated and other package outputs may not be physically available, do not invent competing global systems. Use minimal clearly-labelled temporary mirrors only when compilation/testing requires them.


==================================================
ABSOLUTE FINAL PRODUCT CONTRACT — NON-NEGOTIABLE
==================================================

This is FINAL-PRODUCT engineering, not ideation, an MVP, a prototype, a demo, a mockup, a proof of concept, or a partial feature pass.

Forbidden:
- MVP shortcuts or knowingly incomplete production paths
- placeholders, fake-success states, dead buttons, disconnected screens, mock-backed “working” behavior, TODO-driven completion claims, or silent deferral of hard requirements
- frontend-only, backend-only, schema-only, or test-only completion claims
- a new duplicate global architecture when a canonical HEY contract already exists
- assuming code exists means behavior is integrated, verified, secure, recoverable, observable, accessible, performant, or production-ready
- replacing a stronger future-existing HEY implementation merely because this package differs
- inventing details about the unavailable real HEY repository
- claiming platform capabilities the platform does not expose
- claiming successful side effects without independent postcondition verification

For every applicable capability, the completion pipeline is:
discovery -> current research -> explicit requirements -> architecture -> implementation -> contracts -> data/state -> permissions/authentication/authorization boundaries -> privacy/security -> integration seams -> failure handling -> retry/timeout/cancellation -> recovery/rollback/compensation -> offline/degraded behavior -> weak-device behavior -> performance/cost controls -> observability/auditability -> accessibility/localization readiness -> unit tests -> integration tests -> adversarial/failure tests -> realistic end-to-end tests -> independent verification -> evidence.

If you discover a fixable defect inside this package, FIX IT. Discovery creates work; it is not a reason to stop.

Use the maturity ladder:
MISSING -> DESIGNED -> IMPLEMENTING -> FUNCTIONAL -> INTEGRATED -> VERIFIED -> PRODUCTION_READY.

PRODUCTION_READY requires current, reproducible evidence. Evidence becomes stale when affected implementation, dependencies, policy, environment, tests, schemas, contracts, or providers change.

Never use “confirmed: true”, “approved: true”, UI state, model output, retrieved content, or client-supplied claims as sufficient authority for consequential actions.

Every consequential action must be attributable to the human/service actor, the executing component/device/tool, the exact authority used, the exact target/parameters, the result, verification evidence, cost where relevant, and rollback/compensation status where applicable.

==================================================
SOURCE / INTEGRATION AUTHORITY
==================================================

The newest real HEY codebase is currently unavailable.

Therefore:
1. Build a production-grade, interface-stable, integration-ready HEY-NEXT package.
2. Do not invent the current repository structure, existing tables, current routes, current providers, or current implementations.
3. Clearly separate VERIFIED package behavior from UNVERIFIED future-integration assumptions.
4. If you need a shared contract from another HEY-NEXT package that is not physically present, create only a minimal TEMPORARY CONTRACT MIRROR and label it exactly:
   TEMPORARY CONTRACT MIRROR — MUST BE RECONCILED WITH CANONICAL HEY CONTRACT DURING INTEGRATION.
5. Do not create a competing identity, permission, event, mission, Cosmos, provider, device, artifact, or evidence system simply because the canonical package is unavailable.
6. Every external dependency, service, environment variable, database requirement, native entitlement, build requirement, model/runtime requirement, and installation step must be recorded for Claude Code in DEPENDENCIES.md and INTEGRATION_MANIFEST.md.
7. Future Claude Code integration must inspect the real HEY implementation first, preserve unique stronger behavior, migrate/consolidate safely, wire all layers, run regression/adversarial tests, and retire obsolete duplicates only after evidence.
8. Never destructively assume that HEY-NEXT automatically supersedes existing production code.

==================================================
GLOBAL HEY LAWS
==================================================

HEY is one intelligence, not a visible pile of disconnected bots.

All surfaces eventually share canonical identity, missions, permissions, policies, Cosmos, agents, tools, models, devices, artifacts, receipts, evidence, events, context, and user preferences.

HEY is provider-independent and device-independent.

Prefer, when suitable:
deterministic code/rules/cache/algorithms -> tiny classifiers/micro-models -> local/small models -> cheap strong cloud models -> specialist models -> frontier models -> multi-agent councils only when measured value justifies them.

HEY must work across web/PWA, Android, iOS/iPadOS within platform limits, Windows, macOS, Linux, tablets/phones/desktops, very weak devices, remote/cloud runtimes, local/self-hosted runtimes, and future device adapters.

Ultra-light device law:
The intelligence does not need to live on the device. The device needs only the smallest trusted local runtime necessary to expose supported capabilities, enforce authority, access permitted resources, execute typed actions, verify postconditions, and communicate securely.

Device classes:
CLASS 0 LEGACY TERMINAL — interaction/gateway only when local OS capabilities are unavailable.
CLASS 1 HEY EDGE — tiny deterministic action runtime, no LLM required.
CLASS 2 HEY EDGE+ — adds lightweight local intent/search/speech/classification where viable.
CLASS 3 FULL LOCAL HEY — can run local reasoning/vision/speech/agents/creation when hardware allows.

Offline is a core requirement. Every capability must truthfully declare its local/cloud/offline behavior and degrade explicitly.

No hidden dark patterns, coercion, fake scarcity, deceptive sponsorship influence, or addiction-maximizing mechanics. Psychology may optimize trust, clarity, motivation, reduced cognitive load, commitment, salience, legitimate social proof, reversible defaults, and attention efficiency.

Minors are supported. Build age-aware boundaries, not surveillance assumptions.

==================================================
BASE CONTRACT COMPATIBILITY
==================================================

Design against the intent of Prompt 01 Global Foundation and Prompt 02 Identity/Accounts/Device Trust:
- typed versioned contracts
- durable mission lifecycle
- canonical events/errors/receipts/evidence
- action-bound authorization
- device identity/trust
- workspace/account separation
- local/cloud classifications
- privacy classifications
- capability maturity
- independent verification

If those package files are absent, mirror only what is essential and flag reconciliation work.

==================================================
DEPENDENCY + INTEGRATION DISCIPLINE
==================================================

For every library/service/runtime:
record purpose, version strategy, license, security considerations, platform support, install command, optional/mandatory status, alternatives considered, and future migration cost.

INTEGRATION_MANIFEST.md must state:
- what this package owns and deliberately does NOT own
- contracts consumed/exported
- APIs/events emitted/consumed
- storage/schema requirements
- environment variables/secrets as names only
- dependencies/install steps
- web/backend/native/Edge wiring
- likely conflicts/duplicates Claude must inspect
- migration order/data migration/rollback
- post-integration tests
- capability maturity/evidence requirements
- unknowns requiring the real HEY repository

==================================================
RESEARCH STANDARD
==================================================

Where current research access exists, use current primary/authoritative sources first: official specifications, standards bodies, platform documentation, original technical papers, official provider/runtime docs, and maintained project documentation.

Compare alternatives on correctness, interoperability, security, privacy, platform reach, weak-device cost, latency, memory, battery, licensing, maintainability, vendor lock-in, ecosystem maturity, observability, testability, and migration risk. Record major accepted/rejected decisions.

==================================================
FINAL SELF-ATTACK
==================================================

Before completion, run a hostile self-review designed to prove your package is partial, insecure, duplicated, misleading, too heavyweight, provider-locked, platform-faked, difficult to integrate, or impossible to recover.

At minimum ask:
- Can a model/tool/retrieved document escalate authority?
- Can another user/workspace/device receive data or capability accidentally?
- Can retries duplicate side effects?
- Can cancellation still allow later side effects?
- Can “success” occur without verified postconditions?
- Can stale evidence remain valid?
- What happens offline, on weak hardware, under rate limits, after auth expiry, during provider outage, on corrupted state, and during partial success?
- Does this package duplicate a global HEY concern?
- Are mocks/test adapters clearly impossible to confuse with production?
- Are all install/migration/wiring steps written down?
- Is anything labelled complete that cannot actually be proven without the real HEY repository?

Fix every reproducible defect. Mark remaining codebase-dependent claims UNVERIFIED.


==================================================
MANDATORY CAPABILITIES / ARCHITECTURE
==================================================

Build, specify, test, and document at least all of the following. This is a floor, not a ceiling. Add any missing capability, state, edge case, contract, verifier, recovery path, performance mechanism, security boundary, migration concern, or test required to make this subsystem genuinely production-grade.

- Expert Pack manifest: domain/scope/jurisdictions/standards/models/sources/tools/rules/safety/evidence/update cadence/maintainers/benchmarks/limits.
- Certified source hierarchy per domain.

- Education packs curriculum/integrity.
- Religious packs source hierarchy/authenticity/disagreement/madhhab/no fabricated rulings.
- Business packs tied to real metrics.
- Language packs for translation/linguistics/pronunciation/register.

- Organization/private packs.
- Marketplace/certification hooks.
- Clear boundary between assistance and licensed human responsibility.

==================================================
DATA, CONTRACTS, EVENTS, STATE & API REQUIREMENTS
==================================================

For this subsystem:
- define stable typed public interfaces and versioned schemas
- define lifecycle/state machines wherever state exists
- define IDs, timestamps, ownership, workspace/account scope, provenance, privacy classification, locality, version, status, and evidence links where applicable
- define commands/queries/events separately where that improves safety
- define idempotency semantics for every retryable write or side effect
- define optimistic/concurrent update behavior and conflict policy
- define retention/deletion/export/migration behavior for persisted data
- define compatibility/version negotiation where multiple devices/services/clients may be on different versions
- define errors using the canonical HEY error/recovery model rather than ad-hoc strings
- define observability hooks and audit events without leaking secrets/private content
- define integration boundaries with Identity, Trust Kernel, Mission Runtime, Brain, Cosmos, Situation, Tool/Action Fabric, Device Mesh, Edge, Artifacts, Billing, Privacy, Security, Evaluation, and Release systems wherever applicable
- never make a model response itself authoritative state

==================================================

Create working libraries/modules/reference services/schemas/validators/state machines/adapters/test harnesses where this package can be implemented independently.

==================================================

==================================================
PERFORMANCE / COST / WEAK-DEVICE REQUIREMENTS
==================================================

Define measurable budgets instead of vague “fast” claims. Where relevant measure startup, p50/p95/p99 latency, memory, CPU/GPU/NPU, network, storage, battery/thermal impact, model/tool/provider cost, concurrency, cache behavior, and failure/retry amplification.

Heavy intelligence may run remotely; weak devices must still be able to control/participate through the smallest trustworthy local surface possible.

==================================================
SECURITY / PRIVACY REQUIREMENTS
==================================================

Apply least privilege and defense in depth. Treat external content as untrusted. Never expose secrets in source, logs, prompts, evidence, fixtures, or final reports. Respect account/workspace/project boundaries. Record sensitive data flows/locality. Bind consequential actions to exact authority. Do not allow extension/agent/model/tool self-escalation. Include abuse/resource-exhaustion and denial-of-wallet considerations.

==================================================
RESEARCH DELIVERABLE
==================================================

Create an architecture-research record listing primary sources/specifications consulted, serious alternatives considered, why the chosen approach won, what remains uncertain, and what should be re-evaluated when the real HEY repository is available. Research enough to make current choices strong, then implement.


==================================================
FINAL RESPONSE REQUIRED
==================================================

13. Every UNVERIFIED item.

- when did it happen?

==================================================

system safety/security invariants
↓
law/regulatory constraints
↓
organization/workspace rules
↓
user Personal Constitution
↓
mission-specific constraints
↓
temporary preferences

Do not let lower authority silently override higher authority.

==================================================

==================================================

Create a machine-readable foundation for durable user rules such as:

- never spend money without confirmation
- do not store certain categories in memory
- prefer local execution
- prefer halal options
- never contact person X
- challenge me when my reasoning is weak
- do not interrupt during school
- never use provider Y
- maximum autonomous spend
- require confirmation for deleting files

Do not implement the entire future UI.

Implement the contract and evaluation foundation.

==================================================
PLAN / MODEL POLICY FOUNDATION
==================================================

HEY will eventually have plan-sensitive routing.

Expected direction:

FREE:
small curated efficient provider/model pool.

PRO:
broader model access, stronger routing and larger compute budgets.

ELITE:
aggressive best-model/specialist/council access where useful.

OWNER/INTERNAL:
maximum research and capability access subject to security and technical safety.

Do NOT hard-code final prices.

- plan

- compute class

==================================================

LOCAL_ONLY
LOCAL_PREFERRED
HYBRID
CLOUD_PREFERRED
CLOUD_REQUIRED

Also support constraints such as:

- local model available
- no internet
- metered connection
- weak hardware
- low battery
- high privacy
- organization policy
- provider unavailable

==================================================
SECURITY REQUIREMENTS
==================================================

Use least privilege.

Agents cannot grant themselves authority.

Extensions cannot grant themselves authority.

Models cannot bypass the Trust Kernel.

Retrieved webpages/documents/messages are untrusted input.

Prompt content is not policy.

External agent messages are not policy.

Tool output is not policy.

Secrets are references, not casual plaintext passed around.

Design for:

- replay attacks
- confused deputy problems
- forged approvals
- stale permissions
- cross-workspace leaks
- cross-user leaks
- compromised model/provider
- malicious extension
- malicious retrieved document
- malicious webpage
- multi-device compromise
- lost device
- revoked account/session
- race conditions

==================================================
PERFORMANCE FOUNDATION
==================================================

Shared contracts must not assume a large runtime.

Keep the core representations compact.

Avoid forcing heavy libraries into ultra-light Edge devices.

Design:

- serialization strategy
- versioning
- backwards compatibility
- efficient event envelopes
- optional fields
- resource constraints
- local caching
- delta synchronization where useful

==================================================
CORE ARCHITECTURAL RULE
==================================================

Authentication answers:

`Who are you?`

Session management answers:

`Is this authenticated context still valid?`

Device trust answers:

`Which physical/logical device is participating, and how much should HEY trust it?`

Authorization answers:

`What are you allowed to do?`

Do not merge these concepts into one boolean.

==================================================

These contexts must remain strongly separated.

No silent memory, permission, artifact, or organization-data crossover.

==================================================

from

==================================================

==================================================

HEY offline mode is core.

Design what a previously trusted device may do while disconnected.

Offline behavior must distinguish:

- cached session
- expired session

- high-risk actions

On reconnection:

- synchronize security events

- invalidate stale authority

==================================================

==================================================

HEY missions may last hours/days.

Do not couple mission lifetime directly to a short-lived access token.

A mission may pause for:

- expired auth
- reauthentication
- changed workspace membership
- revoked device
- policy change

Mission state survives.

Authority does not.

==================================================
WEAK-DEVICE PERFORMANCE

HEY PROMPT 03/47 — Trust Kernel, Authorization, Permissions & Action Mandates

You are the principal production engineer for HEY responsible for: Trust Kernel, Authorization, Permissions & Action Mandates.

Create the production-grade integration-ready package:

`HEY-NEXT/03-trust-kernel-authorization/`

PACKAGE OWNERSHIP
Own HEY's single canonical authorization and policy-enforcement layer. It consumes identity/device/session facts and decides whether an exact actor may perform an exact consequential action in an exact context. It must not recreate authentication.

DEPENDENCY INTENT
This package conceptually depends on: Prompt 01 Global Foundation + Prompt 02 Identity/Accounts/Device Trust.
Because every Codex task is isolated and other package outputs may not be physically available, do not invent competing global systems. Use minimal clearly-labelled temporary mirrors only when compilation/testing requires them.


==================================================
ABSOLUTE FINAL PRODUCT CONTRACT — NON-NEGOTIABLE
==================================================

This is FINAL-PRODUCT engineering, not ideation, an MVP, a prototype, a demo, a mockup, a proof of concept, or a partial feature pass.

Forbidden:
- MVP shortcuts or knowingly incomplete production paths

PRODUCTION_READY requires current, reproducible evidence. Evidence becomes stale when affected implementation, dependencies, policy, environment, tests, schemas, contracts, or providers change.

Never use “confirmed: true”, “approved: true”, UI state, model output, retrieved content, or client-supplied claims as sufficient authority for consequential actions.

==================================================
GLOBAL HEY LAWS
==================================================

HEY is one intelligence, not a visible pile of disconnected bots.

All surfaces eventually share canonical identity, missions, permissions, policies, Cosmos, agents, tools, models, devices, artifacts, receipts, evidence, events, context, and user preferences.

HEY is provider-independent and device-independent.

Prefer, when suitable:
deterministic code/rules/cache/algorithms -> tiny classifiers/micro-models -> local/small models -> cheap strong cloud models -> specialist models -> frontier models -> multi-agent councils only when measured value justifies them.

HEY must work across web/PWA, Android, iOS/iPadOS within platform limits, Windows, macOS, Linux, tablets/phones/desktops, very weak devices, remote/cloud runtimes, local/self-hosted runtimes, and future device adapters.

Ultra-light device law:
The intelligence does not need to live on the device. The device needs only the smallest trusted local runtime necessary to expose supported capabilities, enforce authority, access permitted resources, execute typed actions, verify postconditions, and communicate securely.

Device classes:
CLASS 0 LEGACY TERMINAL — interaction/gateway only when local OS capabilities are unavailable.
CLASS 1 HEY EDGE — tiny deterministic action runtime, no LLM required.
CLASS 2 HEY EDGE+ — adds lightweight local intent/search/speech/classification where viable.
CLASS 3 FULL LOCAL HEY — can run local reasoning/vision/speech/agents/creation when hardware allows.

Offline is a core requirement. Every capability must truthfully declare its local/cloud/offline behavior and degrade explicitly.

No hidden dark patterns, coercion, fake scarcity, deceptive sponsorship influence, or addiction-maximizing mechanics. Psychology may optimize trust, clarity, motivation, reduced cognitive load, commitment, salience, legitimate social proof, reversible defaults, and attention efficiency.

Minors are supported. Build age-aware boundaries, not surveillance assumptions.

Offline is a core requirement. Every capability must truthfully declare its local/cloud/offline behavior and degrade explicitly.

Offline is a core requirement. Every capability must truthfully declare its local/cloud/offline behavior and degrade explicitly.

CLASS 2 HEY EDGE+ — adds lightweight local intent/search/speech/classification where viable.
CLASS 3 FULL LOCAL HEY — can run local reasoning/vision/speech/agents/creation when hardware allows.

Offline is a core requirement. Every capability must truthfully declare its local/cloud/offline behavior and degrade explicitly.

No hidden dark patterns, coercion, fake scarcity, deceptive sponsorship influence, or addiction-maximizing mechanics. Psychology may optimize trust, clarity, motivation, reduced cognitive load, commitment, salience, legitimate social proof, reversible defaults, and attention efficiency.

CLASS 3 FULL LOCAL HEY — can run local reasoning/vision/speech/agents/creation when hardware allows.

Offline is a core requirement. Every capability must truthfully declare its local/cloud/offline behavior and degrade explicitly.

CLASS 3 FULL LOCAL HEY — can run local reasoning/vision/speech/agents/creation when hardware allows.

Offline is a core requirement. Every capability must truthfully declare its local/cloud/offline behavior and degrade explicitly.

==================================================

HEY is one intelligence, not a visible pile of disconnected bots.

Ultra-light device law:
The intelligence does not need to live on the device. The device needs only the smallest trusted local runtime necessary to expose supported capabilities, enforce authority, access permitted resources, execute typed actions, verify postconditions, and communicate securely.

Device classes:
CLASS 0 LEGACY TERMINAL — interaction/gateway only when local OS capabilities are unavailable.
CLASS 1 HEY EDGE — tiny deterministic action runtime, no LLM required.
CLASS 2 HEY EDGE+ — adds lightweight local intent/search/speech/classification where viable.
CLASS 3 FULL LOCAL HEY — can run local reasoning/vision/speech/agents/creation when hardware allows.

Offline is a core requirement. Every capability must truthfully declare its local/cloud/offline behavior and degrade explicitly.

No hidden dark patterns, coercion, fake scarcity, deceptive sponsorship influence, or addiction-maximizing mechanics. Psychology may optimize trust, clarity, motivation, reduced cognitive load, commitment, salience, legitimate social proof, reversible defaults, and attention efficiency.

Minors are supported. Build age-aware boundaries, not surveillance assumptions.

==================================================

Before completion, run a hostile self-review designed to prove your package is partial, insecure, duplicated, misleading, too heavyweight, provider-locked, platform-faked, difficult to integrate, or impossible to recover.

At minimum ask:
- Can a model/tool/retrieved document escalate authority?
- Can another user/workspace/device receive data or capability accidentally?
- Can retries duplicate side effects?
- Can cancellation still allow later side effects?
- Can “success” occur without verified postconditions?
- Can stale evidence remain valid?

- Does this package duplicate a global HEY concern?
- Are mocks/test adapters clearly impossible to confuse with production?
- Are all install/migration/wiring steps written down?
- Is anything labelled complete that cannot actually be proven without the real HEY repository?

Fix every reproducible defect. Mark remaining codebase-dependent claims UNVERIFIED.

Review dates: 2026-10-02–03. Phase: review and implementation planning only. No application implementation, deployment, migrations, or source edits performed.

## A. Workstream summary

**The current coordination records cannot establish whole-product readiness.** The inspected implementation has useful registries, execution guards, transactional upgrade machinery, tests and honest native-release limits. Its reporting layer nevertheless promotes names, catalog entries, source presence and test-file references into verification claims. It does not provide the required traceability from all approved source requirements to one owner, repository binding, acceptance conditions, candidate-specific evidence and production disposition.

Director outcome: establish one authoritative requirement/ownership/dependency/evidence coordination record and derive product status from it. Do not implement every product domain in this workstream. Other workstreams own functionality; Director owns source resolution, assignment, priorities, dependencies, conflicts and truthful product state.

### Authority applied

1. Current user instructions authorize this review and final tailored prompt, superseding initialization-only waiting and the refined document's earlier instruction to defer a prompt until the user says done.
2. `HEY_REFINED_ENGINEERING_DOCUMENT.md`, embedded `00_START_HERE.md`, explicitly elevates canonical resolution files, domain contracts and new amendments above original decisions for covered conflicts. Its `01_GOVERNANCE/01_AUTHORITY_AND_COMPLETION.md` and `02_REFINEMENT_APPLICATION.md` retain all non-conflicting original requirements. The 215 cards are additions/refinements, **not the total product scope**.
3. Original `HEY_FINAL_ABSOLUTE_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH_COMBINED.md`: embedded foundation, intelligence, interaction, governance and execution files govern over conflicting old detailed/reference material. Preserve the specific newest product-flow amendment where refined authority says it controls navigation/composition.
4. Repository `AGENTS.md` describes the prior September 30 authority and `E:\hey`; do not treat an uploaded snapshot as proof of the Windows working tree or remote HEAD. Its old 229-agent baseline is a seed requirement, not a limit on the Unlimited Agent Foundry. Older V1/V2 and free-only/free-first launch assumptions cannot narrow newer approved scope.
5. Maturity: `MISSING → DESIGNED → IMPLEMENTING → FUNCTIONAL → INTEGRATED → VERIFIED → PRODUCTION_READY`. Record blockers and evidence categories separately. UNKNOWN, MOCK_ONLY, IMPLEMENTED_UNVERIFIED, BLOCKED_EXTERNAL and WAIVED are not PASS. A waiver never fulfills a requirement.

### Review boundary and evidence

The cleaned archive was extracted for read-only review, without displaying `.env` values. Sources and coordination files were read directly. Structure was mapped across frontend, core, legacy TS routes, edge functions, SQL, native adapters, service worker, config and tests. Director-owned ledgers/generators/orchestrator/status/release documents were inspected deeply; functional domains were inspected as dependencies, not exhaustively audited.

This is **not** a complete semantic certification of 52,123 specification lines or every product capability. Original source sections and all 215 refined cards are indexed below; cards without domain review remain explicitly UNREVIEWED. The original 8,560 clause candidates and 14,248 occurrence records are described in the refined document, but their referenced JSON ledgers are not supplied as separate files here. Do not pretend to have read them. Combined documents are sufficient to start traceability; full occurrence disposition remains open.

## D. Strengths to preserve

- Existing runtime capability registry starts unavailable and separates platform support/permission/restriction. This is a useful fail-closed boundary, not a completion ledger.
- `tests/release-surfaces.test.js` explicitly tests missing provider, unverified result, and absent Forge/automation runner failures. Keep these negative cases; mocked provider success is only contract-test evidence.
- PowerShell upgrade code refuses baseline conflicts even with Force, backs up files, captures exit status and supports rollback. Strengthen it rather than creating another upgrade runner.
- `src/core/platformMatrix.js` explicitly identifies unbuilt desktop/mobile releases. Preserve honest platform limits while correcting the meaning of release verification.
- Existing SQL admission/owner/Forge changes and tests are useful evidence anchors; leave migrations and domain logic to their owners.

## E. Problems found

### D00-01 — Evidence fabrication by heuristics (high; confirmed static)

`scripts/generate-capability-ledger.mjs`: `evidenceForV1Name()` returns VERIFIED WORKING for names containing words such as chat, voice, agent or memory. Agent mapping assigns VERIFIED WORKING unconditionally. Feature status `implemented` becomes AUTOMATED TESTED. `testsReferencing()` uses substring matches and never executes or reads a run result. The engine stub heuristic only checks short files and narrow text patterns; absent matches do not establish correctness. Impact: generated claims can certify unimplemented/unexecuted behavior. Remove these promotion rules, retaining heuristic inventory only as non-evidence metadata.

### D00-02 — Historical complete-looking rollup contradicts its notes (high; confirmed static)

`docs/upgrade/MASTER-STATUS.json` summary says total=34, verified=34, pending=0, failed=0. Module notes disclose no dedicated mode-transition test, no performance-budget test and native scaffolds/external setup. `HEY-CAPABILITY-LEDGER.json` records 2,040 entries, 238 verified-working, zero partial and zero blocked. These are stale inventory/status claims, not full production coverage; duplicates and catalog entries inflate the denominator. Preserve history with its original scope; never convert it to current pass evidence.

### D00-03 — Stale evidence can suppress work (high; confirmed static)

`Invoke-HeyAllUpgrade` skips `verified-local`, `verified-backend`, `verified-native` in Apply/Resume without checking candidate/source/plan/environment fingerprint. `VerifyOnly` writes verified-local when probes complete. `verify-module.mjs` can succeed on existence/import checks and can succeed with zero requested probes; it is not a full product validator. Impact: changed code or requirements can retain old completion status. Add applicability and freshness validation; probe success is one evidence kind, not maturity promotion.

### D00-04 — Declared dependencies are not a validated scheduling DAG (high; confirmed inspected traversal)

`Get-HeyModulePlans` sorts filenames; `Invoke-HeyAllUpgrade` iterates that order. Example: `02-UI-DESIGN-SYSTEM` precedes `20-AUTH-SECURITY`, while newest product order puts shared authorization/contracts first. Android/iOS plans depend on Windows rather than expressing shared adapter/platform prerequisites. Do not mechanically replace these with the 19 workstream IDs: upgrade modules and ownership are separate dimensions. Derive scheduling from explicit task dependencies, detect cycles and missing prerequisites, and let independent work proceed around blockers.

### D00-05 — Release verdicts exceed their evidence (high; confirmed static)

`docs/release/RELEASE_GATE.md` is dated September 20 and says CONDITIONAL GO, includes catalog presence as QA-agent evidence, reports secret-scan/build/test results without a current candidate, and defers duplicate-registry disposition post-launch. Newer authority requires candidate-specific integration, independent/device and release evidence. `src/core/platformMatrix.js:isReleaseVerified()` returns true for the web's `verifiedSource`; source verification is not production release verification. Workstream 10 owns release behavior; Director requests contract correction and prevents stale public readiness claims.

### D00-06 — No demonstrated comprehensive requirement ownership/wiring (high; bounded search finding)

Searches in `scripts`, `docs/upgrade` and `tests` for refined HEY-CAP IDs, requirement/source/primary-owner fields did not establish the required ledger. Generator imports old V1, Infinity, feature, agent and mode catalogs, not the authoritative refined occurrence/cards. Mapping source meaning is a semantic task; name matching is insufficient. No numeric catalog count is a substitute for complete source disposition.

### D00-07 — Broader architecture overlaps need explicit handoffs (medium; review candidates)

Active Vite SPA coexists with `src/app` TS/Next routes and Prisma. Provider routers exist at `src/core/providerRouter.js` and `src/core/infinity/providerRouter.js`; computer/workspace/memory layers also overlap in names. These are candidates for caller-level reconciliation by 01/13, not proven interchangeable implementations. Keep unique behavior until replacement wiring and tests demonstrate safe retirement.

### D00-08 — Reproduction and archive hygiene gaps (medium; confirmed inventory)

The archive contains `.env` and `.env.local` plus stored reports/logs and backups. Values were not read or copied into this report; no assertion that they contain live credentials. 09 should assess and rotate only if actual exposure warrants it, and 10 should define a redacted source bundle. Archived reports lack demonstrated relevance to the current candidate. `E:\hey` current dirty/unpushed state remains unknown.

### Fresh test evidence and limitations

Executed in extracted snapshot: `node --test tests/*.test.js`, Node v24.19.0. Exit 1; runner reported 117 tests, 107 pass, 10 fail, 0 skipped/cancelled/todo; 1,767.235309 ms reported test duration. Nine test files fail loading missing packages (`react`, `@tauri-apps/api`, or `@supabase/supabase-js`), and upgrade-orchestrator fails because PowerShell is absent. These are review-environment blockers; no product logic failure is established by those load failures. No dependencies installed and no source modified to make checks green.

No lint/build, live Supabase/RLS, browser E2E, native build/install, device flows, paid calls, deployment or independent review executed. Missing dependencies also block a meaningful full build/lint baseline. Passing deterministic/contract checks do not verify providers, external side effects, production databases or devices. Stored Playwright results were inventoried, not replayed or adopted as current evidence.

# ORIGINAL SOURCE 8: Pasted text(1).txt

**Preserved original source.** Older progress/audit report, historical only; cannot override newer repo evidence. SHA-256 `d61734c06a72b89678ab5299871767ae648350c672dd71fe091e122f94f2d65a`. **Source is historical where superseded by newer decisions above.**

## Audit result

**None of the 47 steps meets the master program’s completion standard.** The repository has useful features and foundations, but the required step-by-step implementation, integration, hostile testing, evidence, and progress ledger are missing.

I reviewed the master program and the separate detailed prompt archive for Steps 03–47, then checked the current GitHub branch. The checkout matched that branch’s exact tree.

## Important findings

- **No HEY-NEXT packages or master progress ledger are in the HEY repository.** The separate `hey-next-production-program` repository contains only a README. I found no source for Packages 01–04 or later packages in those repositories.
- **The approved 4,210+ capability list is not in the checked repository.** The app’s feature catalog has 100 entries, 21 marked “active” and 79 “expanding.” The master says not to invent the missing capability list, so its exact coverage remains unknown.
- **The code has false-success paths that need fixing.** `diagnosticsEngine.js` marks recovery successful even though its recovery methods are stubs. `developerEngine.js` hard-codes package signature and other validation checks to `true`. The scheduled automation calculation ignores the requested schedule and returns a time one minute later. These affect trust, recovery, scheduling, and package safety.
- **There are overlapping state owners that need a canonical architecture audit:** auth/account and billing, permissions/trust, missions/workflows/automation, memory/Cosmos, provider routing, and offline sync. The code does not yet show that each has one authoritative implementation.
- **The repository is public**, although the release report says it is private. The report also refers to `docs/history/`, which does not exist in the checked tree. Treat those claims as stale and verify whether the public visibility is intentional.
- The working branch is [44 commits ahead of `main`](https://github.com/sakosalm2812-droid/hey/tree/codex/production-readiness-2026-10-13). It is at `3edec21c46b2319ffa00f9504e5b845e300a9b8e`. GitHub reports **no CI checks for that commit**; CI passed on its prior commit, not this exact one.

Local evidence for the checked tree: **54 tests passed**, lint passed, build passed, and `npm audit --audit-level=high` found zero vulnerabilities. The build still warns about mixed static/dynamic imports, and sitemap generation was skipped because `SITE_URL` is unset. These checks do not prove the full 47-step system works end to end.

## Step-by-step gaps

“Partial” means related code exists; it does **not** mean the step is complete or production-ready. “Missing/very partial” means there is no complete integrated subsystem for the step.

| # | Step | Status and remaining work |
|---:|---|---|
| 01 | Global foundation and contracts | **Partial.** Define and test shared contracts; signed action mandates; replay, expiry, usage limits, revocation and delegation; evidence freshness; event idempotency; durable authority storage; secure serialization; offline authority; recovery and benchmarks. |
| 02 | Identity, accounts and device trust | **Partial.** Supabase auth exists. Add the provider-neutral runtime, passkeys/WebAuthn, MFA/TOTP, recovery codes, refresh rotation and reuse detection, device enrollment/credential rotation, service identities, offline grants, and deletion invalidation. |
| 03 | Trust, permissions and action mandates | **Partial.** Permission and Trust Center code exists. Add delegation-chain attenuation, extensible scopes, policy simulation/diff/rollout/rollback, revocation propagation, multi-node storage, offline reconciliation, and replay/concurrency tests. |
| 04 | Durable mission runtime | **Partial.** Mission/workflow code and checkpoints exist. Add durable distributed execution, timers and external waits, compensation, parallel joins, deadlines/budgets, dead letters, cancellation races, stale-worker recovery, migrations, and load tests. |
| 05 | Brain and Intent-to-Reality graph | **Partial.** Brain, router, planner, and mission modules exist. The required single, end-to-end path from intent through authority, action, independent verification, receipt, and reality graph is not established. |
| 06 | Providers and adaptive compute | **Partial.** Provider registries and routing exist. Add measured routing by quality, cost, latency, privacy, and device class; quotas/fallbacks; local-model support; provider conformance and benchmarks. Live providers need credentials. |
| 07 | Agents and experts | **Partial.** Agent code exists and some paths fail closed. Add scoped agent identities and delegation, sandboxing, budgets, reputation/evaluation, and safe multi-agent coordination. |
| 08 | Tools and actions | **Partial.** Tool registry and execution gates exist. Complete the universal tool contract, exact authority/target receipts, idempotent side effects, independent postcondition verification, and recovery/compensation across real tools. |
| 09 | Edge action core | **Partial.** Tauri and capability boundaries exist. Build and test a minimal deterministic edge runtime, offline authority validation, and device-class behavior. |
| 10 | Device mesh | **Partial.** Device fabric code exists. Secure remote pairing, attestation, key rotation, cross-device handoff/scheduling, revocation, and physical-device tests remain. |
| 11 | Computer use and OS control | **Partial.** Some browser/file/terminal commands exist; critical control is blocked. Implement safe adapters, isolation, injection defenses, permission checks, and verified OS/browser behavior. |
| 12 | Cosmos memory | **Partial.** Memory and graph modules exist. Complete provenance/confidence, temporal updates, correction/forgetting/retention/export, private spaces, and account-isolated end-to-end behavior. |
| 13 | Situation engine and context compiler | **Partial.** Context and routing code exist. Build a canonical situation/context compiler with confidence, source, freshness, fusion, privacy limits, and tests for stale/conflicting context. |

| 16 | Voice and live multimodal | **Partial.** Voice/browser-provider code exists. Reliable interruption, confirmations, wake-word controls, visible listening state, offline queueing, and live device/provider testing remain. |

## External blockers versus buildable work

**Genuinely external:** production credentials and deployment, live AI/search/voice providers, payment-provider account and legal setup, domain/CORS configuration, signing identities/app-store approvals, and physical target devices.

**Still buildable without those:** the missing contracts, local/reference runtimes, conformance harnesses, durable scheduling/recovery, safety and permission logic, fake-success fixes, tests, benchmarks, migration tooling, and integration manifests. The external blockers do not explain those gaps.

The first work should be: fix the false-success recovery/package-validation paths, correct automation scheduling, establish the canonical architecture and per-step evidence ledger, and then complete Steps 01–04 before advancing.

HEY

MASTER PRODUCT BIBLE

The complete vision, capability map, experience model, system architecture, user possibilities, platform boundaries, and vNext expansion plan

S&A • HEY AI Life Operating System

Canonical feature inventory: 1–1460 • Built-in agents: exactly 229 (843–1071)

## How to read this document

HEY is intentionally broader than a normal application. To avoid confusing vision with implementation evidence, use these meanings:

## Product definition

HEY is conceived as an AI Life Operating System rather than a single chatbot. Its job is to unify conversation, memory, creation, research, automation, device control, projects, files and proactive assistance under one trusted identity and one consistent interface.

The design goal is not “an app with many buttons.” The goal is a coherent intelligence layer that can understand context, remember only what it is allowed to remember, act across supported systems, prove what it changed, and move between devices without forcing the user to rebuild context.

## The promise

HEY should reduce the distance between intent and outcome. A user should be able to say what they want, show what they mean, select the object or screen region involved, and let HEY assemble the right agents, providers, tools and devices while preserving permissions and verification.

Where an operating system or external service prevents a behavior, HEY should expose the limitation and use the strongest legitimate fallback rather than simulate success.

## Core product principles

Conversation-first: after sign-in, the default destination is the Chat/Voice Conversation Surface, not a dashboard.

One context, many surfaces: Chat, Voice, Live, Dynamic Island, widgets, notifications and device handoff should share the same conversation/task identity where appropriate.

Private by default: minimum context, explicit permissions, local-first routing for sensitive work, user-controlled memory and visible sensing state.

Act with proof: actions, automations and missions should distinguish requested, running, verified, partial, failed and cancelled states; a UI animation is never proof of execution.

Project consistency: Project DNA, locks and provenance protect brand, terminology, structure and identity across long-running work.

Platform honesty: web/PWA, Windows, Android and iOS share outcome goals but use different legitimate mechanisms where OS constraints require it.

Free-first launch: launch paths should prefer free, local or free-tier providers; paid adapters can exist but cannot silently become mandatory.

No clutter tax: HEY may contain enormous capability depth without exposing every capability as a permanent navigation item.

## What HEY should feel like

HEY should feel closer to a trusted operating layer than a collection of AI features. The user should not need to decide which model, agent, tool, screen or device to use for ordinary work; HEY should route intelligently while keeping the route inspectable.

The visual direction is premium, calm and minimal: near-black graphite surfaces, refined glass, realistic depth, restrained adaptive accents, strong typography, subtle motion and consistent rounded geometry. The UI should avoid flashy “AI hologram” clichés. Information density can increase in professional/developer contexts, but the base experience stays quiet and deliberate.

The primary relationship is conversational. Sidebars and secondary navigation collapse away when not needed. Mobile uses overlay drawers rather than permanent space-taking panels. Desktop supports compact/collapsible/resizable navigation. The dashboard is secondary; sign-in should land on Chat/Voice.

Voice should feel like a call with the same HEY—not a separate assistant. Spoken user turns and HEY responses belong to the same persisted conversation. Replies default to concise natural speech; interruption should stop speech quickly. The preferred identity is a deep British male voice, with configurable voice and wake phrase.
